passages.textEn: In the twenty-sixth year Jian, King of Qi, and his chancellor Hou Sheng sent troops to guard their western border and cut off contact with Qin. Qin sent the general Wang Ben south from Yan to attack Qi, and captured Jian, King of Qi.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 分天下以為三十六郡，郡置守、尉、監。更名民曰「黔首」。大酺。收天下兵，聚之咸陽，銷以為鐘鐻，金人十二，重各千石，置廷宮中。一法度衡石丈尺。車同軌。書同文字。地東至海暨朝鮮，西至臨洮、羌中，南至北向戶，北據河為塞，并陰山至遼東。
passages.textEn: He divided the realm into thirty-six commanderies, each with a governor, a commandant and an inspector. The people were renamed "the black-headed". There was a great feast. The weapons of the realm were gathered at Xianyang and melted down into bell stands and twelve bronze men, each weighing a thousand dan, which were set in the palace. Laws, weights and measures were made uniform. Carts had the same axle width. Writing used the same characters. The land reached east to the sea and Chaoxian, west to Lintao and the Qiang country, south to the lands where doors face north, and north to the Yellow River, held as a frontier, along the Yin Mountains to Liaodong.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 臣請史官非秦記皆燒之。非博士官所職，天下敢有藏詩、書、百家語者，悉詣守、尉雜燒之。有敢偶語詩書者棄市。以古非今者族。吏見知不舉者與同罪。令下三十日不燒，黥為城旦。所不去者，醫藥卜筮種樹之書。
passages.textEn: "I request that the historians' records other than those of Qin all be burned. Except for what is in the keeping of the court scholars, anyone in the realm who dares to keep the Odes, the Documents or the sayings of the hundred schools must take them to the governor or commandant to be burned. Anyone who dares to discuss the Odes and Documents together shall be executed in the market; anyone who uses the past to criticise the present shall be exterminated with his clan; officials who know of it and do not report it share the crime. Whoever has not burned his books thirty days after the order is issued shall be tattooed and sent to build walls. Books to be spared: medicine, divination and planting."

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 至平原津而病。始皇惡言死，群臣莫敢言死事。上病益甚，乃為璽書賜公子扶蘇曰：「與喪會咸陽而葬。」書已封，在中車府令趙高行符璽事所，未授使者。七月丙寅，始皇崩於沙丘平臺。丞相斯為上崩在外，恐諸公子及天下有變，乃祕之，不發喪。
passages.textEn: At the Pingyuan ford he fell ill. The First Emperor hated talk of death and none of his ministers dared mention it. As he grew worse he wrote a sealed letter to Prince Fusu: "Meet the cortège at Xianyang and bury me." The letter was sealed but left with Zhao Gao, Director of the Palace Carriages, who kept the seals, and was never handed to a messenger. On bingyin of the seventh month the First Emperor died at the Pingtai terrace of Shaqiu. Chancellor Li Si, because the emperor had died away from the capital and he feared the princes and the realm might rise, kept it secret and announced no mourning.

summary.zh: 外戚王莽輔政多年後篡漢，「即真天子位，定有天下之號曰新」，改正朔、易服色。推行王田、私屬、五均六筦、屢改幣制等新政，天下騷動；23年綠林軍攻入長安，王莽被殺。
summary.en: Wang Mang, a consort kinsman who had run the Han government for years, took the throne: "I take the throne as true Son of Heaven and fix the name of the realm as Xin", changing the calendar and the colours of dress. His reforms — royal fields, a ban on selling slaves, state monopolies, repeated changes of the coinage — threw the realm into turmoil; in 23 the Lülin armies broke into Chang'an and Wang Mang was killed.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷九十九上 王莽傳上
passages.textZh: 以戊辰直定，御王冠，即真天子位，定有天下之號曰新。其改正朔，易服色，變犧牲，殊徽幟，異器制。以十二月朔癸酉為建國元年正月之朔，以雞鳴為時。
passages.textEn: "On the day wuchen, under the sign ding, I put on the royal cap and take the throne as true Son of Heaven, and fix the name of the realm as Xin. The calendar is changed, the colours of dress altered, the sacrificial animals changed, the banners made different and the vessels of a new pattern. The first day of the twelfth month, guiyou, shall be the first day of the first month of the first year of Shijianguo, and the day shall begin at cockcrow."

summary.zh: 618年李淵受隋恭帝禪，即皇帝位於太極殿，改元武德。626年玄武門之變後李世民即位（太宗），630年李靖破突厥於陰山。690年武則天改國號為周，705年復唐。755年安祿山以誅楊國忠為名起兵，安史之亂後藩鎮割據。880年黃巢陷長安。907年朱溫篡唐。
summary.en: In 618 Li Yuan took the abdication of the last Sui emperor and the throne in the Taiji Hall, proclaiming the Wude era. After the Xuanwu Gate incident of 626 Li Shimin (Taizong) took the throne, and in 630 Li Jing beat the Turks in the Yin Mountains. Wu Zetian renamed the state Zhou in 690; Tang was restored in 705. In 755 An Lushan rose in the name of punishing Yang Guozhong; after the An–Shi rebellion the military governors ruled their provinces as their own. Huang Chao took Chang'an in 880, and in 907 Zhu Wen usurped the throne.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一 高祖本紀
passages.textZh: 甲子，高祖即皇帝位於太極殿，命刑部尚書蕭造兼太尉，告於南郊，大赦天下，改隋義寧二年為唐武德元年。
passages.textEn: On jiazi Gaozu took the imperial throne in the Taiji Hall, had the Minister of Justice Xiao Zao act as Grand Commandant to report to Heaven at the southern altar, proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the second year of Yining of Sui into the first year of Wude of Tang.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷二 太宗本紀上
passages.textZh: 九年，皇太子建成、齊王元吉謀害太宗。六月四日，太宗率長孫無忌、尉遲敬德、房玄齡、杜如晦、宇文士及、高士廉、侯君集、程知節、秦叔寶、段志玄、屈突通、張士貴等於玄武門誅之。甲子，立為皇太子，庶政皆斷決。
passages.textEn: In the ninth year the Crown Prince Jiancheng and Yuanji, Prince of Qi, plotted against Taizong. On the fourth day of the sixth month Taizong, with Zhangsun Wuji, Yuchi Jingde, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Yuwen Shiji, Gao Shilian, Hou Junji, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, Duan Zhixuan, Qutu Tong, Zhang Shigui and others, killed them at the Xuanwu Gate. On jiazi he was made Crown Prince, and all affairs of government were decided by him.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷三 太宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 甲辰，李靖又破突厥於陰山，頡利可汗輕騎遠遁。
passages.textEn: On jiachen Li Jing beat the Turks again in the Yin Mountains, and Illig Qaghan fled far away with a few light horsemen.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷九 玄宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 丙寅，范陽節度使安祿山率蕃、漢之兵十餘萬，自幽州南向詣闕，以誅楊國忠為名，先殺太原尹楊光翽於博陵郡。
passages.textEn: On bingyin An Lushan, Military Governor of Fanyang, led more than a hundred thousand foreign and Han troops south from Youzhou towards the capital, in the name of punishing Yang Guozhong, first killing Yang Guanghui, Intendant of Taiyuan, at Boling.

confidenceNote.zh: 松贊干布統一諸部的年代約在629年前後，諸說不一。
confidenceNote.en: Songtsen Gampo unified the tribes around 629; dates vary.

summary.zh: 青藏高原上的王朝。贊普弄贊（松贊干布）時強盛；641年唐太宗以文成公主嫁之，弄贊率部兵至柏海，親迎於河源。其後與唐爭奪安西四鎮、河西與隴右，763年一度攻入長安，立廣武王承宏為帝，十五日而退。842年後王室分裂，帝國瓦解。
summary.en: The empire of the Tibetan plateau. It grew strong under the Tsenpo Nongzan (Songtsen Gampo); in 641 Tang Taizong gave him Princess Wencheng, and he led his troops to Lake Bo to meet her at the source of the Yellow River. Tubo later fought Tang for the Four Garrisons, Hexi and Longyou, and in 763 briefly took Chang'an, setting up Chenghong, Prince of Guangwu, as emperor before leaving after fifteen days. After 842 the royal house split and the empire broke up.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十六上 吐蕃傳上
passages.textZh: 貞觀十五年，太宗以文成公主妻之，令禮部尚書、江夏郡王道宗主婚，持節送公主於吐蕃。弄贊率其部兵次柏海，親迎於河源。見道宗，執子婿之禮甚恭。既而嘆大國服飾禮儀之美，俯仰有愧沮之色。
passages.textEn: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan Taizong gave him Princess Wencheng in marriage, and had Daozong, Minister of Rites and Prince of Jiangxia, preside over the wedding and escort the princess to Tubo with the imperial tally. Nongzan [Songtsen Gampo] led his troops to camp at Lake Bo and came himself to meet her at the source of the Yellow River. Meeting Daozong he behaved most respectfully, as a son-in-law should. Then, admiring the beauty of the great country's dress and ceremony, he looked abashed.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十六上 吐蕃傳上
passages.textZh: 吐蕃以吐谷渾、党項羌之眾二十余萬，自龍光度而東。郭子儀退軍，車駕幸陜州，京師失守。降將高暉引吐蕃入上都城，與吐蕃大將馬重英等立故邠王男廣武王承宏為帝，立年號，大赦，署置官員，尋以司封崔瑰等為相。郭子儀退軍南保商州，吐蕃居城十五日退，官軍收上都，以郭子儀為留守。
passages.textEn: Tubo, with more than two hundred thousand Tuyuhun and Tangut troops, crossed east at Longguang. Guo Ziyi fell back, the emperor fled to Shanzhou and the capital was lost. The renegade general Gao Hui led Tubo into the capital, and with the Tubo general Ma Chongying set up Chenghong, Prince of Guangwu, son of the late Prince of Bin, as emperor, with an era name, an amnesty and appointed officials, soon making Cui Gui and others his ministers. Guo Ziyi withdrew south to hold Shangzhou. Tubo stayed in the city fifteen days and left; the government troops retook the capital and Guo Ziyi was made its regent.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十八 西戎傳 龜茲
passages.textZh: 先是，太宗既破龜茲，移置安西都護府於其國城，以郭孝恪為都護，兼統於闐、疏勒、碎葉，謂之「四鎮」。高宗嗣位，不欲廣地勞人，復命有司棄龜茲等四鎮，移安西依舊於西州。其後吐蕃大入，焉耆已西四鎮城堡，並為賊所陷。
passages.textEn: Earlier, when Taizong had beaten Kucha, he moved the Anxi Protectorate to its capital, with Guo Xiaoke as Protector, also in charge of Khotan, Kashgar and Suyab — the "Four Garrisons". When Gaozong succeeded he did not want to stretch the realm and burden the people, and had the Four Garrisons abandoned and Anxi moved back to Xizhou. Later Tubo came in great force, and the forts of the Four Garrisons west of Karashahr all fell to them.

summary.zh: 907年朱溫受唐哀帝禪，「被袞冕，即皇帝位」，國號梁，都汴州（開封府），史稱後梁。與據河東的晉王李克用、李存勖父子連年交戰，923年為後唐所滅。
summary.en: In 907 Zhu Wen took the abdication of the last Tang emperor, "put on the imperial robes and crown and took the throne", naming his state Liang, with its capital at Bianzhou (Kaifeng) — the "Later Liang". It fought year after year with the Princes of Jin, Li Keyong and his son Li Cunxu, who held Hedong, and fell to the Later Tang in 923.

passages.sourceEn: Old History of the Five Dynasties (Xue Juzheng et al., 974)
passages.locator: 卷三 梁書 太祖紀三
passages.textZh: 甲子，張文蔚、楊涉乘輅自上源驛至，從冊寶諸司各備儀衛鹵簿前導，百官從其後，至金祥殿前陳之。王被袞冕，即皇帝位。
passages.textEn: On jiazi Zhang Wenwei and Yang She arrived from the Shangyuan post station in state carriages, the offices carrying the patents and seals leading with their guards and insignia and the officials following, and set them out before the Jinxiang Hall. The prince put on the imperial robes and crown and took the throne.

note.en: the state name changed back and forth between Great Khitan and Great Liao

summary.zh: 契丹迭剌部耶律阿保機於907年燔柴告天、即皇帝位，916年建元神冊。938年後晉以幽、薊等十六州並圖籍獻契丹，遼以皇都為上京臨潢府，升幽州為南京。1004年與宋訂澶淵之盟。1125年天祚帝為金所俘，遼亡；耶律大石西走，建西遼。
summary.en: Yelü Abaoji of the Khitan Yila tribe burned offerings to Heaven and took the imperial throne in 907, and proclaimed the Shence era in 916. In 938 the Later Jin presented sixteen prefectures, including You and Ji, with their maps and registers; Liao made its imperial capital the Upper Capital, Linhuang, and raised Youzhou to the Southern Capital. In 1004 it made the Treaty of Chanyuan with Song. In 1125 Emperor Tianzuo was captured by the Jin and Liao ended; Yelü Dashi went west and founded the Western Liao.

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖本紀上
passages.textZh: 元年春正月庚寅，命有司設壇于如迂王集會堝，燔柴告天，即皇帝位。
passages.textEn: In the first month of the first year, on gengyin, he had an altar built at the Ruyu royal assembly ground, burned offerings to Heaven and took the imperial throne.

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷四 太宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 是月，晉復遣趙瑩奉表來賀，以幽、薊、瀛、莫、涿、檀、順、媯、儒、新、武、雲、應、朔、寰、蔚十六州並圖籍來獻。於是詔以皇都為上京，府曰臨潢。升幽州為南京，南京為東京。
passages.textEn: That month Jin again sent Zhao Ying with a memorial of congratulation, presenting the sixteen prefectures of You, Ji, Ying, Mo, Zhuo, Tan, Shun, Gui, Ru, Xin, Wu, Yun, Ying, Shuo, Huan and Yu, with their maps and registers. An edict then made the imperial capital the Upper Capital, with the prefecture called Linhuang; Youzhou was raised to the Southern Capital, and the old Southern Capital became the Eastern Capital.

question.en: When did Abaoji become emperor?

claim.zh: 《遼史》記907年正月燔柴告天，即皇帝位。
claim.en: The History of Liao has him take the imperial throne in the first month of 907, burning offerings to Heaven.

source.en: History of Liao, Annals of Taizu

accounts.quoteZh: 燔柴告天，即皇帝位。

claim.zh: 同書又記916年群臣上尊號、建元神冊；不少今人認為907年所即的是可汗之位，916年才正式稱帝建元。
claim.en: The same book records that in 916 the ministers gave him an imperial title and the Shence era was proclaimed; many historians think 907 marks his election as qaghan and 916 his imperial title.

source.zh: 《遼史·太祖本紀上》神冊元年條；今人研究
source.en: History of Liao, first year of Shence; modern scholarship

accounts.quoteZh: 上尊號曰大聖大明天皇帝

summary.zh: 960年正月，後周殿前都點檢趙匡胤在陳橋驛被諸軍擁立，「有以黃衣加太祖身」，回師開封受禪，國號宋。此後削平荊南、湖南、後蜀、南漢、南唐，吳越納土，979年滅北漢。1004年與遼訂澶淵之盟，1038年後與西夏屢戰。神宗用王安石推行新法。1127年金人擄徽、欽二帝北去，北宋亡。
summary.en: In the first month of 960 Zhao Kuangyin, Commander of the Palace Army of Later Zhou, was proclaimed emperor by his troops at the Chenqiao post station — "someone put a yellow garment on him" — and returned to Kaifeng to take the abdication, naming his state Song. Jingnan, Hunan, Later Shu, Southern Han and Southern Tang were conquered, Wuyue surrendered its lands, and Northern Han fell in 979. Song made the Treaty of Chanyuan with Liao in 1004 and fought Xi Xia after 1038. Shenzong put Wang Anshi's New Laws into force. In 1127 the Jin carried the emperors Huizong and Qinzong north, and the Northern Song ended.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖本紀一
passages.textZh: 夜五鼓，軍士集驛門，宣言策點檢為天子，或止之，眾不聽。遲明，逼寢所，太宗入白，太祖起。諸校露刃列於庭，曰：「諸軍無主，願策太尉為天子。」未及對，有以黃衣加太祖身，眾皆羅拜，呼萬歲，即掖太祖乘馬。
passages.textEn: At the fifth watch of the night the soldiers gathered at the gate of the post station and declared that they would make the Commander of the Palace Army emperor; some tried to stop them, but the crowd would not listen. At dawn they pressed into his bedchamber; Taizong went in to tell him, and Taizu rose. The officers stood in the courtyard with drawn swords and said: "The armies have no lord. We wish to make the Grand Commandant emperor." Before he could answer, someone put a yellow garment on him; they all bowed around him and cried "Ten thousand years!", and helped him onto his horse.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二十三 欽宗本紀
passages.textZh: 夏四月庚申朔，大風吹石折木。金人以帝及皇后、皇太子北歸。凡法駕、鹵簿，皇后以下車輅、鹵簿，冠服、禮器、法物，大樂、教坊樂器，祭器、八寶、九鼎、圭璧，渾天儀、銅人、刻漏，古器、景靈宮供器，太清樓秘閣三館書、天下州府圖……
passages.textEn: On gengshen, the first day of the fourth month of summer, a great wind blew stones about and broke trees. The Jin took the emperor, the empress and the crown prince back north with them, and with them all the state carriages and processional regalia, the carriages and regalia of the empress and below, the robes, ritual vessels and sacred objects, the court and conservatory instruments, the sacrificial vessels, the eight seals, the nine cauldrons, the jade tablets, the armillary sphere, the bronze acupuncture figure, the clepsydras, the antiques, the vessels of the Jingling Temple, the books of the Taiqing Tower, the Secret Pavilion and the Three Institutes, the maps of all the prefectures of the realm…

summary.zh: 1127年五月康王趙構即位於應天府，改元建炎；後南渡，以臨安為行在。1141年與金議和，以淮水中流為界，割唐、鄧二州，向金稱臣。1161年金主完顏亮南侵，至采石。1234年與蒙古聯軍滅金，隨即與蒙古交戰；1273年襄陽、樊城陷落，1276年臨安出降，1279年崖山兵敗，陸秀夫負帝昺投海，宋亡。
summary.en: In the fifth month of 1127 Zhao Gou, Prince of Kang, took the throne at Yingtian prefecture, proclaiming the Jianyan era; he later moved south and made Lin'an (Hangzhou) his "temporary" capital. In 1141 Song made peace with Jin, with the border along the middle of the Huai, ceding Tang and Deng prefectures and calling itself Jin's subject. In 1161 the Jin ruler Wanyan Liang invaded and reached Caishi. In 1234 Song and the Mongols together destroyed Jin, then fell to fighting each other; Xiangyang and Fancheng fell in 1273, Lin'an surrendered in 1276, and after the defeat at Yashan in 1279 Lu Xiufei leapt into the sea with the boy emperor Bing on his back, and Song ended.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二十四 高宗本紀一
passages.textZh: 五月庚寅朔，帝登壇受命，禮畢慟哭，遙謝二帝，即位於府治。改元建炎。大赦，常赦所不原者咸赦除之。張邦昌及應于供奉金國之人，一切不問。
passages.textEn: On gengyin, the first day of the fifth month, the emperor ascended the altar and received the mandate; when the rite was over he wept bitterly, bowing in the distance to the two emperors, and took the throne in the prefectural office. The era was changed to Jianyan. There was a great amnesty, pardoning even crimes not normally pardoned; Zhang Bangchang and all who had served the Jin were not to be questioned.

passages.sourceEn: History of Jin (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷七十七 宗弼傳
passages.textZh: 宋主遣端明殿學士何鑄等進誓表，其表曰：「臣構言，今來畫疆，合以淮水中流為界，西有唐、鄧州割屬上國。自鄧州西四十裏並南四十裏為界，屬鄧州。其四十裏外並西南盡屬光化軍，為弊邑沿邊州城。既蒙恩造，許備籓方，世世子孫，謹守臣節。
passages.textEn: The Song ruler sent He Zhu, Academician of the Duanming Hall, and others with a sworn memorial, which said: "Your subject Gou says: in fixing the border now, it shall run along the middle of the Huai River; to the west, Tang and Deng prefectures are ceded to the superior state. Forty li west and forty li south of Dengzhou shall be the line, belonging to Dengzhou; beyond those forty li, to the west and south-west, all belongs to Guanghua Army, as border towns of our humble state. Having received your favour and been allowed to serve as a frontier vassal, we and our sons and grandsons for all generations will keep the duty of subjects."

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 瀛國公本紀 二王附
passages.textZh: 諸軍潰，翟國秀及團練使劉俊等解甲降。大軍至中軍，會暮，且風雨，昏霧四塞，咫尺不相辨。世傑乃與蘇劉義斷維，以十餘舟奪港而去，陸秀夫走衛王舟，王舟大，且諸舟環結，度不得出走，乃負昺投海中，後宮及諸臣多從死者，七日，浮屍出於海十餘萬人。楊太后聞昺死，撫膺大慟曰：「我忍死艱關至此者，正爲趙氏一塊肉爾，今無望矣！」遂赴海死，世傑葬之海濱，已而世傑亦自溺死。宋遂亡。
passages.textEn: The armies broke; Zhai Guoxiu, the militia commissioner Liu Jun and others took off their armour and surrendered. When the great army reached the central squadron, night was falling with wind and rain, and a dark fog shut everything in, so that one could not see a foot ahead. Shijie and Su Liuyi cut their moorings and fought their way out of the harbour with a dozen ships. Lu Xiufei went to the Prince of Wei's ship; it was large and lashed in a ring with the others, and judging it could not escape, he took Bing on his back and leapt into the sea. Many of the palace women and ministers died with them; after seven days more than a hundred thousand bodies floated up out of the sea. When Empress Dowager Yang heard that Bing was dead she beat her breast and wailed: "I endured death and hardship to come this far only for this one morsel of Zhao flesh — now there is no hope!" She threw herself into the sea. Shijie buried her on the shore, and soon drowned himself too. And so Song ended.

summary.zh: 党項首領元昊於1038年十月郊壇備禮，即皇帝位，「國稱大夏，年號天授禮法延祚」，史稱西夏，都興州（興慶府）。元昊自製蕃書（西夏文），命野利仁榮演繹，以之紀事、譯經。與宋、遼（後為金）鼎立近兩百年，1227年為蒙古所滅。
summary.en: In the tenth month of 1038 the Tangut leader Yuanhao took the throne with full rites at the suburban altar: "the state was named Great Xia, and the era Tianshou Lifa Yanzuo" — the "Western Xia" of the histories, with its capital at Xingzhou (Xingqing). Yuanhao devised a native script, which Yeli Renrong elaborated, and used it for records and translations. Xia stood against Song and Liao (later Jin) for nearly two hundred years and fell to the Mongols in 1227.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百八十五 夏國傳上
passages.textZh: 遂以十月十一日郊壇備禮，為世祖始文本武興法建禮仁孝皇帝，國稱大夏，年號天授禮法延祚。
passages.textEn: [Yuanhao's memorial to Song:] "So on the eleventh day of the tenth month, with full rites at the suburban altar, I became the Emperor Shiwen Benwu Xingfa Jianli Renxiao, the state was named Great Xia, and the era Tianshou Lifa Yanzuo."

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百八十五 夏國傳上
passages.textZh: 元昊自製蕃書，命野利仁榮演繹之，成十二卷，字形體方整類八分，而畫頗重複。教國人紀事用蕃書，而譯孝經、爾雅、四言雜字為蕃語。
passages.textEn: Yuanhao devised a native script himself and had Yeli Renrong elaborate it, in twelve chapters; the characters were square like the bafen style of clerical script, but with many strokes repeated. He taught his people to keep records in the native script, and had the Classic of Filial Piety, the Erya and the Four-Character Miscellany translated into the native language.

summary.zh: 女真完顏部首領阿骨打於1115年正月即皇帝位，以「賓鐵雖堅，終亦變壞，惟金不變不壞」，國號大金。1125年滅遼，1127年擄宋徽、欽二帝。1153年遷都燕京（中都）。受蒙古進逼，1214年南遷開封；1233年哀宗入蔡州，1234年正月城破，哀宗自縊，末帝承麟為亂兵所殺，金亡。
summary.en: In the first month of 1115 Aguda of the Jurchen Wanyan clan took the throne and named his state Great Jin — Gold — because "hard as fine iron is, in the end it changes and decays; only gold does not change or decay". Jin destroyed Liao in 1125 and carried off the Song emperors in 1127. It moved its capital to Yanjing (Zhongdu) in 1153. Pressed by the Mongols, it moved south to Kaifeng in 1214; in 1233 Emperor Aizong entered Caizhou, and when the city fell in the first month of 1234 he hanged himself and the last emperor Chenglin was killed — the end of Jin.

passages.sourceEn: History of Jin (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷二 太祖本紀
passages.textZh: 收國元年正月壬申朔，群臣奉上尊號。是日，即皇帝位。上曰：「遼以賓鐵爲號，取其堅也。賓鐵雖堅，終亦變壞，惟金不變不壞。金之色白，完顏部色尚白。」于是國號大金，改元收國。丙子，上自將攻黃龍府，進臨益州。
passages.textEn: In the first year of Shouguo, on renshen, the first day of the first month, the ministers presented him with an imperial title, and that day he took the throne. He said: "Liao took its name from fine iron, for its hardness. But hard as fine iron is, in the end it changes and decays; only gold does not change or decay. The colour of gold is white, and the Wanyan tribe honours white." So the state was named Great Jin [Gold], and the era Shouguo. On bingzi the emperor marched in person against Huanglong and advanced to Yizhou.

passages.sourceEn: History of Jin (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷十八 哀宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 己酉，承麟即皇帝位。百官稱賀。禮畢，亟出捍敵，而南面已立幟。俄頃，四面呼聲震天地。南面守者棄門，大軍入，與城中軍巷戰，城中軍不能禦。帝自縊于幽蘭軒。末帝退保子城，聞帝崩，率群臣入哭，諡曰哀宗。哭奠未畢，城潰，諸禁近舉火焚之。奉禦絳山收哀宗骨瘞之汝水上。末帝為亂兵所害，金亡。
passages.textEn: On jiyou Chenglin took the throne and the officials offered congratulations. The rite over, he hurried out to resist the enemy, but their banners were already raised on the south wall. In a moment shouts shook heaven and earth on all four sides. The defenders of the south gate abandoned it, the great army came in and fought in the streets, and the city's troops could not hold them. The emperor hanged himself in the Youlan Pavilion. The last emperor fell back to the inner citadel; hearing that the emperor was dead he led the ministers in to mourn and gave him the posthumous name Aizong. Before the mourning was done the city fell, and the attendants set fire to the body. The servant Jiang Shan gathered Aizong's bones and buried them by the Ru River. The last emperor was killed by the soldiery, and Jin ended.

summary.zh: 1206年鐵木真大會諸王群臣，建九游白旗，即皇帝位於斡難河之源，號成吉思皇帝。蒙古先後滅西夏（1227）、金（1234），西征至中亞與東歐。1259年蒙哥崩於釣魚山下。1271年忽必烈建國號大元，1272年以中都為大都。1276年取臨安，1279年崖山之戰後統一中國。
summary.en: In 1206 Temüjin held a great assembly of the princes and ministers, raised the white banner with nine tails and took the throne at the source of the Onon, as Chinggis Emperor. The Mongols destroyed Xi Xia (1227) and Jin (1234) and campaigned west into Central Asia and Eastern Europe. Möngke died beneath Diaoyu Mountain in 1259. In 1271 Khubilai proclaimed the dynastic name Great Yuan, and in 1272 made Zhongdu his capital as Dadu. Lin'an was taken in 1276, and after the battle of Yashan in 1279 all of China was under Yuan rule.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖本紀
passages.textZh: 元年丙寅，帝大會諸王羣臣，建九游白旗，即皇帝位於斡難河之源。諸王羣臣共上尊號曰成吉思皇帝。是歲實金泰和之六年也。
passages.textEn: In the first year, bingyin, the emperor held a great assembly of the princes and ministers, raised the white banner with nine tails, and took the throne at the source of the Onon River. The princes and ministers together gave him the title Chinggis Emperor. That year was in fact the sixth year of Taihe of the Jin.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷三 憲宗本紀
passages.textZh: 六月丁巳，汪田哥復選兵夜登外城馬軍寨，殺寨主及守城者。王堅率兵來戰。遲明，遇雨，梯折，後軍不克進而止。是月，帝不豫。秋七月辛亥，留精兵三千守之，餘悉攻重慶。癸亥，帝崩于釣魚山，壽五十有二，在位九年。
passages.textEn: On dingsi of the sixth month Wang Tiange again picked men to climb by night into the cavalry stockade of the outer wall, killing its commander and defenders. Wang Jian led his troops out to fight. At dawn it rained, the ladders broke, and the troops behind could not go on, so the attack stopped. That month the emperor fell ill. On xinhai of the seventh month he left three thousand picked men to hold the siege and sent the rest to attack Chongqing. On guihai the emperor died at Diaoyu Mountain, aged fifty-two, in the ninth year of his reign.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷八 世祖本紀五
passages.textZh: 癸亥，阿里海牙等大攻樊城，拔之，守將呂文煥懼而請降
passages.textEn: On guihai Ariq Qaya and others launched a great assault on Fancheng and took it; the commander Lü Wenhuan, afraid, asked to surrender.

summary.zh: 秦孝公十二年（前350）自櫟陽遷都於此。秦統一後收天下兵器聚之咸陽，銷以為鐘鐻及金人十二。前206年劉邦入咸陽，封府庫，還軍霸上；項羽隨後入城，焚燒宮室。漢改名渭城。
summary.en: Duke Xiao of Qin moved his capital here from Yueyang in 350 BCE. After unification the weapons of the realm were gathered here and melted down into bell stands and twelve bronze men. Liu Bang entered Xianyang in 206 BCE, sealed the storehouses and went back to Bashang; Xiang Yu came after him and burned the palaces. Han renamed the town Weicheng.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 分天下以為三十六郡，郡置守、尉、監。更名民曰「黔首」。大酺。收天下兵，聚之咸陽，銷以為鐘鐻，金人十二，重各千石，置廷宮中。一法度衡石丈尺。車同軌。書同文字。地東至海暨朝鮮，西至臨洮、羌中，南至北向戶，北據河為塞，并陰山至遼東。
passages.textEn: He divided the realm into thirty-six commanderies, each with a governor, a commandant and an inspector. The people were renamed "the black-headed". There was a great feast. The weapons of the realm were gathered at Xianyang and melted down into bell stands and twelve bronze men, each weighing a thousand dan, which were set in the palace. Laws, weights and measures were made uniform. Carts had the same axle width. Writing used the same characters. The land reached east to the sea and Chaoxian, west to Lintao and the Qiang country, south to the lands where doors face north, and north to the Yellow River, held as a frontier, along the Yin Mountains to Liaodong.

summary.zh: 齊國都城，自西周至戰國末。前221年秦軍入齊，齊亡。
summary.en: Capital of Qi from the Western Zhou to the end of the Warring States. Qin troops took Qi in 221 BCE.

confidenceNote.zh: 楚都屢遷，「郢」可指數地；此處標紀南城。
confidenceNote.en: Chu moved its capital several times and "Ying" can mean more than one place; the marker is at Jinan cheng.

summary.zh: 楚國都城，在今湖北荊州紀南城一帶。前506年吳軍「比至郢，五戰，楚五敗」，攻入郢都；前278年秦將白起拔郢，楚東遷於陳。
summary.en: Capital of Chu, at Jinan cheng near modern Jingzhou in Hubei. In 506 BCE the Wu army "fought five times on the way to Ying and Chu lost five times", and entered the city; in 278 BCE the Qin general Bai Qi took Ying and Chu moved its capital east to Chen.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷三十一 吳太伯世家
passages.textZh: 九年，吳王闔廬請伍子胥、孫武曰：「始子之言郢未可入，今果如何？」二子對曰：「楚將子常貪，而唐、蔡皆怨之。王必欲大伐，必得唐、蔡乃可。」闔廬從之，悉興師，與唐、蔡西伐楚，至於漢水。楚亦發兵拒吳，夾水陳。吳王闔廬弟夫槩欲戰，闔廬弗許。夫槩曰：「王已屬臣兵，兵以利爲上，尚何待焉？」遂以其部五千人襲冒楚，楚兵大敗，走。於是吳王遂縱兵追之。比至郢，五戰，楚五敗。楚昭王亡出郢，奔鄖。鄖公弟欲弑昭王，昭王與鄖公犇隨。而吳兵遂入郢。子胥、伯嚭鞭平王之屍以報父讎。
passages.textEn: In his ninth year Helü, King of Wu, asked Wu Zixu and Sun Wu: "At first you said Ying could not yet be entered. How is it now?" They answered: "The Chu general Zichang is greedy and Tang and Cai both resent him. If Your Majesty wants a great campaign, you must have Tang and Cai." Helü followed this, raised his whole army and with Tang and Cai went west against Chu as far as the Han River. Chu too sent troops to resist, and the armies drew up on either side of the river. Fugai, Helü's younger brother, wanted to fight; Helü would not allow it. Fugai said: "Your Majesty has entrusted troops to me. In war advantage comes first — what are we waiting for?" With his own five thousand men he fell on Chu, and the Chu army was badly beaten and fled. Then the King of Wu let his army loose in pursuit. By the time they reached Ying they had fought five times and Chu had lost five times. King Zhao of Chu fled from Ying to Yun; the younger brother of the lord of Yun wanted to kill him, and he fled with the lord of Yun to Sui. The Wu army entered Ying. Zixu and Bo Pi flogged the corpse of King Ping to avenge their fathers.

summary.zh: 趙國都城（前386年起）。前259–前257年秦軍圍邯鄲，魏、楚來救而解圍；前228年秦破邯鄲。
summary.en: Capital of Zhao from 386 BCE. Qin besieged it from 259 to 257 BCE until Wei and Chu relieved it; Qin took it in 228 BCE.

summary.zh: 戰國時魏都大梁；隋唐為汴州，汴河（通濟渠）在此，漕運繁盛。後梁、後晉、後漢、後周及北宋皆都於此（北宋稱東京開封府）。1127年靖康之變後為金所有，1214年金南遷於此，1233年降於蒙古。
summary.en: Daliang, capital of Wei in the Warring States. Under Sui and Tang it was Bianzhou on the Bian River (the Tongji Canal), a great hub of grain transport. Later Liang, Later Jin, Later Han, Later Zhou and the Northern Song all made it their capital (the Song "Eastern Capital, Kaifeng prefecture"). Jin held it after 1127, moved its own court here in 1214, and surrendered it to the Mongols in 1233.

summary.zh: 隋置杭州，江南河南端。五代吳越國都。1129年升為臨安府，1138年起為南宋行在。1276年元軍至，宋廷出降。
summary.en: Hangzhou prefecture was created by Sui at the southern end of the Jiangnan Canal. It was the capital of the Wuyue kingdom in the Five Dynasties. Raised to Lin'an prefecture in 1129, it was the "temporary capital" of Southern Song from 1138. The Song court surrendered to the Yuan army here in 1276.

note.en: prefecture name under Sui, Tang and the Five Dynasties

summary.zh: 戰國燕都薊。隋唐為幽州，安祿山由此起兵。938年入契丹，升為南京（燕京）。1153年金遷都於此，稱中都；1215年為蒙古所破。1272年忽必烈以之為大都。
summary.en: Ji, capital of Yan in the Warring States. Youzhou under Sui and Tang, from which An Lushan marched in 755. Given to the Khitan in 938, it became their Southern Capital (Yanjing). Jin made it its capital, Zhongdu, in 1153; the Mongols took it in 1215, and Khubilai made it his capital, Dadu, in 1272.

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷四 太宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 是月，晉復遣趙瑩奉表來賀，以幽、薊、瀛、莫、涿、檀、順、媯、儒、新、武、雲、應、朔、寰、蔚十六州並圖籍來獻。於是詔以皇都為上京，府曰臨潢。升幽州為南京，南京為東京。
passages.textEn: That month Jin again sent Zhao Ying with a memorial of congratulation, presenting the sixteen prefectures of You, Ji, Ying, Mo, Zhuo, Tan, Shun, Gui, Ru, Xin, Wu, Yun, Ying, Shuo, Huan and Yu, with their maps and registers. An edict then made the imperial capital the Upper Capital, with the prefecture called Linhuang; Youzhou was raised to the Southern Capital, and the old Southern Capital became the Eastern Capital.

summary.zh: 魯國都城。孔子生於魯，周遊列國後返魯，卒葬於此。
summary.en: Capital of Lu. Confucius was born in Lu and came back to it after his years of wandering; he died and was buried here.

summary.zh: 漢武帝時置敦煌郡，為河西走廊西端、出玉門關與陽關通往西域的門戶。唐稱沙州；8世紀80年代入吐蕃，848年張議潮起兵逐吐蕃，歸義軍據之。莫高窟藏經洞（1900年發現）保存大量寫本。
summary.en: Han Wudi created Dunhuang commandery at the western end of the Hexi Corridor, the gateway through the Yumen and Yang passes to the Western Regions. Called Shazhou under Tang; held by Tubo from the 780s until Zhang Yichao drove them out in 848, after which the Guiyi Army ruled it. The library cave at Mogao (found in 1900) preserved a vast trove of manuscripts.

summary.zh: 党項李德明築懷遠鎮為興州以居，元昊升為興慶府，西夏都城，在今寧夏銀川。1227年為蒙古所破。
summary.en: Li Deming of the Tanguts built up the town of Huaiyuan as Xingzhou to live in; Yuanhao raised it to Xingqing prefecture, the capital of Xi Xia, at modern Yinchuan in Ningxia. The Mongols took it in 1227.

summary.zh: 遼的皇都，938年定名上京臨潢府，在今內蒙古巴林左旗。1120年為金所破。
summary.en: The imperial capital of Liao, named Upper Capital Linhuang in 938, in modern Bairin Left Banner, Inner Mongolia. Taken by Jin in 1120.

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷四 太宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 是月，晉復遣趙瑩奉表來賀，以幽、薊、瀛、莫、涿、檀、順、媯、儒、新、武、雲、應、朔、寰、蔚十六州並圖籍來獻。於是詔以皇都為上京，府曰臨潢。升幽州為南京，南京為東京。
passages.textEn: That month Jin again sent Zhao Ying with a memorial of congratulation, presenting the sixteen prefectures of You, Ji, Ying, Mo, Zhuo, Tan, Shun, Gui, Ru, Xin, Wu, Yun, Ying, Shuo, Huan and Yu, with their maps and registers. An edict then made the imperial capital the Upper Capital, with the prefecture called Linhuang; Youzhou was raised to the Southern Capital, and the old Southern Capital became the Eastern Capital.

summary.zh: 金初都城，在今黑龍江阿城白城子。1153年海陵王遷都燕京後一度削去上京之號。
summary.en: The first capital of Jin, at Baichengzi near Acheng in Heilongjiang. After the move to Yanjing in 1153 the Prince of Hailing briefly abolished its status as Upper Capital.

summary.zh: 蒙古帝國都城，窩闊台於1235年築城，在今蒙古國鄂爾渾河畔。忽必烈遷都開平與大都後地位下降。
summary.en: Capital of the Mongol Empire, walled by Ögedei in 1235, on the Orkhon in modern Mongolia. It declined after Khubilai moved the capital to Kaiping and Dadu.

summary.zh: 漢廣陵，隋改江都，運河與長江交會處。隋煬帝三下江都，618年在此為宇文化及等所弒。唐代為東南最繁華的商業城市。
summary.en: Han Guangling, renamed Jiangdu by Sui, where the canal meets the Yangtze. Emperor Yang of Sui went there three times and was murdered there by Yuwen Huaji and others in 618. Under Tang it was the richest commercial city of the south-east.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷四 煬帝紀下
passages.textZh: 二年三月，右屯衞將軍宇文化及，武賁郎將司馬德戡、元禮，監門直閣裴虔通，將作少監宇文智及，武勇郎將趙行樞，鷹揚郎將孟景，內史舍人元敏，符璽郎李覆、牛方裕，千牛左右李孝本、弟孝質，直長許弘仁、薛世良，城門郎唐奉義，醫正張愷等，以驍果作亂，入犯宮闈。上崩于溫室，時年五十。蕭后令宮人撤牀簀為棺以埋之。
passages.textEn: In the third month of the second year, Yuwen Huaji, General of the Right Encampment Guard, with Sima Dekan and Yuan Li, Pei Qiantong, Yuwen Zhiji, Zhao Xingshu, Meng Jing, Yuan Min, Li Fu, Niu Fangyu, Li Xiaoben and his brother Xiaozhi, Xu Hongren, Xue Shiliang, Tang Fengyi, the physician Zhang Kai and others, rose with the Courageous Guards and broke into the palace. The emperor died in the Warm Chamber, aged fifty. Empress Xiao had the palace women take apart a bed to make a coffin and buried him.

summary.zh: 在今重慶合川東，嘉陵江、渠江、涪江匯流處的山城。南宋余玠於1243年築城，王堅守城；1259年蒙哥汗攻城不下，崩於城下。
summary.en: A hill fortress east of modern Hechuan, Chongqing, where the Jialing, Qu and Fu rivers meet. Built by Yu Jie of Southern Song in 1243 and held by Wang Jian; Möngke Khan failed to take it in 1259 and died before its walls.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷三 憲宗本紀
passages.textZh: 六月丁巳，汪田哥復選兵夜登外城馬軍寨，殺寨主及守城者。王堅率兵來戰。遲明，遇雨，梯折，後軍不克進而止。是月，帝不豫。秋七月辛亥，留精兵三千守之，餘悉攻重慶。癸亥，帝崩于釣魚山，壽五十有二，在位九年。
passages.textEn: On dingsi of the sixth month Wang Tiange again picked men to climb by night into the cavalry stockade of the outer wall, killing its commander and defenders. Wang Jian led his troops out to fight. At dawn it rained, the ladders broke, and the troops behind could not go on, so the attack stopped. That month the emperor fell ill. On xinhai of the seventh month he left three thousand picked men to hold the siege and sent the rest to attack Chongqing. On guihai the emperor died at Diaoyu Mountain, aged fifty-two, in the ninth year of his reign.

summary.zh: 名夷吾，齊桓公之相。輔佐桓公成為春秋第一位霸主；桓公自言「九合諸侯，一匡天下」。桓公欲封禪泰山，管仲固諫而止。
summary.en: Guan Yiwu, chief minister to Duke Huan of Qi, who under his guidance became the first hegemon of the Spring and Autumn period; the duke boasted that he had "nine times gathered the lords and once set all under Heaven right". When the duke wanted to perform the feng and shan sacrifices on Mount Tai, Guan Zhong argued him out of it.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷三十二 齊太公世家
passages.textZh: 寡人南伐至召陵，望熊山；北伐山戎、離枝、孤竹；西伐大夏，涉流沙；束馬懸車登太行，至卑耳山而還。諸侯莫違寡人。寡人兵車之會三，乘車之會六，九合諸侯，一匡天下。
passages.textEn: "I have campaigned south as far as Shaoling, within sight of Mount Xiong; north against the Mountain Rong, Lizhi and Guzhu; west against Daxia, across the shifting sands; I have bound up my horses and slung my chariots to climb the Taihang and turned back only at Mount Bei'er. None of the lords defies me. I have held three assemblies under arms and six in carriages; nine times I have gathered the lords and once set all under Heaven right."

confidenceNote.zh: 生年據通行說法；流亡路線依《史記·晉世家》《左傳》，各地停留年份為約數。
confidenceNote.en: Year of birth by the usual reckoning; the exile route follows the Shiji and the Zuo zhuan, and the years at each stop are approximate.

summary.zh: 名重耳，晉獻公之子。驪姬之亂中出奔，流亡狄、衛、齊、曹、宋、鄭、楚、秦等地十九年，前636年在秦穆公支持下回國即位。前632年率晉軍與宋、齊、秦之師在城濮大敗楚軍——開戰前依昔日在楚時的承諾「退三舍」——此後在踐土會盟，成為霸主。
summary.en: Chong'er, son of Duke Xian of Jin, fled during the troubles stirred up by Lady Li and wandered for nineteen years among the Di, Wey, Qi, Cao, Song, Zheng, Chu and Qin before returning with Duke Mu of Qin's backing to take the throne in 636 BCE. In 632 BCE he crushed Chu at Chengpu with the armies of Song, Qi and Qin — first falling back "three stages", as he had promised the King of Chu during his exile — and then held the assembly at Jiantu as hegemon.

label.en: Flees to the Di, his mother's people
In Qi; Duke Huan gives him a wife
In Chu; promises the King to fall back three stages
In Qin; Duke Mu takes him in
Returns to Jin and takes the throne
Assembly at Jiantu; presents the Chu captives to Zhou

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷三十九 晉世家
passages.textZh: 楚得臣怒，撃晉師，晉師退。軍吏曰：「爲何退？」文公曰：「昔在楚，約退三舍，可倍乎！」楚師欲去，得臣不肯。四月戊辰，宋公、齊將、秦將與晉侯次城濮。己巳，與楚兵合戰，楚兵敗，得臣收餘兵去。甲午，晉師還至衡雍，作王宮于踐土。
passages.textEn: Dechen of Chu, enraged, attacked the Jin army, and the Jin army fell back. The officers asked: "Why do we retreat?" Duke Wen said: "When I was in Chu I promised to fall back three stages — can I break my word?" The Chu army wanted to leave, but Dechen would not. On wuchen of the fourth month the Duke of Song, the generals of Qi and Qin and the Marquis of Jin camped at Chengpu. On jisi they joined battle with the Chu army; the Chu army was beaten and Dechen gathered what was left and withdrew. On jiawu the Jin army returned to Hengyong and built a royal lodge at Jiantu.

confidenceNote.zh: 生年有前551、前552二說；周遊列國的路線與年份諸家考訂不一，地圖所示為示意。
confidenceNote.en: He was born in 551 or 552 BCE; the route and dates of his travels are reconstructed differently by different scholars, and the map is only indicative.

summary.zh: 名丘，字仲尼，魯國人。曾為季氏史，後為司空。其後「去魯，斥乎齊，逐乎宋、衞，困於陳蔡之間」，終於返魯，整理典籍、教授弟子。
summary.en: Kong Qiu, courtesy name Zhongni, of Lu. He served the Ji family as a steward and later as Minister of Works. Then he "left Lu, was rejected in Qi, driven out of Song and Wey, and trapped between Chen and Cai", and at last came home to Lu, where he edited the old texts and taught his disciples.

label.zh: 過宋，宋司馬桓魋欲殺之
label.en: Passes through Song; Huan Tui tries to kill him

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 孔子世家
passages.textZh: 孔子貧且賤。及長，嘗為季氏史，料量平；嘗為司職吏而畜蕃息。由是為司空。已而去魯，斥乎齊，逐乎宋、衞，困於陳蔡之間，於是反魯。
passages.textEn: Confucius was poor and of low station. Grown up, he served the Ji family as a steward, and his measures were fair; as a keeper of livestock, and the herds multiplied. So he became Minister of Works. Then he left Lu, was rejected in Qi, driven out of Song and Wey, and trapped between Chen and Cai, and so came back to Lu.

summary.zh: 越王。前496年在檇李擊敗吳軍，吳王闔廬傷死。前494年反為夫差所敗於夫椒，以餘兵五千人保棲會稽，卑辭厚禮求和。歸國後「置膽於坐，坐臥即仰膽，飲食亦嘗膽」，與百姓同其勞。前473年滅吳。
summary.en: King of Yue. In 496 BCE he beat Wu at Zuili and King Helü died of his wound. In 494 BCE Fuchai beat him at Fujiao; he took refuge on Kuaiji with five thousand men and sued humbly for peace. Back home he "set a gall bladder by his seat, looked up at it sitting or lying, and tasted it when he ate or drank", sharing the toil of his people. In 473 BCE he destroyed Wu.

label.en: Takes refuge on Kuaiji and sues for peace

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十一 越王句踐世家
passages.textZh: 元年，呉王闔廬聞允常死，乃興師伐越。越王句踐使死士挑戰，三行，至呉陳，呼而自剄。呉師觀之，越因襲撃呉師，呉師敗於檇李，射傷呉王闔廬。闔廬且死，告其子夫差曰：「必毋忘越。」
passages.textEn: In the first year Helü, King of Wu, heard that Yunchang was dead and raised an army against Yue. Goujian, King of Yue, sent men sworn to die to challenge them: three ranks of them walked up to the Wu lines, shouted and cut their own throats. While the Wu army stared, Yue attacked and beat it at Zuili, and King Helü was wounded by an arrow. As he was dying he told his son Fuchai: "Never forget Yue."

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十一 越王句踐世家
passages.textZh: 三年，句踐聞呉王夫差日夜勒兵，且以報越，越欲先呉未發往伐之。范蠡諫曰：「不可。臣聞兵者凶器也，戰者逆德也，爭者事之末也。陰謀逆德，好用凶器，試身於所末，上帝禁之，行者不利。」越王曰：「吾已決之矣。」遂興師。呉王聞之，悉發精兵撃越，敗之夫椒。越王乃以餘兵五千人保棲於會稽。呉王追而圍之。
passages.textEn: In the third year Goujian heard that Fuchai, King of Wu, was drilling his troops day and night to take revenge on Yue, and wanted to strike before Wu moved. Fan Li remonstrated: "No. I have heard that arms are instruments of ill omen, war goes against virtue, and contention is the last of all things. To plot against virtue and delight in ill-omened instruments, staking oneself on the last of things, is forbidden by Heaven; whoever does it will not prosper." The King of Yue said: "I have decided." He raised his army. When the King of Wu heard, he sent all his best troops against Yue and beat them at Fujiao. The King of Yue took refuge on Kuaiji with the five thousand men he had left, and the King of Wu pursued and besieged him.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十一 越王句踐世家
passages.textZh: 呉旣赦越，越王句踐反國，乃苦身焦思，置膽於坐，坐臥卽仰膽，飲食亦嘗膽也。曰：「女忘會稽之恥邪？」身自耕作，夫人自織，食不加肉，衣不重采，折節下賢人，厚遇賓客，振貧弔死，與百姓同其勞。
passages.textEn: When Wu had pardoned Yue and Goujian had gone home, he punished his body and wore out his mind. He set a gall bladder by his seat and looked up at it sitting or lying, and tasted it when he ate or drank, saying: "Have you forgotten the shame of Kuaiji?" He ploughed with his own hands and his wife wove; he ate no second meat and wore no second colour; he humbled himself before worthy men, treated his guests generously, relieved the poor, mourned the dead and shared the toil of the common people.

fiction.zh: 「臥薪」不見於《史記》，《史記》只記「嘗膽」。「臥薪嘗膽」連用是宋代以後的說法（如蘇軾《擬孫權答曹操書》）。句踐入吳為奴三年的情節見於《國語》《吳越春秋》，不見於《史記·越王句踐世家》。
fiction.en: "Sleeping on brushwood" is not in the Shiji, which mentions only the gall. The phrase "sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall" appears from the Song onward (e.g. Su Shi). The story that Goujian served three years as a slave in Wu comes from the Guoyu and the later Wu Yue chunqiu, not from the Shiji.

summary.zh: 衛國公子，名鞅，入秦。秦孝公以為左庶長，定變法之令：什伍連坐，告姦者與斬敵首同賞；二男以上不分家者倍賦；軍功授爵；努力耕織者免役。後封於商，號商君。孝公死後被車裂。
summary.en: A prince of Wey named Yang, who went to Qin. Duke Xiao made him Zuo Shuzhang and decreed his new laws: households grouped in fives and tens and punished together, denouncing a crime rewarded like taking an enemy head; double tax on households with two grown sons living together; rank for merit in war; exemption from labour for diligent farmers and weavers. He was enfeoffed at Shang as Lord Shang. After Duke Xiao died he was torn apart by chariots.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六十八 商君列傳
passages.textZh: 以衛鞅為左庶長，卒定變法之令。令民為什伍，而相牧司連坐。不告姦者腰斬，告姦者與斬敵首同賞，匿姦者與降敵同罰。民有二男以上不分異者，倍其賦。有軍功者，各以率受上爵；為私斗者，各以輕重被刑大小。戮力本業，耕織致粟帛多者復其身
passages.textEn: Wei Yang was made Zuo Shuzhang and the decrees changing the laws were settled at last. The people were organised in groups of ten and five, to watch each other and share each other's punishments. Whoever failed to denounce a crime was cut in two at the waist; whoever denounced one was rewarded as if he had taken an enemy head; whoever hid a criminal was punished as if he had surrendered to the enemy. A household with two or more grown sons who did not set up separately paid double tax. Those with merit in war received rank according to a scale; those who fought private quarrels were punished according to the gravity. Those who worked hard at the basic occupations, and produced much grain and cloth by ploughing and weaving, were exempted from labour service.

confidenceNote.zh: 卒年有前278年等數說。
confidenceNote.en: The year of his death is disputed; 278 BCE is one of several dates.

summary.zh: 名平，楚國貴族，事楚懷王，任左徒。遭讒被疏，流放江南，作《離騷》等辭。後懷石自沉汨羅。宋玉、唐勒、景差等皆祖其辭令。
summary.en: Qu Ping, a noble of Chu who served King Huai as Zuotu. Slandered and pushed aside, he was banished south of the Yangtze, where he wrote the Lisao and other poems. In the end he drowned himself in the Miluo, clasping a stone. Song Yu, Tang Le, Jing Cha and others all modelled their poetry on his.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八十四 屈原賈生列傳
passages.textZh: 於是懷石遂自（投）［沈］汨羅以死。
passages.textEn: Then, clasping a stone, he drowned himself in the Miluo.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八十四 屈原賈生列傳
passages.textZh: 屈原既死之後，楚有宋玉、唐勒、景差之徒者，皆好辭而以賦見稱；然皆祖屈原之從容辭令，終莫敢直諫。
passages.textEn: After Qu Yuan's death Chu had men such as Song Yu, Tang Le and Jing Cha, who loved poetry and were known for their rhapsodies; but though they all modelled themselves on Qu Yuan's graceful language, none ever dared to remonstrate openly.

summary.zh: 衛人，遊於燕。燕太子丹使之刺秦王。太子及賓客白衣冠送至易水之上，高漸離擊筑，荊軻和歌「風蕭蕭兮易水寒，壯士一去兮不復還」。至秦，獻督亢地圖，圖窮匕見，刺秦王不中，被殺。
summary.en: A man of Wey who went to Yan. Crown Prince Dan sent him to assassinate the King of Qin. The prince and his retainers, dressed in white, saw him off at the River Yi; Gao Jianli struck the zhu and Jing Ke sang "The wind sighs, the River Yi is cold; the hero goes and will not return." In Qin he presented a map of Dukang; when the map was unrolled the dagger was revealed, but he missed the king and was killed.

label.en: Attacks the King of Qin at Xianyang and is killed

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八十六 刺客列傳
passages.textZh: 太子及賓客知其事者，皆白衣冠以送之。至易水之上，既祖，取道，髙漸離撃筑，荊軻和而歌，爲變徴之聲，士皆垂涙涕泣。又前而爲歌曰：「風蕭蕭兮易水寒，壯士一去兮不復還！」復爲羽聲慨，士皆瞋目，發盡上指冠。於是荊軻就車而去，終已不顧。
passages.textEn: The crown prince and those of his retainers who knew of the plan saw him off dressed in white. At the River Yi, after the sacrifice to the road, Gao Jianli struck the zhu and Jing Ke sang to it in the mournful bianzhi mode, and all the men wept. Then he stepped forward and sang: "The wind sighs, the River Yi is cold; the hero goes and will not return!" Then in the stirring yu mode, and every man glared, his hair standing up against his cap. And Jing Ke mounted his carriage and left, and never looked back.

summary.zh: 名政，前246年即秦王位。前230年至前221年先後滅韓、趙、魏、楚、燕、齊，「初并天下」，自號始皇帝。分天下為三十六郡，「車同軌，書同文字」。屢次巡行郡縣，上泰山封禪；前210年出巡途中至平原津而病，七月丙寅崩於沙丘平臺。
summary.en: Ying Zheng, King of Qin from 246 BCE. Between 230 and 221 BCE he destroyed Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan and Qi, "for the first time united the realm", and called himself First Emperor. He divided the realm into thirty-six commanderies — "carts with the same axle width, writing with the same characters". He toured the provinces again and again and performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai; on his last tour in 210 BCE he fell ill at the Pingyuan ford and died at Shaqiu on bingyin of the seventh month.

label.en: At Kuaiji; sacrifice to Yu the Great
Falls ill at the Pingyuan ford

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 二十六年，齊王建與其相后勝發兵守其西界，不通秦。秦使將軍王賁從燕南攻齊，得齊王建。
passages.textEn: In the twenty-sixth year Jian, King of Qi, and his chancellor Hou Sheng sent troops to guard their western border and cut off contact with Qin. Qin sent the general Wang Ben south from Yan to attack Qi, and captured Jian, King of Qi.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 分天下以為三十六郡，郡置守、尉、監。更名民曰「黔首」。大酺。收天下兵，聚之咸陽，銷以為鐘鐻，金人十二，重各千石，置廷宮中。一法度衡石丈尺。車同軌。書同文字。地東至海暨朝鮮，西至臨洮、羌中，南至北向戶，北據河為塞，并陰山至遼東。
passages.textEn: He divided the realm into thirty-six commanderies, each with a governor, a commandant and an inspector. The people were renamed "the black-headed". There was a great feast. The weapons of the realm were gathered at Xianyang and melted down into bell stands and twelve bronze men, each weighing a thousand dan, which were set in the palace. Laws, weights and measures were made uniform. Carts had the same axle width. Writing used the same characters. The land reached east to the sea and Chaoxian, west to Lintao and the Qiang country, south to the lands where doors face north, and north to the Yellow River, held as a frontier, along the Yin Mountains to Liaodong.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 二十八年，始皇東行郡縣，上鄒嶧山。立石，與魯諸儒生議，刻石頌秦德，議封禪望祭山川之事。乃遂上泰山，立石，封，祠祀。
passages.textEn: In the twenty-eighth year the First Emperor toured the eastern commanderies and climbed Mount Yi in Zou. He set up a stone, conferred with the Confucian scholars of Lu, had an inscription carved praising the virtue of Qin, and discussed the feng and shan sacrifices and the distant offerings to mountains and rivers. Then he climbed Mount Tai, set up a stone, performed the feng sacrifice and made offerings.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 至平原津而病。始皇惡言死，群臣莫敢言死事。上病益甚，乃為璽書賜公子扶蘇曰：「與喪會咸陽而葬。」書已封，在中車府令趙高行符璽事所，未授使者。七月丙寅，始皇崩於沙丘平臺。丞相斯為上崩在外，恐諸公子及天下有變，乃祕之，不發喪。
passages.textEn: At the Pingyuan ford he fell ill. The First Emperor hated talk of death and none of his ministers dared mention it. As he grew worse he wrote a sealed letter to Prince Fusu: "Meet the cortège at Xianyang and bury me." The letter was sealed but left with Zhao Gao, Director of the Palace Carriages, who kept the seals, and was never handed to a messenger. On bingyin of the seventh month the First Emperor died at the Pingtai terrace of Shaqiu. Chancellor Li Si, because the emperor had died away from the capital and he feared the princes and the realm might rise, kept it secret and announced no mourning.

summary.zh: 陽城人，字涉。秦二世元年（前209）七月與吳廣在大澤鄉率戍卒起事，號召「王侯將相寧有種乎」，詐稱公子扶蘇、項燕，稱大楚。攻下陳後自立為王，號張楚。前208年兵敗，為其御者莊賈所殺。
summary.en: Of Yangcheng, courtesy name She. In the seventh month of 209 BCE he and Wu Guang led a band of conscripts in revolt at Dazexiang — "Kings, nobles, generals and ministers: are they a breed apart?" — claiming to act for Prince Fusu and Xiang Yan and calling themselves Great Chu. After taking Chen he made himself king of "Zhang Chu". Defeated in 208 BCE, he was killed by his own driver Zhuang Jia.

label.en: Takes Chen and becomes King of Zhang Chu

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十八 陳涉世家
passages.textZh: 陳勝佐之，并殺兩尉。召令徒屬曰：「公等遇雨，皆已失期，失期當斬。
passages.textEn: Chen Sheng helped him and they killed both officers. He called the men together and said: "You have all been caught by the rain and are already late, and being late means death.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十八 陳涉世家
passages.textZh: 且壯士不死即已，死即舉大名耳，王侯將相寧有種乎！」徒屬皆曰：「敬受命。」乃詐稱公子扶蘇、項燕，從民欲也。袒右，稱大楚。為壇而盟，祭以尉首。陳勝自立為將軍，吳廣為都尉。攻大澤鄉，收而攻蘄。
passages.textEn: …And if a brave man is not to die, well and good; but if he dies, let him die making a great name. Kings, nobles, generals and ministers — are they a breed apart?" The men all said: "We take your orders." They falsely claimed to be led by Prince Fusu and Xiang Yan, as the people wished; they bared their right arms and called themselves Great Chu. They built an altar and swore an oath, offering the officers' heads in sacrifice. Chen Sheng made himself general and Wu Guang commandant. They attacked Dazexiang, took it and attacked Qi county.

summary.zh: 名籍，下相人，楚將項燕之孫。前209年隨叔父項梁起兵於吳。前207年鉅鹿之戰「皆沈船，破釜甑，燒廬舍，持三日糧」，大破秦軍。入關後自立為西楚霸王，都彭城，分封諸侯。楚漢相爭，前202年被圍垓下，夜聞四面楚歌，突圍至烏江，不肯渡江而死。
summary.en: Xiang Ji of Xiaxiang, grandson of the Chu general Xiang Yan. He rose with his uncle Xiang Liang at Wu in 209 BCE. At Julu in 207 BCE he "sank the boats, smashed the cooking pots, burned the huts and carried three days' rations" and crushed the Qin army. After entering the passes he made himself Hegemon-King of Western Chu, with his capital at Pengcheng, and parcelled out the realm among the lords. In the war with Han he was surrounded at Gaixia in 202 BCE, heard Chu songs on every side in the night, broke out to the Wu River and died there rather than cross.

label.en: Rises with Xiang Liang at Wu
The feast at Hongmen; enters Xianyang

label.zh: 自立為西楚霸王，都彭城
label.en: Hegemon-King of Western Chu at Pengcheng
At the Wu River; takes his own life

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀
passages.textZh: 項羽已殺卿子冠軍，威震楚國，名聞諸侯。乃遣當陽君、蒲將軍將卒二萬渡河，救鉅鹿。戰少利，陳餘復請兵。項羽乃悉引兵渡河，皆沈船，破釜甑，燒廬舍，持三日糧，以示士卒必死，無一還心。於是至則圍王離，與秦軍遇，九戰，絕其甬道，大破之，殺蘇角，虜王離。涉閒不降楚，自燒殺。當是時，楚兵冠諸侯。
passages.textEn: When Xiang Yu had killed the "Excellent General", his might shook Chu and his name was known to all the lords. He sent the Lord of Dangyang and General Pu across the river with twenty thousand men to relieve Julu. They had little success, and Chen Yu asked for more troops. Then Xiang Yu took his whole army across, sank the boats, smashed the cooking pots, burned the huts and carried three days' rations, to show the men they must die and not one would turn back. On arrival they surrounded Wang Li, met the Qin army, fought nine times, cut its walled supply road and crushed it, killed Su Jiao and captured Wang Li. She Jian would not surrender to Chu and burned himself to death. At that moment the army of Chu stood first among the lords.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀
passages.textZh: 項王軍壁垓下，兵少食盡，漢軍及諸侯兵圍之數重。夜聞漢軍四面皆楚歌，項王乃大驚曰：「漢皆已得楚乎？是何楚人之多也！」項王則夜起，飲帳中。有美人名虞，常幸從；駿馬名騅，常騎之。於是項王乃悲歌忼慨，自為詩曰：「力拔山兮氣蓋世，時不利兮騅不逝。騅不逝兮可柰何，虞兮虞兮柰若何！」
passages.textEn: King Xiang's army was walled up at Gaixia, few in number and out of food, and the Han army and the lords' troops encircled it several deep. In the night he heard Chu songs on every side of the Han lines. Greatly alarmed, he said: "Has Han already taken all of Chu? How many men of Chu there are!" He rose in the night and drank in his tent. He had a beauty named Yu who was always with him, and a fine horse named Zhui which he always rode. Then he sang a sad and passionate song of his own making: "My strength plucked up mountains, my spirit overtopped the world; but the times are against me and Zhui will run no more. If Zhui will run no more, what can I do? Yu, O Yu, what will become of you?"

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀
passages.textZh: 於是項王乃欲東渡烏江。烏江亭長檥船待，謂項王曰：「江東雖小，地方千里，眾數十萬人，亦足王也。願大王急渡。今獨臣有船，漢軍至，無以渡。」項王笑曰：「天之亡我，我何渡為！且籍與江東子弟八千人渡江而西，今無一人還，縱江東父兄憐而王我，我何面目見之？
passages.textEn: Then King Xiang wanted to cross east over the Wu River. The head of the Wujiang post had a boat ready and said: "Jiangdong may be small, but it is a thousand li square with several hundred thousand people — enough to be king of. I beg Your Majesty to cross quickly. I alone have a boat; when the Han army comes it will have no way across." King Xiang laughed: "Heaven is destroying me — why should I cross? Besides, I crossed the river and went west with eight thousand young men of Jiangdong, and now not one comes back. Even if the elders of Jiangdong pitied me and made me their king, how could I face them?

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀 太史公曰
passages.textZh: 五年，卒亡其國，身死東城，尚不覺寤，而不自責，過矣。
passages.textEn: In five years he lost his state and died at Dongcheng, and still did not wake up to it or blame himself — that was his error.

question.zh: 項羽死於烏江還是東城？
question.en: Did Xiang Yu die at the Wu River or at Dongcheng?

claim.zh: 〈項羽本紀〉記他欲東渡烏江，烏江亭長檥船相待，他笑而不渡，戰死於江邊。
claim.en: The Annals of Xiang Yu have him reach the Wu River, where the post chief waits with a boat; he laughs, refuses to cross and dies fighting by the river.

source.en: Shiji, Annals of Xiang Yu

accounts.quoteZh: 於是項王乃欲東渡烏江。

claim.zh: 《史記》他處把他的死繫於東城（今安徽定遠東南）；今人有主張他死於東城、未到烏江者，也有認為烏江亭本屬東城縣境、二說並不矛盾者。
claim.en: Other passages of the Shiji place his death at Dongcheng (south-east of modern Dingyuan, Anhui); some modern scholars argue he died there and never reached the Wu River, others that the Wujiang post lay within Dongcheng county, so the accounts agree.

source.zh: 《史記·項羽本紀》太史公曰及他篇；今人研究
source.en: Other chapters of the Shiji; modern scholarship

accounts.quoteZh: 身死東城

confidenceNote.zh: 生年有前256、前247二說。
confidenceNote.en: He was born in 256 or 247 BCE; both are argued.

summary.zh: 沛縣人，秦末起兵，稱沛公。前206年先入關，至咸陽，封府庫還軍霸上，與父老「約法三章」。受封漢王，與項羽爭天下，前202年垓下滅楚，即皇帝位。前200年北擊匈奴，被冒頓圍於白登七日。漢十二年過沛，置酒沛宮，作〈大風歌〉。
summary.en: Of Pei county, he rose at the end of Qin as "the Lord of Pei". In 206 BCE he was first through the passes; at Xianyang he sealed the storehouses, went back to Bashang and gave the elders his "code of three articles". Made King of Han, he fought Xiang Yu for the realm, destroyed Chu at Gaixia in 202 BCE and took the imperial throne. In 200 BCE he marched against the Xiongnu and was surrounded by Modu at Baideng for seven days. In his twelfth year, passing through Pei, he feasted his old neighbours and sang the "Song of the Great Wind".

label.zh: 入咸陽，還軍霸上，約法三章
label.en: Enters Xianyang; back to Bashang; the three articles

label.zh: 即皇帝位於定陶汜水之陽
label.en: Takes the imperial throne near Dingtao
Besieged at Baideng for seven days

label.zh: 過沛，作〈大風歌〉（漢十二年十月）
label.en: At Pei: the Song of the Great Wind (twelfth year of Han, tenth month)

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八 高祖本紀
passages.textZh: 遂西入咸陽。欲止宮休舍，樊噲、張良諫，乃封秦重寶財物府庫，還軍霸上。召諸縣父老豪桀曰：「父老苦秦苛法久矣，誹謗者族，偶語者棄市。吾與諸侯約，先入關者王之，吾當王關中。與父老約，法三章耳：殺人者死，傷人及盜抵罪。餘悉除去秦法。
passages.textEn: He went west into Xianyang. He wanted to stay in the palace, but Fan Kuai and Zhang Liang advised against it, so he sealed up the treasures and storehouses of Qin and took his army back to Bashang. He summoned the elders and leading men of the counties and said: "Elders, you have suffered long under Qin's harsh laws: for slander a man's whole clan was executed, for talking together men were executed in the market. I agreed with the lords that whoever first entered the passes would be king here, so I am to be king of Guanzhong. I agree with you, elders, on a code of three articles only: whoever kills shall die; whoever wounds or steals shall be punished accordingly. All the rest of Qin's laws are abolished.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八 高祖本紀
passages.textZh: 高祖還歸，過沛，留。置酒沛宮，悉召故人父老子弟縱酒，發沛中兒得百二十人，教之歌。酒酣，高祖擊筑，自為歌詩曰：「大風起兮雲飛揚，威加海內兮歸故鄉，安得猛士兮守四方！」令兒皆和習之。高祖乃起舞，慷慨傷懷，泣數行下。
passages.textEn: On his way home Gaozu passed through Pei and stayed. He gave a feast in the palace at Pei, called together all his old friends, the elders and the young men to drink freely, and chose a hundred and twenty boys of Pei and taught them to sing. When the wine was flowing Gaozu struck the zhu and sang a song of his own: "A great wind rises, the clouds fly up; my might is over all within the seas, and I come home; where shall I find brave men to guard the four quarters?" He had the boys learn to sing it with him. Then he rose and danced, moved and sorrowful, and tears ran down his face.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十 匈奴列傳
passages.textZh: 冒頓匿其精兵，見其羸弱，於是漢悉兵，多步兵，三十二萬，北逐之。高帝先至平城，步兵未盡到，冒頓縱精兵四十萬騎圍高帝於白登，七日，漢兵中外不得相救餉。
passages.textEn: Modu hid his best troops and showed only the weak, so Han sent its whole army — mostly infantry, three hundred and twenty thousand men — north in pursuit. Gaodi reached Pingcheng first, before all his infantry had arrived, and Modu let loose four hundred thousand picked horsemen and surrounded him at Baideng. For seven days the Han troops inside and outside could neither help nor supply each other.

confidenceNote.zh: 出發年份有前139、前138二說；被拘之地與路線為約略。
confidenceNote.en: He set out in 139 or 138 BCE; where he was held and the exact route are approximate.

summary.zh: 漢中人。武帝時應募出使大月氏，欲與之共擊匈奴。途中為匈奴所拘十餘年，脫身後經大宛、康居抵大月氏，又至大夏。歸途再被匈奴所得，前126年乘匈奴內亂逃回長安：出發時百餘人，去十三歲，唯二人得還。他親歷大宛、大月氏、大夏、康居，並把聽聞的西方諸國報告武帝。後又出使烏孫，封博望侯。
summary.en: Of Hanzhong. Under Emperor Wu he volunteered to go as envoy to the Great Yuezhi, to win them as allies against the Xiongnu. Held by the Xiongnu for more than ten years on the way, he escaped and went on through Dayuan and Kangju to the Yuezhi and on to Daxia. Caught again by the Xiongnu on the way back, he escaped to Chang'an in 126 BCE during their civil war: of over a hundred men who set out, only two came back after thirteen years. He had seen Dayuan, the Yuezhi, Daxia and Kangju himself and reported on the other states he heard of. He later went as envoy to the Wusun, and was made Marquis of Bowang.

label.en: Held by the Xiongnu for over ten years

label.zh: 歸途經羌中，再為匈奴所得
label.en: Caught again by the Xiongnu on the way back

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十三 大宛列傳
passages.textZh: 初，騫行時百餘人，去十三歲，唯二人得還。
passages.textEn: When Qian first set out he had over a hundred men; after thirteen years away, only two came back.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十三 大宛列傳
passages.textZh: 騫身所至者大宛、大月氏、大夏、康居，而傳聞其旁大國五六，具為天子言之。
passages.textEn: The places Qian reached himself were Dayuan, the Great Yuezhi, Daxia and Kangju; he had heard of five or six other great states round about, and described them all to the Son of Heaven.

summary.zh: 衛青之甥，任驃騎將軍。前121年出隴西，轉戰六日，過焉支山千餘里，大破匈奴，收休屠祭天金人；同年夏再出北地，渾邪王降漢，河西歸漢。前119年漠北之戰，深入二千餘里，封狼居胥山，禪於姑衍，登臨翰海。二十四歲卒。
summary.en: Nephew of Wei Qing and General of Swift Cavalry. In 121 BCE he struck from Longxi, fought for six days, went a thousand li beyond Mount Yanzhi, crushed the Xiongnu and seized the golden man of the Xiutu King; that summer he struck again from Beidi, the Hunye King surrendered, and the Hexi corridor came to Han. In the great northern campaign of 119 BCE he went over two thousand li deep, sacrificed on Mount Langjuxu and at Guyan and looked out over the Hanhai. He died at twenty-four.

label.en: The Hunye King surrenders; Hexi comes to Han

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十一 衛將軍驃騎列傳
passages.textZh: 驃騎將軍率戎士踰烏盭，討遬濮，涉狐奴，歷五王國，輜重人眾懾慴者弗取，冀獲單于子。轉戰六日，過焉支山千有餘里，合短兵，殺折蘭王，斬盧胡王，誅全甲，執渾邪王子及相國、都尉，首虜八千餘級，收休屠祭天金人，益封去病二千戶。
passages.textEn: "The General of Swift Cavalry led his men over the Wuli, punished the Supu, crossed the Hunu and passed through five kingdoms, sparing the cowed baggage trains and people in hope of taking the Chanyu's son. He fought for six days and went more than a thousand li beyond Mount Yanzhi; at close quarters he killed the King of Zhelan and beheaded the King of Luhu, destroyed their armoured men, captured the son of the Hunye King with his chancellor and commandants, took over eight thousand heads and prisoners and seized the golden man the Xiutu King used to worship Heaven. Qubing's fief is increased by two thousand households."

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十一 衛將軍驃騎列傳
passages.textZh: 驃騎將軍去病率師，躬將所獲葷粥之士，約輕齎，絕大幕，涉獲章渠，以誅比車耆，轉擊左大將，斬獲旗鼓，歷涉離侯。濟弓閭，獲屯頭王、韓王等三人，將軍、相國、當戶、都尉八十三人，封狼居胥山，禪於姑衍，登臨翰海。
passages.textEn: "Qubing, General of Swift Cavalry, led the army himself, with Xunyu men he had captured, carrying light supplies; he crossed the great desert, forded the Zhangqu to punish Biju'qi, turned to attack the Left General, seized his banners and drums, crossed the Lihou, forded the Gonglü, captured three kings including the Tuntou and Han kings, and eighty-three generals, chancellors, danghu and commandants; he performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Langjuxu and the shan sacrifice at Guyan, and climbed up to look over the Hanhai."

confidenceNote.zh: 生年有前145、前135二說；卒年不詳。
confidenceNote.en: He was born in 145 or 135 BCE; the year of his death is unknown.

summary.zh: 太史令。因替李陵辯護下獄受腐刑，發憤完成《史記》一百三十篇，自述「欲以究天人之際，通古今之變，成一家之言」。本圖春秋至楚漢的引文大多出自《史記》。
summary.en: Grand Historian. Castrated for defending Li Ling, he finished the Shiji in a hundred and thirty chapters, "wishing to fathom the boundary between Heaven and man, to see through the changes of past and present, and to make a school of my own". Most of this atlas's quotations from the Spring and Autumn to the war of Chu and Han come from his book.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷六十二 司馬遷傳
passages.textZh: 網羅天下放失舊聞，考之行事，稽其成敗興壞之理，凡百三十篇，亦欲以究天人之際，通古今之變，成一家之言。
passages.textEn: "I have gathered up the old traditions of the world that were scattered and lost, examined the deeds and studied the principles of success and failure, rise and ruin, in a hundred and thirty chapters, wishing to fathom the boundary between Heaven and man, to see through the changes of past and present, and to make a school of my own."

note.en: spelling in the Book of Han

summary.zh: 名嬙，漢元帝宮人。前33年匈奴呼韓邪單于入朝，元帝以之賜單于，號寧胡閼氏，生一男伊屠智牙師，為右日逐王。
summary.en: Wang Qiang, a palace lady of Emperor Yuan. When the Huhanye Chanyu came to court in 33 BCE the emperor gave her to him; she was titled Ninghu Yanzhi, "Consort who brings peace to the Hu", and bore a son, Yitu Zhiyashi, who became the Right Rizhu King.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷九十四下 匈奴傳下
passages.textZh: 竟寧元年，單于復入朝，禮賜如初，加衣服錦帛絮，皆倍於黃龍時。單于自言願婿漢氏以自親。元帝以後宮良家子王牆字昭君賜單于。
passages.textEn: In the first year of Jingning the Chanyu came to court again and was received and rewarded as before, with twice the clothes, brocade, silk and floss of the Huanglong visit. The Chanyu said he wished to become a son-in-law of the house of Han, to draw closer to it. Emperor Yuan gave the Chanyu Wang Qiang, courtesy name Zhaojun, a good-family girl of the rear palace.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷九十四下 匈奴傳下
passages.textZh: 王昭君號寧胡閼氏，生一男伊屠智牙師，為右日逐王。
passages.textEn: Wang Zhaojun was titled Ninghu Yanzhi — "Consort who brings peace to the Hu". She bore a son, Yitu Zhiyashi, who became the Right Rizhu King.

fiction.zh: 畫工毛延壽醜化其畫像的故事出自晉代《西京雜記》，不見於《漢書》。
fiction.en: The story that the painter Mao Yanshou made her portrait ugly comes from the Jin-period Xijing zaji, not from the Book of Han.

summary.zh: 元帝皇后之侄，以外戚輔政。9年「即真天子位，定有天下之號曰新」。推行改制，天下大亂；23年綠林軍攻入長安，王莽被殺。
summary.en: Nephew of Emperor Yuan's empress, he ran the government as a consort kinsman. In 9 CE he "took the throne as true Son of Heaven and fixed the name of the realm as Xin". His reforms threw the realm into chaos; in 23 the Lülin armies broke into Chang'an and he was killed.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷九十九上 王莽傳上
passages.textZh: 以戊辰直定，御王冠，即真天子位，定有天下之號曰新。其改正朔，易服色，變犧牲，殊徽幟，異器制。以十二月朔癸酉為建國元年正月之朔，以雞鳴為時。
passages.textEn: "On the day wuchen, under the sign ding, I put on the royal cap and take the throne as true Son of Heaven, and fix the name of the realm as Xin. The calendar is changed, the colours of dress altered, the sacrificial animals changed, the banners made different and the vessels of a new pattern. The first day of the twelfth month, guiyou, shall be the first day of the first month of the first year of Shijianguo, and the day shall begin at cockcrow."

summary.zh: 南陽人，漢室宗親。23年昆陽之戰，率敢死者三千人衝王尋、王邑中堅，殺王尋，莽兵大潰。後徇河北，25年即皇帝位於鄗，定都洛陽，重建漢朝，史稱東漢。
summary.en: Of Nanyang, a kinsman of the Han house. At Kunyang in 23 he charged Wang Xun and Wang Yi's centre with three thousand men ready to die, killed Wang Xun and routed Wang Mang's army. Sent north of the Yellow River, he took the throne at Hao in 25 and made Luoyang his capital, restoring the Han — the "Eastern Han".

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷一 光武帝紀上
passages.textZh: 光武乃與敢死者三千人，從城西水上衝其中堅，……尋、邑陳亂，乘銳崩之，遂殺王尋。城中亦鼓譟而出，中外合埶，震呼動天地，莽兵大潰，走者相騰踐，奔殪百餘里閒。
passages.textEn: Then Guangwu, with three thousand men ready to die, charged from the river west of the city into the enemy's centre. Wang Xun and Wang Yi's lines fell into disorder; riding the momentum, they broke them and killed Wang Xun. The garrison too came out drumming and shouting; inside and outside joined forces, their shouts shook heaven and earth, and Wang Mang's army collapsed, the fleeing men trampling one another and falling dead for more than a hundred li. [Commentary omitted.]

summary.zh: 班固之弟。73年出使西域，至鄯善，以「不入虎穴，不得虎子」激勵吏士，夜襲匈奴使者，鄯善降服。此後經營西域三十年，官至西域都護，封定遠侯，102年返回洛陽，同年卒。
summary.en: Younger brother of the historian Ban Gu. Sent to the Western Regions in 73, at Shanshan he roused his men with "If you do not enter the tiger's den you cannot take the tiger's cub", attacked the Xiongnu envoys by night, and Shanshan submitted. He spent thirty years in the Western Regions, rising to Protector-General and Marquis of Dingyuan, and returned to Luoyang in 102, dying the same year.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 班梁列傳
passages.textZh: 超曰：「不入虎穴，不得虎子。當今之計，獨有因夜以火攻虜，使彼不知我多少，必大震怖，可殄盡也。滅此虜，則鄯善破膽，功成事立矣。」
passages.textEn: Chao said: "If you do not enter the tiger's den you cannot take the tiger's cub. The only plan now is to attack the barbarians with fire by night, so they cannot tell how many we are; they will be thrown into terror and we can destroy them all. Once they are wiped out, Shanshan's nerve will break, and our task will be done."

summary.zh: 南陽西鄂人，東漢科學家、文學家，任太史令。132年造候風地動儀，以精銅鑄成，直徑八尺，形似酒尊，外有八龍銜丸、下有蟾蜍承之。
summary.en: Of Xi'e in Nanyang, scientist and writer of Eastern Han, Grand Astrologer. In 132 he built his instrument for the movements of the earth: cast in bronze, eight chi across, shaped like a wine jar, with eight dragons holding balls above eight open-mouthed toads.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷五十九 張衡列傳
passages.textZh: 陽嘉元年，復造候風地動儀。以精銅鑄成，員徑八尺，合蓋隆起，形似酒尊，飾以篆文山龜鳥獸之形。中有都柱，傍行八道，施關發機。外有八龍，首銜銅丸，下有蟾蜍，張口承之。其牙機巧制，皆隱在尊中，覆蓋周密無際。如有地動，尊則振龍機發吐丸，而蟾蜍銜之。振聲激揚，伺者因此覺知。雖一龍發機，而七首不動，尋其方面，乃知震之所在。驗之以事，合契若神。
passages.textEn: In the first year of Yangjia he also made an instrument for observing the winds and the movements of the earth. It was cast in fine bronze, eight chi across, with a domed lid, shaped like a wine jar and decorated with seal characters and figures of mountains, tortoises, birds and beasts. Inside was a central pillar, with eight channels running out from it and a trigger mechanism. Outside were eight dragons holding bronze balls in their mouths, and below them toads with open mouths to catch them. The cunning mechanism was all hidden inside the jar, closely covered without a gap. When the earth moved, the jar shook a dragon's trigger and it let fall its ball, which the toad caught. The ringing sound alerted the watchers. Though one dragon's mechanism was set off, the other seven heads did not move; from its direction one knew where the earthquake was. Tested against events, it matched them as if by magic.

summary.zh: 唐高祖次子。626年六月四日在玄武門誅殺太子建成、齊王元吉，旋立為皇太子，同年即位，是為唐太宗。630年李靖大破突厥於陰山，頡利可汗遠遁。641年以文成公主嫁吐蕃贊普弄贊。
summary.en: Second son of Tang Gaozu. On the fourth day of the sixth month of 626 he killed the Crown Prince Jiancheng and Yuanji, Prince of Qi, at the Xuanwu Gate; he was made Crown Prince and took the throne the same year as Emperor Taizong. In 630 Li Jing crushed the Turks in the Yin Mountains and Illig Qaghan fled. In 641 he gave Princess Wencheng in marriage to the Tibetan Tsenpo Nongzan.

label.en: Rises with his father at Jinyang

label.zh: 親征高句麗，圍安市城不下
label.en: Leads the campaign against Goguryeo; fails at Anshi

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷二 太宗本紀上
passages.textZh: 九年，皇太子建成、齊王元吉謀害太宗。六月四日，太宗率長孫無忌、尉遲敬德、房玄齡、杜如晦、宇文士及、高士廉、侯君集、程知節、秦叔寶、段志玄、屈突通、張士貴等於玄武門誅之。甲子，立為皇太子，庶政皆斷決。
passages.textEn: In the ninth year the Crown Prince Jiancheng and Yuanji, Prince of Qi, plotted against Taizong. On the fourth day of the sixth month Taizong, with Zhangsun Wuji, Yuchi Jingde, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Yuwen Shiji, Gao Shilian, Hou Junji, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, Duan Zhixuan, Qutu Tong, Zhang Shigui and others, killed them at the Xuanwu Gate. On jiazi he was made Crown Prince, and all affairs of government were decided by him.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷三 太宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 甲辰，李靖又破突厥於陰山，頡利可汗輕騎遠遁。
passages.textEn: On jiachen Li Jing beat the Turks again in the Yin Mountains, and Illig Qaghan fled far away with a few light horsemen.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十六上 吐蕃傳上
passages.textZh: 貞觀十五年，太宗以文成公主妻之，令禮部尚書、江夏郡王道宗主婚，持節送公主於吐蕃。弄贊率其部兵次柏海，親迎於河源。見道宗，執子婿之禮甚恭。既而嘆大國服飾禮儀之美，俯仰有愧沮之色。
passages.textEn: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan Taizong gave him Princess Wencheng in marriage, and had Daozong, Minister of Rites and Prince of Jiangxia, preside over the wedding and escort the princess to Tubo with the imperial tally. Nongzan [Songtsen Gampo] led his troops to camp at Lake Bo and came himself to meet her at the source of the Yellow River. Meeting Daozong he behaved most respectfully, as a son-in-law should. Then, admiring the beauty of the great country's dress and ceremony, he looked abashed.

confidenceNote.zh: 出發年份有貞觀元年（627）、三年（629）二說，《舊唐書》只作「貞觀初」；路線依《大唐西域記》，年份為約數。
confidenceNote.en: He left in 627 or 629 — the Old Book of Tang only says "early in Zhenguan"; the route follows his Record of the Western Regions and the years are approximate.

summary.zh: 俗姓陳，洛州偃師人。嫌當時佛經譯本多有訛謬，貞觀初隨商人往遊西域，遍求原本。「在西域十七年，經百余國，悉解其國之語」，歸國後撰《西域記》十二卷，並主持譯經。
summary.en: Born Chen, of Yanshi in Luo prefecture. Finding the Buddhist translations full of errors, early in Zhenguan he travelled west with merchants to look for the originals. "He was in the west seventeen years and passed through more than a hundred countries, learning all their languages"; back home he wrote the Record of the Western Regions in twelve chapters and directed the translation of the sutras.

label.en: Guazhou; slips past the Yumen Pass
Gaochang; welcomed by King Qu Wentai

label.zh: 素葉城，見西突厥葉護可汗
label.en: Suyab; meets the Western Turkic qaghan

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十一 方伎傳 玄奘
passages.textZh: 僧玄奘，姓陳氏，洛州偃師人。大業末出家，博涉經論。嘗謂翻譯者多有訛謬，故就西域，廣求異本以參驗之。貞觀初，隨商人往游西域。玄奘既辯博出群，所在必為講釋論難，蕃人遠近咸尊伏之。在西域十七年，經百余國，悉解其國之語，仍采其山川謠俗，土地所有，撰《西域記》十二卷。
passages.textEn: The monk Xuanzang, surname Chen, was from Yanshi in Luo prefecture. He left home at the end of the Daye era and read widely in the sutras and treatises. Believing the translations full of errors, he went to the Western Regions to search for other texts to compare them with. Early in Zhenguan he travelled west with merchants. His learning and eloquence were outstanding; wherever he went he lectured and debated, and foreigners near and far revered him. He was in the west seventeen years and passed through more than a hundred countries, learning all their languages; he also gathered their landscapes, customs and products, and wrote the Record of the Western Regions in twelve chapters.

summary.zh: 唐宗室女。641年太宗以之嫁吐蕃贊普弄贊（松贊干布），由江夏郡王李道宗主婚、持節護送；弄贊率部兵至柏海，親迎於河源。680年卒於吐蕃。
summary.en: A woman of the Tang imperial clan. In 641 Taizong gave her in marriage to the Tibetan Tsenpo Nongzan (Songtsen Gampo); Li Daozong, Prince of Jiangxia, presided and escorted her, and Nongzan led his troops to Lake Bo to meet her at the source of the Yellow River. She died in Tibet in 680.

label.en: Met by Nongzan at Lake Bo

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十六上 吐蕃傳上
passages.textZh: 貞觀十五年，太宗以文成公主妻之，令禮部尚書、江夏郡王道宗主婚，持節送公主於吐蕃。弄贊率其部兵次柏海，親迎於河源。見道宗，執子婿之禮甚恭。既而嘆大國服飾禮儀之美，俯仰有愧沮之色。
passages.textEn: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan Taizong gave him Princess Wencheng in marriage, and had Daozong, Minister of Rites and Prince of Jiangxia, preside over the wedding and escort the princess to Tubo with the imperial tally. Nongzan [Songtsen Gampo] led his troops to camp at Lake Bo and came himself to meet her at the source of the Yellow River. Meeting Daozong he behaved most respectfully, as a son-in-law should. Then, admiring the beauty of the great country's dress and ceremony, he looked abashed.

summary.zh: 唐高宗皇后。高宗死後臨朝稱制，690年九月九日「革唐命，改國號為周」，改元天授，加尊號聖神皇帝，以洛陽為神都。705年神龍政變後退位，唐室復辟，同年卒。中國歷史上唯一正式稱帝的女性。
summary.en: Empress of Tang Gaozong. After his death she ruled as regent, and on the ninth day of the ninth month of 690 "ended the mandate of Tang and changed the name of the state to Zhou", proclaiming the Tianshou era and taking the title Sage and Divine Emperor, with Luoyang as her Divine Capital. Forced to step down in the coup of 705, when Tang was restored, she died the same year — the only woman in Chinese history to rule as emperor in her own name.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷六 則天皇后本紀
passages.textZh: 九月九日壬午，革唐命，改國號為周。改元為天授，大赦天下，賜酺七日。乙酉，加尊號曰聖神皇帝，降皇帝為皇嗣。丙戌，初立武氏七廟於神都。
passages.textEn: On the ninth day of the ninth month, renwu, she ended the mandate of Tang and changed the name of the state to Zhou. The era was changed to Tianshou, there was a general amnesty and seven days of feasting. On yiyou she took the title Sage and Divine Emperor and reduced the emperor to Imperial Heir. On bingxu the seven ancestral temples of the Wu family were first set up in the Divine Capital.

confidenceNote.zh: 生年有703年等說。
confidenceNote.en: Year of birth uncertain (703 is usual).

summary.zh: 營州柳城胡人，兼任平盧、范陽、河東三鎮節度使。755年十一月率蕃、漢之兵十餘萬自幽州南下，以誅楊國忠為名起兵，十二月陷洛陽，756年在洛陽稱大燕皇帝，同年六月破潼關，玄宗奔蜀。757年為其子安慶緒所殺。
summary.en: A man of mixed Sogdian and Turkic descent from Liucheng in Yingzhou, Military Governor of Pinglu, Fanyang and Hedong at once. In the eleventh month of 755 he marched south from Youzhou with over a hundred thousand foreign and Han troops in the name of punishing Yang Guozhong, took Luoyang in the twelfth month, declared himself Emperor of Great Yan there in 756, broke through Tong Pass in the sixth month and sent Xuanzong fleeing to Shu. His son An Qingxu killed him in 757.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷九 玄宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 丙寅，范陽節度使安祿山率蕃、漢之兵十餘萬，自幽州南向詣闕，以誅楊國忠為名，先殺太原尹楊光翽於博陵郡。
passages.textEn: On bingyin An Lushan, Military Governor of Fanyang, led more than a hundred thousand foreign and Han troops south from Youzhou towards the capital, in the name of punishing Yang Guozhong, first killing Yang Guanghui, Intendant of Taiyuan, at Boling.

summary.zh: 名李隆基。開元年間國勢鼎盛。756年潼關失守，六月乙未凌晨出延秋門奔蜀；至馬嵬驛，諸衛頓軍不進，陳玄禮奏請誅楊國忠，楊貴妃亦被賜死。至成都。太子在靈武即位，尊其為太上皇；757年還長安，762年卒。
summary.en: Li Longji, under whose Kaiyuan era Tang reached its height. When Tong Pass fell in 756 he left by the Yanqiu Gate at dawn on yiwei of the sixth month and fled towards Shu; at the Mawei station the guards halted and Chen Xuanli demanded Yang Guozhong's death, and Consort Yang was made to die too. He reached Chengdu. The Crown Prince took the throne at Lingwu and made him Retired Emperor; he returned to Chang'an in 757 and died in 762.

label.en: Leaves Chang'an by the Yanqiu Gate

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷九 玄宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 辛卯，哥舒翰至潼關，為其帳下火拔歸仁以左右數十騎執之降賊，關門不守，京師大駭，河東、華陰、上洛等郡皆委城而走。甲午，將謀幸蜀，乃下詔親征，仗下，從士庶恐駭，奔走於路。乙未，凌晨自延秋門出，微雨沾濕，扈從惟宰相楊國忠、韋見素、內侍高力士及太子，親王，妃主、皇孫已下多從之不及。
