passages.textEn: On xinmao Geshu Han reached Tong Pass, where his own officer Huoba Guiren with a few dozen horsemen seized him and went over to the rebels; the pass was lost, the capital was in panic, and Hedong, Huayin, Shangluo and other commanderies abandoned their cities. On jiawu, planning to go to Shu, the emperor issued an edict for a personal campaign; when the court dispersed, officials and commoners fled in terror along the roads. On yiwei at dawn he left by the Yanqiu Gate in a light rain, attended only by the chief ministers Yang Guozhong and Wei Jiansu, the eunuch Gao Lishi and the Crown Prince; most of the princes, consorts, princesses and grandsons could not follow in time.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷九 玄宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 丙辰，次馬嵬驛，諸衛頓軍不進。龍武大將軍陳玄禮奏曰：「逆胡指闕，以誅國忠為名，然中外群情，不無嫌怨。今國步艱阻，乘輿震蕩，陛下宜徇群情，為社稷大計，國忠之徒，可置之於法。」
passages.textEn: On bingchen they stopped at the Mawei post station, and the guards halted and would go no further. Chen Xuanli, General of the Dragon-Martial Army, memorialised: "The rebel barbarian marches on the palace in the name of punishing Guozhong, yet at court and in the realm there is no little resentment of him. Now that the state is in peril and Your Majesty's carriage is shaken, Your Majesty should follow the feeling of the men and, for the sake of the dynasty, let Guozhong and his faction be dealt with by the law."

summary.zh: 曹州冤句人，鹽商出身。875年起響應王仙芝起事，轉戰南北，879年攻陷廣州，880年十一月陷洛陽，十二月入長安，僖宗奔蜀；黃巢在長安稱帝，國號大齊。883年被逐出長安，884年敗死於泰山狼虎谷。
summary.en: Of Yuanju in Caozhou, a salt trader. He joined Wang Xianzhi's rising in 875 and fought his way across the country, took Guangzhou in 879, Luoyang in the eleventh month of 880 and Chang'an in the twelfth, when Xizong fled to Shu; in Chang'an he declared himself emperor of Great Qi. Driven from Chang'an in 883, he was defeated and died in the Langhu valley near Mount Tai in 884.

label.en: Enters Chang'an; emperor of Great Qi

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷二百下 黃巢傳
passages.textZh: 十二月三日，僖宗夜自開遠門出，趨駱谷，諸王官屬相次奔命。觀軍容使田令孜、王若儔收合禁軍扈從。四日，賊至昭應，金吾大將軍張直方率在京兩班迎賊灞上。五日，賊陷京師。
passages.textEn: On the third day of the twelfth month Xizong left at night by the Kaiyuan Gate and made for the Luo valley; the princes and officials fled after him one by one. The army supervisor Tian Lingzi and Wang Ruochou gathered the palace troops to escort him. On the fourth the rebels reached Zhaoying, and Zhang Zhifang, General of the Golden Guard, led the officials who remained in the capital to welcome them at Bashang. On the fifth the rebels took the capital.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷二百下 黃巢傳
passages.textZh: 既入春明門，坊市聚觀，尚讓慰曉市人曰：「黃王為生靈，不似李家不恤汝輩，但各安家。」
passages.textEn: When they had come in through the Chunming Gate and the people of the wards and markets crowded to watch, Shang Rang reassured them: "King Huang has risen for the people's sake; he is not like the house of Li, which cared nothing for you. Just stay quietly at home."

names.name: Zhu Wen (Emperor Taizu of Later Liang)

summary.zh: 宋州碭山人。初從黃巢，任諸衛大將軍；882年降唐，賜名全忠，任宣武軍節度使，據汴州。904年逼遷昭宗至洛陽並弒之，907年受唐哀帝禪，即皇帝位，國號梁。912年為其子朱友珪所殺。
summary.en: Of Dangshan in Songzhou. He served Huang Chao as a general of the guards, went over to Tang in 882, was given the name Quanzhong and made Military Governor of Xuanwu at Bianzhou. In 904 he forced Emperor Zhaozong to move to Luoyang and had him killed; in 907 he took the abdication of the last Tang emperor and the throne of Liang. His son Zhu Yougui killed him in 912.

label.en: Goes over to Tang at Tongzhou

passages.sourceEn: Old History of the Five Dynasties (Xue Juzheng et al., 974)
passages.locator: 卷三 梁書 太祖紀三
passages.textZh: 甲子，張文蔚、楊涉乘輅自上源驛至，從冊寶諸司各備儀衛鹵簿前導，百官從其後，至金祥殿前陳之。王被袞冕，即皇帝位。
passages.textEn: On jiazi Zhang Wenwei and Yang She arrived from the Shangyuan post station in state carriages, the offices carrying the patents and seals leading with their guards and insignia and the officials following, and set them out before the Jinxiang Hall. The prince put on the imperial robes and crown and took the throne.

summary.zh: 契丹迭剌部人。907年燔柴告天，即皇帝位；916年群臣上尊號，建元神冊。926年滅渤海國，同年卒於扶餘城。
summary.en: Of the Khitan Yila tribe. In 907 he burned offerings to Heaven and took the imperial throne; in 916 the ministers gave him an imperial title and the Shence era was proclaimed. He destroyed the kingdom of Balhae in 926 and died the same year at Fuyu.

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖本紀上
passages.textZh: 元年春正月庚寅，命有司設壇于如迂王集會堝，燔柴告天，即皇帝位。
passages.textEn: In the first month of the first year, on gengyin, he had an altar built at the Ruyu royal assembly ground, burned offerings to Heaven and took the imperial throne.

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖本紀上
passages.textZh: 丙申，群臣及諸屬國築壇州東，上尊號曰大聖大明天皇帝，后曰應天大明地皇后。大赦，建元神冊
passages.textEn: On bingshen the ministers and the subject states built an altar east of the city and gave him the title Great Sage, Great Bright Heavenly Emperor, and the empress the title Earthly Empress. There was an amnesty and the era Shence was proclaimed.

names.name: Shi Jingtang (Emperor Gaozu of Later Jin)

summary.zh: 後唐河東節度使。936年借契丹兵起事，滅後唐，受契丹冊立為帝，國號晉（後晉），對契丹稱臣、稱兒。938年遣使以幽、薊等十六州並圖籍獻契丹。
summary.en: Military Governor of Hedong under the Later Tang. In 936 he rose with Khitan help, destroyed the Later Tang and was enthroned by the Khitan as emperor of Jin (the Later Jin), calling himself their subject and son. In 938 he sent the sixteen prefectures, including You and Ji, with their maps and registers to the Khitan.

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷四 太宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 是月，晉復遣趙瑩奉表來賀，以幽、薊、瀛、莫、涿、檀、順、媯、儒、新、武、雲、應、朔、寰、蔚十六州並圖籍來獻。於是詔以皇都為上京，府曰臨潢。升幽州為南京，南京為東京。
passages.textEn: That month Jin again sent Zhao Ying with a memorial of congratulation, presenting the sixteen prefectures of You, Ji, Ying, Mo, Zhuo, Tan, Shun, Gui, Ru, Xin, Wu, Yun, Ying, Shuo, Huan and Yu, with their maps and registers. An edict then made the imperial capital the Upper Capital, with the prefecture called Linhuang; Youzhou was raised to the Southern Capital, and the old Southern Capital became the Eastern Capital.

summary.zh: 後周殿前都點檢。960年正月出兵禦契丹，至陳橋驛，諸軍擁立，「有以黃衣加太祖身」，回師開封受禪，國號宋。次年召石守信等飲宴，勸其「多積金、市田宅以遺子孫」，諸將次日稱病解兵權。此後削平荊南、湖南、後蜀、南漢、南唐。
summary.en: Commander of the Palace Army of Later Zhou. Marching against the Khitan in the first month of 960, at the Chenqiao post station he was proclaimed by his troops — "someone put a yellow garment on him" — and went back to Kaifeng to take the abdication, naming his state Song. The next year he feasted Shi Shouxin and other generals and urged them to "pile up gold and buy fields and houses to leave to your sons"; the next day they pleaded illness and gave up their commands. He went on to conquer Jingnan, Hunan, Later Shu, Southern Han and Southern Tang.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖本紀一
passages.textZh: 夜五鼓，軍士集驛門，宣言策點檢為天子，或止之，眾不聽。遲明，逼寢所，太宗入白，太祖起。諸校露刃列於庭，曰：「諸軍無主，願策太尉為天子。」未及對，有以黃衣加太祖身，眾皆羅拜，呼萬歲，即掖太祖乘馬。
passages.textEn: At the fifth watch of the night the soldiers gathered at the gate of the post station and declared that they would make the Commander of the Palace Army emperor; some tried to stop them, but the crowd would not listen. At dawn they pressed into his bedchamber; Taizong went in to tell him, and Taizu rose. The officers stood in the courtyard with drawn swords and said: "The armies have no lord. We wish to make the Grand Commandant emperor." Before he could answer, someone put a yellow garment on him; they all bowed around him and cried "Ten thousand years!", and helped him onto his horse.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二百五十 石守信傳
passages.textZh: 乾德初，帝因晚朝與守信等飲酒，酒酣，帝曰：「我非爾曹不及此，然吾為天子，殊不若為節度使之樂，吾終夕未嘗安枕而臥。」守信等頓首曰：「今天命已定，誰復敢有異心，陛下何為出此言耶？」帝曰：「人孰不欲富貴，一旦有以黃袍加汝之身，雖欲不為，其可得乎？」守信等謝曰：「臣愚不及此，惟陛下哀矜之。」帝曰：「人生駒過隙爾，不如多積金、市田宅以遺子孫，歌兒舞女以終天年。君臣之間無所猜嫌，不亦善乎？」守信謝曰：「陛下念及此，所謂生死而肉骨也。」明日，皆稱病，乞解兵權，帝從之
passages.textEn: Early in Qiande, after the evening audience, the emperor was drinking with Shixin and the others. When the wine was flowing he said: "Without you I would not be here. But being emperor is not nearly as pleasant as being a military governor — I have not slept easy a single night." Shixin and the others bowed their heads: "Heaven's mandate is settled now — who would dare to think otherwise? Why does Your Majesty say this?" The emperor said: "Who does not want wealth and honour? If one day someone puts the yellow robe on you, then even if you do not want it, how could you refuse?" Shixin and the others bowed: "We are too dull to have thought of this. We beg Your Majesty's pity." The emperor said: "Life passes like a colt glimpsed through a crack. Better to pile up gold and buy fields and houses to leave to your sons and grandsons, and live out your years with singing boys and dancing girls. With no suspicion between lord and subject — would that not be good?" Shixin bowed: "That Your Majesty thinks of this is to raise the dead and put flesh on bones." The next day they all pleaded illness and asked to give up their commands, and the emperor agreed.

summary.zh: 撫州臨川人。宋神宗熙寧二年（1069）任參知政事，設制置三司條例司，推行農田水利、青苗、均輸、保甲、免役、市易、保馬、方田等法，「號為新法」。青苗法以常平糴本作青苗錢貸與民戶，取息二分，春散秋斂。新法引起激烈爭議，安石兩度罷相，晚年退居江寧。
summary.en: Of Linchuan in Fuzhou. Made Assisting Councillor by Emperor Shenzong in 1069, he set up a commission for fiscal planning and launched the measures for farmland and water works, green-sprout loans, equitable transport, mutual security, hired service, state trade, horse-rearing and land survey — "called the New Laws". The green-sprout law lent the price-stabilisation funds to households at two-tenths interest, paid out in spring and collected in autumn. The New Laws were bitterly fought over; he was twice dismissed and spent his last years at Jiangning.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百二十七 王安石傳
passages.textZh: 而農田水利、青苗、均輸、保甲、免役、市易、保馬、方田諸役相繼並興，號為新法，遣提舉官四十餘輩，頒行天下。青苗法者，以常平糴本作青苗錢，散與人戶，令出息二分，春散秋斂。
passages.textEn: Then the measures for farmland and water works, green-sprout loans, equitable transport, mutual security, hired service, state trade, horse-rearing and land survey were launched one after another, called the New Laws, and more than forty commissioners were sent out to put them into force across the realm. The green-sprout law took the price-stabilisation funds as "green-sprout money" and lent it to households at two-tenths interest, paid out in spring and collected in autumn.

summary.zh: 眉州眉山人。1079年御史摭其表語與詩作指為訕謗，逮赴御史臺獄（烏臺詩案）；神宗憐之，以黃州團練副使安置。在黃州「築室於東坡，自號東坡居士」。後屢遭貶謫，遠至惠州、儋州，1101年北歸途中卒於常州。
summary.en: Of Meishan in Meizhou. In 1079 censors twisted phrases from his memorial and his poems into slander and had him thrown into the Censorate prison (the "Crow Terrace poetry case"); Shenzong pitied him and sent him to Huangzhou as a Deputy Militia Commissioner under supervision. There he "built a house on the eastern slope and called himself the Retired Scholar of the Eastern Slope". Exiled again and again, as far as Huizhou and Danzhou on Hainan, he died at Changzhou on his way north in 1101.

label.en: Crow Terrace case; in the Censorate prison

label.zh: 黃州安置，自號東坡居士

label.en: Dies at Changzhou on his way north

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百三十八 蘇軾傳
passages.textZh: 徙知湖州，上表以謝。又以事不便民者不敢言，以詩託諷，庶有補於國。御史李定、舒亶、何正臣摭其表語，並媒蘖所爲詩以爲訕謗，逮赴臺獄，欲置之死，鍛煉久之不決。神宗獨憐之，以黃州團練副使安置。軾與田父野老，相從溪山間，築室於東坡，自號「東坡居士」。
passages.textEn: Moved to Huzhou, he sent up a memorial of thanks. Since he dared not speak openly of the things that harmed the people, he hinted at them in poems, hoping to help the state. The censors Li Ding, Shu Dan and He Zhengchen picked out phrases from his memorial and twisted his poems into slander; he was arrested and taken to the Censorate prison, and they wanted him put to death, but the case dragged on undecided. Shenzong alone pitied him and had him sent to Huangzhou as Deputy Militia Commissioner under supervision. There Shi went about the streams and hills with old farmers, built a house on the eastern slope and called himself "the Retired Scholar of the Eastern Slope" — Dongpo.

summary.zh: 女真完顏部首領。1114年起兵反遼，1115年正月即皇帝位，以金「不變不壞」，國號大金，改元收國，隨即親攻黃龍府。1120年攻破遼上京，1122年取燕京。1123年卒。
summary.en: Chief of the Jurchen Wanyan clan. He rose against Liao in 1114 and took the throne in the first month of 1115, naming his state Great Jin — gold "does not change or decay" — and the era Shouguo, then marched in person on Huanglong. He took the Liao Upper Capital in 1120 and Yanjing in 1122, and died in 1123.

passages.sourceEn: History of Jin (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷二 太祖本紀
passages.textZh: 收國元年正月壬申朔，群臣奉上尊號。是日，即皇帝位。上曰：「遼以賓鐵爲號，取其堅也。賓鐵雖堅，終亦變壞，惟金不變不壞。金之色白，完顏部色尚白。」于是國號大金，改元收國。丙子，上自將攻黃龍府，進臨益州。
passages.textEn: In the first year of Shouguo, on renshen, the first day of the first month, the ministers presented him with an imperial title, and that day he took the throne. He said: "Liao took its name from fine iron, for its hardness. But hard as fine iron is, in the end it changes and decays; only gold does not change or decay. The colour of gold is white, and the Wanyan tribe honours white." So the state was named Great Jin [Gold], and the era Shouguo. On bingzi the emperor marched in person against Huanglong and advanced to Yizhou.

confidenceNote.zh: 卒於紹興十一年十二月，公曆已入1142年1月。
confidenceNote.en: He died in the twelfth month of the eleventh year of Shaoxing, which falls in January 1142.

summary.zh: 相州湯陰人，南宋抗金將領。1134年收復襄陽六郡。1140年北伐，諸將分道出戰、相繼報捷，岳飛自以輕騎駐郾城，大破兀朮；曾對部下說「直抵黃龍府，與諸君痛飲爾」。不久宋廷命其班師。1141年被秦檜等誣以謀反下獄，十二月被殺；韓世忠詰問，秦檜答以「其事體莫須有」。
summary.en: Of Tangyin in Xiangzhou, a Southern Song general against the Jin. He recovered the six commanderies around Xiangyang in 1134. In his northern campaign of 1140 his generals reported victory after victory, while he held Yancheng with light cavalry and beat Wuzhu; he told his officers, "We will drive straight to Huanglong and drink deep there together." The court soon ordered him back. In 1141 Qin Hui and others framed him for treason and he was put to death in the twelfth month; when Han Shizhong demanded the facts, Qin Hui answered "mo xu you".

label.en: Recovers Xiangyang and five other commanderies

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百六十五 岳飛傳
passages.textZh: 未幾，所遣諸將相繼奏捷。大軍在潁昌，諸將分道出戰，飛自以輕騎駐郾城，兵勢甚銳。兀朮大懼，會龍虎大王議，以為諸帥易與，獨飛不可當，欲誘致其師，併力一戰。
passages.textEn: Before long the generals he had sent out reported victory one after another. The main army was at Yingchang and the generals went out by separate roads; Fei himself held Yancheng with light cavalry, in high fighting spirit. Wuzhu was greatly alarmed and conferred with the Longhu Prince: the other commanders were easy to deal with, but Fei could not be withstood, so they would lure his army out and fight it with all their strength together.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百六十五 岳飛傳
passages.textZh: 飛大喜，語其下曰：「直抵黃龍府，與諸君痛飲爾！」
passages.textEn: Fei was delighted and said to his officers: "We will drive straight to Huanglong and drink deep there together!"

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百六十五 岳飛傳
passages.textZh: 初命何鑄鞠之，飛裂裳以背示鑄，有「盡忠報國」四大字，深入膚理。既而閱實無左驗，鑄明其無辜。改命万俟禼。
passages.textEn: He Zhu was first ordered to try him. Fei tore open his clothes and showed He Zhu his back, which bore four large characters, "Serve the country with utmost loyalty", cut deep into the skin. When the evidence was examined and nothing supported the charge, He Zhu declared him innocent. Moqi Xie was appointed in his place.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百六十五 岳飛傳
passages.textZh: 獄之將上也，韓世忠不平，詣檜詰其實，檜曰：「飛子雲與張憲書雖不明，其事體莫須有。」世忠曰：「『莫須有』三字，何以服天下？」
passages.textEn: When the case was about to be submitted, Han Shizhong, indignant, went to Qin Hui and demanded the facts. Hui said: "Though the letter from Fei's son Yun to Zhang Xian is unclear, the matter is mo xu you — it need not be that it did not happen." Shizhong said: "Mo xu you — how can those three words satisfy the realm?"

fiction.zh: 岳母刺字的故事出自明清小說（如《說岳全傳》）；《宋史》只記他在獄中裂裳示背，背上有「盡忠報國」四大字。朱仙鎮大捷僅見於其孫岳珂所編的家傳，今人多存疑。
fiction.en: The story of his mother tattooing him comes from Ming and Qing fiction (such as Shuo Yue quanzhuan); the History of Song says only that in prison he bared his back, which bore the words "serve the country with utmost loyalty". The great victory at Zhuxian town is known only from the family biography compiled by his grandson Yue Ke, and many historians doubt it.

confidenceNote.en: He was born in 1155, 1162 or 1167; all are argued.

summary.zh: 名鐵木真。統一蒙古高原諸部後，1206年在斡難河源大會諸王群臣，建九游白旗，即皇帝位，號成吉思皇帝。此後伐西夏、攻金，1219年西征花剌子模，1227年征西夏途中卒。
summary.en: Temüjin. Having united the tribes of the Mongolian plateau, in 1206 he held a great assembly of the princes and ministers at the source of the Onon, raised the white banner with nine tails and took the throne as Chinggis Emperor. He then attacked Xi Xia and Jin, marched west against Khwarazm in 1219, and died on campaign against Xi Xia in 1227.

label.en: Takes the throne at the source of the Onon
Dies on campaign against Xi Xia

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖本紀
passages.textZh: 元年丙寅，帝大會諸王羣臣，建九游白旗，即皇帝位於斡難河之源。諸王羣臣共上尊號曰成吉思皇帝。是歲實金泰和之六年也。
passages.textEn: In the first year, bingyin, the emperor held a great assembly of the princes and ministers, raised the white banner with nine tails, and took the throne at the source of the Onon River. The princes and ministers together gave him the title Chinggis Emperor. That year was in fact the sixth year of Taihe of the Jin.

summary.zh: 成吉思汗之孫，1251年即大汗位。1258年親征四川，1259年攻合州釣魚城不下，六月不豫，七月崩於釣魚山。
summary.en: Grandson of Chinggis, Great Khan from 1251. He led the invasion of Sichuan himself in 1258, failed to take the Diaoyu fortress at Hezhou in 1259, fell ill in the sixth month and died at Diaoyu Mountain in the seventh.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷三 憲宗本紀
passages.textZh: 六月丁巳，汪田哥復選兵夜登外城馬軍寨，殺寨主及守城者。王堅率兵來戰。遲明，遇雨，梯折，後軍不克進而止。是月，帝不豫。秋七月辛亥，留精兵三千守之，餘悉攻重慶。癸亥，帝崩于釣魚山，壽五十有二，在位九年。
passages.textEn: On dingsi of the sixth month Wang Tiange again picked men to climb by night into the cavalry stockade of the outer wall, killing its commander and defenders. Wang Jian led his troops out to fight. At dawn it rained, the ladders broke, and the troops behind could not go on, so the attack stopped. That month the emperor fell ill. On xinhai of the seventh month he left three thousand picked men to hold the siege and sent the rest to attack Chongqing. On guihai the emperor died at Diaoyu Mountain, aged fifty-two, in the ninth year of his reign.

summary.zh: 成吉思汗之孫。1260年在開平即汗位，1271年建國號大元，1272年以中都為大都。1273年元軍攻破樊城，呂文煥以襄陽降；1276年取臨安，1279年崖山之戰後南宋亡。
summary.en: Grandson of Chinggis. He took the khanate at Kaiping in 1260, proclaimed the dynastic name Great Yuan in 1271 and made Zhongdu his capital, Dadu, in 1272. His armies took Fancheng in 1273 and Lü Wenhuan surrendered Xiangyang; Lin'an fell in 1276, and after Yashan in 1279 the Southern Song was gone.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷八 世祖本紀五
passages.textZh: 癸亥，阿里海牙等大攻樊城，拔之，守將呂文煥懼而請降
passages.textEn: On guihai Ariq Qaya and others launched a great assault on Fancheng and took it; the commander Lü Wenhuan, afraid, asked to surrender.

confidenceNote.zh: 就義於至元十九年十二月，公曆已入1283年1月。
confidenceNote.en: He was executed in the twelfth month of the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan, which falls in January 1283.

summary.zh: 吉州廬陵人，1256年狀元。元兵南下時起兵勤王，任右丞相。1278年在五坡嶺兵敗被俘。元將張弘範要他寫信招降張世傑，他書所過《零丁洋詩》與之，末云「人生自古誰無死，留取丹心照汗青」。崖山破後被押往大都，囚禁三年不屈，就義於大都。
summary.en: Of Luling in Jizhou, top graduate of 1256. When the Yuan armies came south he raised troops for the throne and became Chancellor of the Right. Defeated and captured at Wupoling in 1278, he was asked by the Yuan general Zhang Hongfan to write to Zhang Shijie urging surrender; instead he wrote out his poem "Crossing the Lingding Sea", which ends "Since ancient times who has not died? Let me leave a loyal heart to shine in the annals." After Yashan he was taken to Dadu, held for three years without yielding, and executed there.

label.en: Sent to the Yuan camp and detained
Crosses the Lingding Sea; the poem

label.zh: 在元軍中目睹崖山之戰
label.en: Witnesses Yashan from the Yuan fleet

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百一十八 文天祥傳
passages.textZh: 天祥至潮陽，見弘範，左右命之拜，不拜，弘範遂以客禮見之，與俱入厓山，使為書招張世傑。天祥曰：「吾不能捍父母，乃教人叛父母，可乎？」索之固，乃書所過《零丁洋詩》與之。其末有云：「人生自古誰無死，留取丹心照汗青。」弘範笑而置之。
passages.textEn: When Tianxiang reached Chaoyang and was brought before Zhang Hongfan, the attendants ordered him to bow; he would not, and Hongfan received him as a guest. Hongfan took him to Yashan and wanted him to write a letter calling on Zhang Shijie to surrender. Tianxiang said: "I could not defend my own parents — shall I now teach others to betray theirs?" Pressed hard, he wrote out the poem he had made crossing the Lingding Sea and gave it to him. It ends: "Since ancient times who has not died? Let me leave a loyal heart to shine in the annals." Hongfan laughed and put it aside.

summary.zh: 字君實，楚州鹽城人。南宋末擁立益王趙昰、衛王趙昺，任左丞相。1279年崖山兵敗，見衛王舟大且被諸舟環結，無法突圍，遂負昺投海。
summary.en: Courtesy name Junshi, of Yancheng in Chuzhou. At the end of Southern Song he helped set up the boy princes Zhao Shi and Zhao Bing and became Chancellor of the Left. When Yashan fell in 1279 and the Prince of Wei's ship, large and lashed to the others, could not get away, he leapt into the sea with the boy emperor on his back.

label.en: Leaps into the sea with the boy emperor

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百五十一 忠義傳 陸秀夫
passages.textZh: 陸秀夫，字君實，楚州鹽城人。生三歲，其父徙家鎮江。
passages.textEn: Lu Xiufei, courtesy name Junshi, was from Yancheng in Chuzhou. When he was three his father moved the family to Zhenjiang.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 瀛國公本紀 二王附
passages.textZh: 諸軍潰，翟國秀及團練使劉俊等解甲降。大軍至中軍，會暮，且風雨，昏霧四塞，咫尺不相辨。世傑乃與蘇劉義斷維，以十餘舟奪港而去，陸秀夫走衛王舟，王舟大，且諸舟環結，度不得出走，乃負昺投海中，後宮及諸臣多從死者，七日，浮屍出於海十餘萬人。楊太后聞昺死，撫膺大慟曰：「我忍死艱關至此者，正爲趙氏一塊肉爾，今無望矣！」遂赴海死，世傑葬之海濱，已而世傑亦自溺死。宋遂亡。
passages.textEn: The armies broke; Zhai Guoxiu, the militia commissioner Liu Jun and others took off their armour and surrendered. When the great army reached the central squadron, night was falling with wind and rain, and a dark fog shut everything in, so that one could not see a foot ahead. Shijie and Su Liuyi cut their moorings and fought their way out of the harbour with a dozen ships. Lu Xiufei went to the Prince of Wei's ship; it was large and lashed in a ring with the others, and judging it could not escape, he took Bing on his back and leapt into the sea. Many of the palace women and ministers died with them; after seven days more than a hundred thousand bodies floated up out of the sea. When Empress Dowager Yang heard that Bing was dead she beat her breast and wailed: "I endured death and hardship to come this far only for this one morsel of Zhao flesh — now there is no hope!" She threw herself into the sea. Shijie buried her on the shore, and soon drowned himself too. And so Song ended.

names.name: King Ping moves the Zhou capital east

confidenceNote.zh: 幽王被殺在前771年，東遷在次年；「烽火」情節的可信度見「東周」條的分歧說明。
confidenceNote.en: King You was killed in 771 BCE and the move came the next year; on the beacon story see the open question under "Eastern Zhou".

summary.zh: 申侯聯合繒與犬戎攻周，殺幽王於驪山下，諸侯共立太子宜臼為平王。平王東遷雒邑以避戎寇。此後周室衰微，諸侯強者兼併弱者，齊、楚、秦、晉始大，政由方伯。
summary.en: The Marquis of Shen, with the Zeng and the Quanrong, attacked Zhou and killed King You below Mount Li; the lords set up the crown prince Yijiu as King Ping, who moved east to Luoyi to escape the Rong raiders. From then on the royal house grew weak, the strong lords swallowed the weak, Qi, Chu, Qin and Jin began to grow great, and government came from the regional overlords.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四 周本紀
passages.textZh: 申侯怒，與繒、西夷犬戎攻幽王。幽王舉烽火徵兵，兵莫至。遂殺幽王驪山下，虜褒姒，盡取周賂而去。於是諸侯乃即申侯而共立故幽王太子宜臼，是為平王，以奉周祀。
passages.textEn: The Marquis of Shen, in anger, joined the Zeng and the Quanrong of the western barbarians in attacking King You. King You lit the beacon fires to summon troops, but none came. They killed King You below Mount Li, carried off Baosi, took all the wealth of Zhou and left. The lords then went to the Marquis of Shen and together set up Yijiu, the former crown prince of King You, as King Ping, to continue the sacrifices of Zhou.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四 周本紀
passages.textZh: 平王立，東遷于雒邑，辟戎寇。平王之時，周室衰微，諸侯彊并弱，齊、楚、秦、晉始大，政由方伯。
passages.textEn: When King Ping was set up he moved east to Luoyi to escape the Rong raiders. In King Ping's time the house of Zhou grew weak; the strong lords swallowed the weak; Qi, Chu, Qin and Jin began to grow great, and government came from the regional overlords.

names.name: Duke Huan of Qi as hegemon

summary.zh: 齊桓公以管仲為相，成為春秋第一位霸主。他自言「南伐至召陵」，「北伐山戎、離枝、孤竹」，「兵車之會三，乘車之會六，九合諸侯，一匡天下」，並想封禪泰山，經管仲諫阻而止。
summary.en: With Guan Zhong as his minister, Duke Huan of Qi became the first hegemon of the Spring and Autumn period. He boasted that he had "campaigned south as far as Shaoling" and "north against the Mountain Rong, Lizhi and Guzhu", and "held three assemblies under arms and six in carriages; nine times I have gathered the lords and once set all under Heaven right"; he wanted to perform the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai, but Guan Zhong talked him out of it.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷三十二 齊太公世家
passages.textZh: 寡人南伐至召陵，望熊山；北伐山戎、離枝、孤竹；西伐大夏，涉流沙；束馬懸車登太行，至卑耳山而還。諸侯莫違寡人。寡人兵車之會三，乘車之會六，九合諸侯，一匡天下。
passages.textEn: "I have campaigned south as far as Shaoling, within sight of Mount Xiong; north against the Mountain Rong, Lizhi and Guzhu; west against Daxia, across the shifting sands; I have bound up my horses and slung my chariots to climb the Taihang and turned back only at Mount Bei'er. None of the lords defies me. I have held three assemblies under arms and six in carriages; nine times I have gathered the lords and once set all under Heaven right."

names.name: Duke Mu of Qin masters the Western Rong
Qín Mù gōng bà Xī Róng

summary.zh: 秦穆公用由余之謀伐戎王，「益國十二，開地千里，遂霸西戎」。周天子使召公過以金鼓相賀。
summary.en: Following You Yu's plans, Duke Mu of Qin attacked the Rong king, "added twelve states, opened a thousand li of land and became overlord of the Western Rong". The Zhou king sent the Duke of Shao to congratulate him with bronze drums.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷五 秦本紀
passages.textZh: 三十七年，秦用由余謀伐戎王，益國十二，開地千里，遂霸西戎。天子使召公過賀繆公以金鼓。
passages.textEn: In the thirty-seventh year Qin, following You Yu's plans, attacked the Rong king, added twelve states, opened a thousand li of land and became overlord of the Western Rong. The Son of Heaven sent the Duke of Shao, Guo, to congratulate Duke Mu with bronze drums.

confidenceNote.zh: 城濮的地望有今山東鄄城西南、河南陳留等說。
confidenceNote.en: Chengpu is placed south-west of modern Juancheng in Shandong, or near Chenliu in Henan.

summary.zh: 楚將得臣進攻晉軍，晉軍後退；晉文公說：「昔在楚，約退三舍，可倍乎！」四月戊辰，宋公、齊將、秦將與晉侯駐軍城濮；己巳合戰，楚兵敗，得臣收餘兵而去。晉文公在踐土作王宮，五月向周王獻楚俘。
summary.en: The Chu commander Dechen attacked and the Jin army fell back; Duke Wen said: "When I was in Chu I promised to fall back three stages — can I break my word?" On wuchen of the fourth month the Duke of Song, the generals of Qi and Qin and the Marquis of Jin camped at Chengpu; on jisi they joined battle, Chu was beaten and Dechen withdrew with what was left. Duke Wen built a royal lodge at Jiantu and in the fifth month presented the Chu captives to the Zhou king.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷三十九 晉世家
passages.textZh: 楚得臣怒，撃晉師，晉師退。軍吏曰：「爲何退？」文公曰：「昔在楚，約退三舍，可倍乎！」楚師欲去，得臣不肯。四月戊辰，宋公、齊將、秦將與晉侯次城濮。己巳，與楚兵合戰，楚兵敗，得臣收餘兵去。甲午，晉師還至衡雍，作王宮于踐土。
passages.textEn: Dechen of Chu, enraged, attacked the Jin army, and the Jin army fell back. The officers asked: "Why do we retreat?" Duke Wen said: "When I was in Chu I promised to fall back three stages — can I break my word?" The Chu army wanted to leave, but Dechen would not. On wuchen of the fourth month the Duke of Song, the generals of Qi and Qin and the Marquis of Jin camped at Chengpu. On jisi they joined battle with the Chu army; the Chu army was beaten and Dechen gathered what was left and withdrew. On jiawu the Jin army returned to Hengyong and built a royal lodge at Jiantu.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷三十九 晉世家
passages.textZh: 五月丁未，獻楚俘於周，駟介百乘，徒兵千。
passages.textEn: On dingwei of the fifth month he presented the Chu captives to Zhou: a hundred armoured four-horse chariots and a thousand foot soldiers.

names.name: King Zhuang of Chu asks about the cauldrons

summary.zh: 楚莊王伐陸渾之戎，至洛水，在周郊觀兵示威。周定王派王孫滿慰勞，莊王問周鼎的大小輕重，王孫滿答：「在德不在鼎。」
summary.en: King Zhuang of Chu attacked the Rong of Luhun, reached the Luo and paraded his troops on the outskirts of the Zhou capital. King Ding of Zhou sent Wangsun Man to greet him; the king asked how large and heavy the Zhou cauldrons were, and Wangsun Man answered: "It lies in virtue, not in the cauldrons."

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十 楚世家
passages.textZh: 八年，伐陸渾戎，遂至洛，觀兵於周郊。周定王使王孫滿勞楚王。楚王問鼎小大輕重，對曰：「在德不在鼎。」
passages.textEn: In his eighth year he attacked the Rong of Luhun and went on to the Luo, parading his troops on the outskirts of the Zhou capital. King Ding of Zhou sent Wangsun Man to greet the King of Chu. The King of Chu asked how large and how heavy the cauldrons were. Wangsun Man answered: "It lies in virtue, not in the cauldrons."

names.name: Wu takes the Chu capital Ying

summary.zh: 吳王闔廬問伍子胥、孫武伐楚之策，二人建議聯合怨恨楚將子常的唐、蔡。吳軍與唐、蔡西伐楚，至漢水；闔廬之弟夫槩以所部五千人先擊楚軍，楚兵大敗。吳軍追擊，「比至郢，五戰，楚五敗」，楚昭王出奔，吳兵入郢，伍子胥、伯嚭鞭楚平王之屍以報父仇。次年越乘虛攻吳，秦出兵救楚，吳師敗。
summary.en: Helü, King of Wu, asked Wu Zixu and Sun Wu how to attack Chu; they advised joining Tang and Cai, who hated the Chu general Zichang. Wu, Tang and Cai marched west to the Han River; Helü's brother Fugai struck first with his five thousand men and the Chu army broke. Wu pursued — "by the time they reached Ying they had fought five times and Chu had lost five times" — King Zhao fled, Wu entered Ying, and Wu Zixu and Bo Pi flogged the corpse of King Ping of Chu to avenge their fathers. The next year Yue struck at Wu's empty homeland and Qin sent troops to save Chu, and the Wu army was beaten.

label.en: Wu, Tang and Cai march west to the Han

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷三十一 吳太伯世家
passages.textZh: 九年，吳王闔廬請伍子胥、孫武曰：「始子之言郢未可入，今果如何？」二子對曰：「楚將子常貪，而唐、蔡皆怨之。王必欲大伐，必得唐、蔡乃可。」闔廬從之，悉興師，與唐、蔡西伐楚，至於漢水。楚亦發兵拒吳，夾水陳。吳王闔廬弟夫槩欲戰，闔廬弗許。夫槩曰：「王已屬臣兵，兵以利爲上，尚何待焉？」遂以其部五千人襲冒楚，楚兵大敗，走。於是吳王遂縱兵追之。比至郢，五戰，楚五敗。楚昭王亡出郢，奔鄖。鄖公弟欲弑昭王，昭王與鄖公犇隨。而吳兵遂入郢。子胥、伯嚭鞭平王之屍以報父讎。
passages.textEn: In his ninth year Helü, King of Wu, asked Wu Zixu and Sun Wu: "At first you said Ying could not yet be entered. How is it now?" They answered: "The Chu general Zichang is greedy and Tang and Cai both resent him. If Your Majesty wants a great campaign, you must have Tang and Cai." Helü followed this, raised his whole army and with Tang and Cai went west against Chu as far as the Han River. Chu too sent troops to resist, and the armies drew up on either side of the river. Fugai, Helü's younger brother, wanted to fight; Helü would not allow it. Fugai said: "Your Majesty has entrusted troops to me. In war advantage comes first — what are we waiting for?" With his own five thousand men he fell on Chu, and the Chu army was badly beaten and fled. Then the King of Wu let his army loose in pursuit. By the time they reached Ying they had fought five times and Chu had lost five times. King Zhao of Chu fled from Ying to Yun; the younger brother of the lord of Yun wanted to kill him, and he fled with the lord of Yun to Sui. The Wu army entered Ying. Zixu and Bo Pi flogged the corpse of King Ping to avenge their fathers.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷三十一 吳太伯世家
passages.textZh: 十年春，越聞吳王之在郢，國空，乃伐吳。吳使別兵撃越。楚告急秦，秦遣兵救楚撃吳，吳師敗。
passages.textEn: In the spring of the tenth year Yue heard that the King of Wu was in Ying and his state was empty, and attacked Wu. Wu sent a detached force against Yue. Chu appealed to Qin for help; Qin sent troops to save Chu and attacked Wu, and the Wu army was beaten.

question.zh: 孫武是否真有其人、參與此役？
question.en: Did Sun Wu exist, and was he at this campaign?

claim.zh: 《史記》記闔廬與伍子胥、孫武謀伐楚。
claim.en: The Shiji has Helü plan the campaign with Wu Zixu and Sun Wu.

source.en: Shiji, House of Wu

accounts.quoteZh: 吳王闔廬請伍子胥、孫武曰

claim.zh: 《左傳》詳記此役，卻完全沒有提到孫武；宋代葉適等人因此懷疑其人其事。1972年銀雀山漢簡出土《孫子兵法》，證明此書在西漢初已流傳，但仍不能證明孫武本人參戰。
claim.en: The Zuo zhuan describes the campaign in detail without ever mentioning Sun Wu, which led Ye Shi and others in the Song to doubt him. The Yinqueshan slips (found 1972) show the Art of War was circulating by early Han, but cannot prove Sun Wu himself was there.

source.zh: 《左傳》定公四年；葉適《習學記言》；銀雀山漢簡
source.en: Zuo zhuan, Duke Ding 4; Ye Shi; Yinqueshan slips

confidenceNote.zh: 夫椒一般認為在太湖中（今蘇州西南），也有主張在今紹興北者。
confidenceNote.en: Fujiao is usually placed in Lake Tai south-west of Suzhou; some put it north of Shaoxing.

summary.zh: 越王句踐聽說吳王夫差日夜練兵要報父仇，不聽范蠡勸阻，搶先攻吳。夫差悉發精兵迎擊，在夫椒大敗越軍；句踐以餘兵五千人退保會稽，被吳軍包圍。
summary.en: Goujian, King of Yue, heard that Fuchai, King of Wu, was drilling his troops day and night to avenge his father, and against Fan Li's advice struck first. Fuchai sent all his best troops against him and crushed Yue at Fujiao; Goujian retreated to Kuaiji with five thousand men and was besieged there.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十一 越王句踐世家
passages.textZh: 三年，句踐聞呉王夫差日夜勒兵，且以報越，越欲先呉未發往伐之。范蠡諫曰：「不可。臣聞兵者凶器也，戰者逆德也，爭者事之末也。陰謀逆德，好用凶器，試身於所末，上帝禁之，行者不利。」越王曰：「吾已決之矣。」遂興師。呉王聞之，悉發精兵撃越，敗之夫椒。越王乃以餘兵五千人保棲於會稽。呉王追而圍之。
passages.textEn: In the third year Goujian heard that Fuchai, King of Wu, was drilling his troops day and night to take revenge on Yue, and wanted to strike before Wu moved. Fan Li remonstrated: "No. I have heard that arms are instruments of ill omen, war goes against virtue, and contention is the last of all things. To plot against virtue and delight in ill-omened instruments, staking oneself on the last of things, is forbidden by Heaven; whoever does it will not prosper." The King of Yue said: "I have decided." He raised his army. When the King of Wu heard, he sent all his best troops against Yue and beat them at Fujiao. The King of Yue took refuge on Kuaiji with the five thousand men he had left, and the King of Wu pursued and besieged him.

summary.zh: 句踐歸國後「置膽於坐」，刻苦圖強。吳王夫差北上與齊、晉爭霸，國力耗盡；越再度大舉伐吳，「吳士民罷弊，輕銳盡死於齊、晉」，越大破吳師，圍之三年，把吳王困在姑蘇山上。夫差求和不成，自殺，吳亡。
summary.en: Back home Goujian "set a gall bladder by his seat" and worked to rebuild his strength. Fuchai spent Wu's strength contending with Qi and Jin in the north; when Yue attacked again, "the people of Wu were worn out and their best troops had all died fighting Qi and Jin". Yue crushed Wu, besieged it for three years and penned the king on the hill of Gusu. Fuchai's plea for peace was refused; he killed himself, and Wu was no more.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十一 越王句踐世家
passages.textZh: 呉旣赦越，越王句踐反國，乃苦身焦思，置膽於坐，坐臥卽仰膽，飲食亦嘗膽也。曰：「女忘會稽之恥邪？」身自耕作，夫人自織，食不加肉，衣不重采，折節下賢人，厚遇賓客，振貧弔死，與百姓同其勞。
passages.textEn: When Wu had pardoned Yue and Goujian had gone home, he punished his body and wore out his mind. He set a gall bladder by his seat and looked up at it sitting or lying, and tasted it when he ate or drank, saying: "Have you forgotten the shame of Kuaiji?" He ploughed with his own hands and his wife wove; he ate no second meat and wore no second colour; he humbled himself before worthy men, treated his guests generously, relieved the poor, mourned the dead and shared the toil of the common people.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十一 越王句踐世家
passages.textZh: 其後四年，越復伐呉。呉士民罷弊，輕鋭盡死於齊、晉。而越大破呉，因而留圍之三年，呉師敗，越遂復棲呉王於姑蘇之山。
passages.textEn: Four years later Yue attacked Wu again. The people of Wu were worn out and their best troops had all died fighting Qi and Jin. Yue crushed Wu and stayed to besiege it for three years; the Wu army was beaten, and Yue penned the King of Wu up on the hill of Gusu.

summary.zh: 智伯率韓、魏圍趙襄子於晉陽。趙襄子暗中與韓、魏約定，夜裡派人殺守堤的官吏，決水反灌智伯軍。智伯軍救水而亂，韓、魏從兩翼夾擊，襄子從正面進攻，大敗智伯，殺智伯，盡滅智氏之族；三家分智氏之田。
summary.en: Zhi Bo, with Han and Wei, besieged Zhao Xiangzi in Jinyang. Xiangzi secretly came to terms with Han and Wei, sent men by night to kill the officers guarding the dykes and turned the water onto Zhi Bo's camp. While Zhi Bo's army struggled with the flood, Han and Wei struck its flanks and Xiangzi its front; Zhi Bo was routed and killed, and his whole clan wiped out. The three houses divided the Zhi lands.

passages.sourceEn: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance (Sima Guang, 1084)
passages.locator: 卷一 周紀一
passages.textZh: 襄子夜使人殺守堤之吏，而決水灌智伯軍。智伯軍救水而亂，韓、魏翼而擊之，襄子將卒犯其前，大敗智伯之眾。遂殺智伯，盡滅智氏之族。
passages.textEn: Zhao Xiangzi sent men by night to kill the officers guarding the dykes and broke them to flood Zhi Bo's army. Zhi Bo's army fell into disorder fighting the water; Han and Wei struck its flanks and Xiangzi led his men against its front, and Zhi Bo's host was routed. They killed Zhi Bo and wiped out the whole Zhi clan.

passages.sourceEn: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance (Sima Guang, 1084)
passages.locator: 卷一 周紀一
passages.textZh: 三家分智氏之田。
passages.textEn: The three houses divided the lands of the Zhi.

summary.zh: 周威烈王二十三年（前403），周天子「命晉大夫魏斯、趙籍、韓虔為諸侯」。司馬光《資治通鑑》從這一年寫起，評論說晉大夫「剖分晉國，天子既不能討，又寵秩之，使列於諸侯」。
summary.en: In 403 BCE the Zhou king "appointed the ministers of Jin, Wei Si, Zhao Ji and Han Qian, feudal lords". Sima Guang began his Comprehensive Mirror with this year, remarking that the ministers "carved up the state of Jin; the Son of Heaven, unable to punish them, honoured them with rank and set them among the lords".

passages.sourceEn: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance (Sima Guang, 1084)
passages.locator: 卷一 周紀一
passages.textZh: 初命晉大夫魏斯、趙籍、韓虔為諸侯。
passages.textEn: For the first time the ministers of Jin, Wei Si, Zhao Ji and Han Qian, were appointed feudal lords.

passages.sourceEn: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance (Sima Guang, 1084)
passages.locator: 卷一 周紀一 臣光曰
passages.textZh: 今晉大夫暴蔑其君，剖分晉國，天子既不能討，又寵秩之，使列於諸侯
passages.textEn: Now the ministers of Jin have trampled on their lord and carved up the state of Jin; the Son of Heaven, unable to punish them, has instead honoured them with rank and set them among the lords.

confidenceNote.zh: 變法分兩次（前356、前350），此處以第一次為起點。
confidenceNote.en: The reforms came in two rounds (356 and 350 BCE).

summary.zh: 秦孝公以衛鞅為左庶長，定變法之令：民眾編為什伍，互相監督、連坐；不告發奸人者腰斬，告發者與斬敵首同賞；二男以上不分家者加倍徵賦；有軍功者按等級受爵，私鬥者依輕重受刑；努力耕織、生產粟帛多者免除徭役。
summary.en: Duke Xiao of Qin made Wei Yang Zuo Shuzhang and decreed his new laws: the people were grouped in fives and tens to watch each other and share punishment; failing to denounce a crime meant being cut in two, denouncing one earned the reward for an enemy head; households with two grown sons living together paid double tax; merit in war earned rank on a fixed scale, private feuding was punished by its gravity; those who produced much grain and cloth were freed from labour service.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六十八 商君列傳
passages.textZh: 以衛鞅為左庶長，卒定變法之令。令民為什伍，而相牧司連坐。不告姦者腰斬，告姦者與斬敵首同賞，匿姦者與降敵同罰。民有二男以上不分異者，倍其賦。有軍功者，各以率受上爵；為私斗者，各以輕重被刑大小。戮力本業，耕織致粟帛多者復其身
passages.textEn: Wei Yang was made Zuo Shuzhang and the decrees changing the laws were settled at last. The people were organised in groups of ten and five, to watch each other and share each other's punishments. Whoever failed to denounce a crime was cut in two at the waist; whoever denounced one was rewarded as if he had taken an enemy head; whoever hid a criminal was punished as if he had surrendered to the enemy. A household with two or more grown sons who did not set up separately paid double tax. Those with merit in war received rank according to a scale; those who fought private quarrels were punished according to the gravity. Those who worked hard at the basic occupations, and produced much grain and cloth by ploughing and weaving, were exempted from labour service.

confidenceNote.zh: 年份有前342、前341二說；馬陵地望有今河南范縣、山東莘縣、山東郯城等說。
confidenceNote.en: Dated 342 or 341 BCE; Maling is placed near modern Fanxian (Henan), Shenxian or Tancheng (Shandong).

summary.zh: 孫臏算定魏將龐涓日暮將至馬陵：那裡道路狹窄，兩旁多險阻，可以伏兵。他砍去大樹樹皮，在白處寫上「龐涓死于此樹之下」，令齊軍萬名善射的弩手夾道埋伏，約定見火舉而齊發。龐涓夜至樹下，點火照看字跡，還沒讀完，齊軍萬弩齊發，魏軍大亂，龐涓自知兵敗，自剄而死。
summary.en: Sun Bin reckoned that the Wei general Pang Juan would reach Maling at dusk, where the road was narrow with steep places on each side, good for an ambush. He stripped a great tree and wrote on the white wood: "Pang Juan dies beneath this tree", and set ten thousand of Qi's best crossbowmen on both sides of the road, to shoot together when they saw a fire. Pang Juan reached the tree that night and struck a light to read it; before he had finished, ten thousand crossbows loosed, the Wei army fell into confusion, and Pang Juan, knowing he was beaten, cut his own throat.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六十五 孫子吳起列傳
passages.textZh: 孫子度其行，暮當至馬陵。馬陵道陜，而旁多阻隘，可伏兵，乃斫大樹白而書之曰「龐涓死于此樹之下」。於是令齊軍善射者萬弩，夾道而伏，期曰「暮見火舉而俱發」。龐涓果夜至斫木下，見白書，乃鉆火燭之。讀其書未畢，齊軍萬弩俱發，魏軍大亂相失。龐涓自知智窮兵敗，乃自剄
passages.textEn: Sun Bin reckoned his pace: by dusk he would reach Maling. The road at Maling was narrow with many steep places beside it, where troops could lie in wait. He stripped the bark off a great tree and wrote on the white wood: "Pang Juan dies beneath this tree." Then he had ten thousand of the best crossbowmen of Qi lie in wait on both sides of the road, with orders: "When you see a fire lit at dusk, shoot all together." Pang Juan did indeed reach the stripped tree that night, saw the writing on the white wood and struck a light to read it. Before he had finished, ten thousand crossbows of Qi loosed at once; the Wei army fell into confusion and lost all order. Pang Juan, knowing his wits were spent and his army beaten, cut his own throat.

names.name: King Wuling's Hu dress and mounted archery

summary.zh: 趙武靈王決心改穿胡服、練習騎射以強兵，問肥義：「今吾將胡服騎射以教百姓，而世必議寡人，柰何？」肥義答以「疑事無功，疑行無名」，勸他不必顧慮天下非議。
summary.en: King Wuling of Zhao resolved to adopt the clothing of the Hu and train his men to shoot from horseback. He asked Fei Yi: "Now I mean to teach the people to wear Hu clothing and shoot from horseback, and the world will surely criticise me. What shall I do?" Fei Yi replied that "a doubtful undertaking achieves nothing and doubtful conduct wins no name", and told him to pay no heed to the critics.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十三 趙世家
passages.textZh: 「今吾將胡服騎射以教百姓，而世必議寡人，柰何？」肥義曰：「臣聞疑事無功，疑行無名。王旣定負遺俗之慮，殆無顧天下之議矣。」
passages.textEn: "Now I mean to teach the people to wear Hu clothing and shoot from horseback, and the world will surely criticise me. What shall I do?" Fei Yi said: "I have heard that a doubtful undertaking achieves nothing and doubtful conduct wins no name. Since Your Majesty has resolved to bear the charge of defying custom, pay no heed to what the world says."

names.name: Tian Dan's fire oxen at Jimo

summary.zh: 燕將樂毅攻破齊國七十餘城，只剩莒與即墨。田單守即墨，收城中千餘頭牛，披上畫有五彩龍紋的絳色衣，角上縛刀，尾上紮浸油的蘆葦點火，夜裡從城牆鑿開的數十個洞放出，五千壯士隨後衝殺，燕軍大驚潰敗。齊人隨後收復失地。
summary.en: The Yan general Yue Yi had taken more than seventy cities of Qi; only Ju and Jimo held out. Tian Dan, holding Jimo, gathered a thousand oxen, dressed them in red silk painted with five-coloured dragons, bound blades to their horns and blazing fat-soaked reeds to their tails, and let them loose at night through dozens of holes cut in the wall, with five thousand men behind them. The Yan army panicked and broke, and Qi went on to recover its lost lands.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八十二 田單列傳
passages.textZh: 田單乃收城中得千餘牛，為絳繒衣，畫以五彩龍文，束兵刃於其角，而灌脂束葦於尾，燒其端。鑿城數十穴，夜縱牛，壯士五千人隨其後。牛尾熱，怒而奔燕軍，燕軍夜大驚。牛尾炬火光明炫燿，燕軍視之皆龍文，所觸盡死傷。
passages.textEn: Tian Dan gathered more than a thousand oxen in the city, dressed them in red silk painted with dragons in five colours, bound blades to their horns, and tied reeds soaked in fat to their tails and set the ends alight. He cut dozens of holes in the city wall and let the oxen loose at night, with five thousand strong men behind them. Their tails burning, the maddened oxen charged the Yan army, which woke in terror. In the blaze of the torches on their tails the Yan soldiers saw only dragons, and all they touched were killed or wounded.

confidenceNote.zh: 今山西高平一帶發現多處屍骨坑，一般認為與此役有關。
confidenceNote.en: Mass graves found around modern Gaoping, Shanxi, are generally associated with the battle.

summary.zh: 秦、趙爭奪上黨，相持於長平。趙王以趙括代廉頗為將，趙括出擊，被秦軍包圍，突圍時被射殺，趙軍四十萬人投降。秦將白起（武安君）以為趙卒反覆，「乃挾詐而盡阬殺之」，只放回年幼者二百四十人；前後斬首虜四十五萬人，趙國大震。
summary.en: Qin and Zhao fought over Shangdang and faced each other at Changping. The King of Zhao replaced Lian Po with Zhao Kuo, who attacked, was surrounded and was shot dead trying to break out; four hundred thousand Zhao soldiers surrendered. The Qin general Bai Qi, Lord of Wu'an, judging Zhao's soldiers fickle, "buried them all alive by a trick", sending back only the two hundred and forty youngest; four hundred and fifty thousand were beheaded or captured in all, and Zhao was thrown into terror.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七十三 白起王翦列傳
passages.textZh: 秦軍射殺趙括。括軍敗，卒四十萬人降武安君。武安君計曰：「前秦已拔上黨，上黨民不樂為秦而歸趙。趙卒反覆。非盡殺之，恐為亂。」乃挾詐而盡阬殺之，遺其小者二百四十人歸趙。前後斬首虜四十五萬人。趙人大震。
passages.textEn: The Qin army shot Zhao Kuo dead. His army was beaten, and four hundred thousand men surrendered to the Lord of Wu'an. The Lord of Wu'an reckoned: "Qin took Shangdang before, but the people of Shangdang did not want to be Qin's and went over to Zhao. Zhao's soldiers are fickle. Unless I kill them all I fear they will rise." So by a trick he buried them all alive, sending back to Zhao only the two hundred and forty youngest. In all, four hundred and fifty thousand were beheaded or captured, and the people of Zhao were thrown into terror.

names.name: Jing Ke's attempt on the King of Qin

summary.zh: 燕太子丹派荊軻入秦行刺。太子與賓客白衣冠送至易水之上，高漸離擊筑，荊軻和而歌：「風蕭蕭兮易水寒，壯士一去兮不復還！」荊軻在咸陽宮獻督亢地圖，圖窮匕見，刺秦王不中，被殺。次年秦攻破燕都薊。
summary.en: Crown Prince Dan of Yan sent Jing Ke to assassinate the King of Qin. The prince and his retainers, dressed in white, saw him off at the River Yi, where Gao Jianli struck the zhu and Jing Ke sang: "The wind sighs, the River Yi is cold; the hero goes and will not return!" At the Qin palace in Xianyang he presented a map of Dukang; when the map was unrolled the dagger appeared, but he missed the king and was killed. The next year Qin took the Yan capital, Ji.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八十六 刺客列傳
passages.textZh: 太子及賓客知其事者，皆白衣冠以送之。至易水之上，既祖，取道，髙漸離撃筑，荊軻和而歌，爲變徴之聲，士皆垂涙涕泣。又前而爲歌曰：「風蕭蕭兮易水寒，壯士一去兮不復還！」復爲羽聲慨，士皆瞋目，發盡上指冠。於是荊軻就車而去，終已不顧。
passages.textEn: The crown prince and those of his retainers who knew of the plan saw him off dressed in white. At the River Yi, after the sacrifice to the road, Gao Jianli struck the zhu and Jing Ke sang to it in the mournful bianzhi mode, and all the men wept. Then he stepped forward and sang: "The wind sighs, the River Yi is cold; the hero goes and will not return!" Then in the stirring yu mode, and every man glared, his hair standing up against his cap. And Jing Ke mounted his carriage and left, and never looked back.

summary.zh: 前230年起秦先後滅韓、趙、魏、楚、燕；前221年秦將王賁自燕南下攻齊，俘齊王建，秦王政「初并天下」。他廢分封，「分天下以為三十六郡，郡置守、尉、監」，收天下兵器聚之咸陽，統一法度衡石丈尺，「車同軌，書同文字」。
summary.en: From 230 BCE Qin destroyed Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu and Yan in turn; in 221 BCE Wang Ben came south from Yan, captured King Jian of Qi, and King Zheng "for the first time united the realm". Instead of fiefs he "divided the realm into thirty-six commanderies, each with a governor, a commandant and an inspector", gathered the realm's weapons at Xianyang, and made laws, weights and measures uniform — "carts with the same axle width, writing with the same characters".

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 二十六年，齊王建與其相后勝發兵守其西界，不通秦。秦使將軍王賁從燕南攻齊，得齊王建。
passages.textEn: In the twenty-sixth year Jian, King of Qi, and his chancellor Hou Sheng sent troops to guard their western border and cut off contact with Qin. Qin sent the general Wang Ben south from Yan to attack Qi, and captured Jian, King of Qi.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 分天下以為三十六郡，郡置守、尉、監。更名民曰「黔首」。大酺。收天下兵，聚之咸陽，銷以為鐘鐻，金人十二，重各千石，置廷宮中。一法度衡石丈尺。車同軌。書同文字。地東至海暨朝鮮，西至臨洮、羌中，南至北向戶，北據河為塞，并陰山至遼東。
passages.textEn: He divided the realm into thirty-six commanderies, each with a governor, a commandant and an inspector. The people were renamed "the black-headed". There was a great feast. The weapons of the realm were gathered at Xianyang and melted down into bell stands and twelve bronze men, each weighing a thousand dan, which were set in the palace. Laws, weights and measures were made uniform. Carts had the same axle width. Writing used the same characters. The land reached east to the sea and Chaoxian, west to Lintao and the Qiang country, south to the lands where doors face north, and north to the Yellow River, held as a frontier, along the Yin Mountains to Liaodong.

names.name: Meng Tian builds the Great Wall

confidenceNote.zh: 今日所見的磚石長城多為明代所築。秦長城多為夯土與石砌，大體連接戰國秦、趙、燕舊長城，走向比明長城偏北。
confidenceNote.en: The brick-and-stone wall seen today is mostly Ming. The Qin wall was rammed earth and rubble, largely joining up the older walls of Qin, Zhao and Yan, and ran further north than the Ming wall.

summary.zh: 秦統一後，派蒙恬率三十萬眾北逐戎狄，收取河南地，修築長城，「因地形，用制險塞，起臨洮，至遼東，延袤萬餘里」。蒙恬渡河據陽山，暴師於外十餘年，威振匈奴。
summary.en: After unification Qin sent Meng Tian with three hundred thousand men to drive off the Rong and Di and take the land south of the river bend, and to build a long wall "following the lie of the land and using the passes as strongpoints, from Lintao to Liaodong, more than ten thousand li". Meng Tian crossed the river and held the Yang Mountains, keeping his army in the field for more than ten years, and his might struck fear into the Xiongnu.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八十八 蒙恬列傳
passages.textZh: 秦已并天下，乃使蒙恬將三十萬眾北逐戎狄，收河南。筑長城，因地形，用制險塞，起臨洮，至遼東，延袤萬餘里。於是渡河，據陽山，逶蛇而北。暴師於外十餘年，居上郡。是時蒙恬威振匈奴。
passages.textEn: When Qin had united the realm it sent Meng Tian with three hundred thousand men to drive off the Rong and Di in the north and take the land south of the river bend. He built a long wall, following the lie of the land and using the passes as strongpoints, from Lintao to Liaodong, more than ten thousand li long. Then he crossed the river and held the Yang Mountains, winding north. He kept his army in the field for more than ten years, based in Shang commandery; at that time Meng Tian's might struck fear into the Xiongnu.

confidenceNote.zh: 次年（前212）阬殺諸生四百六十餘人於咸陽；被殺者是儒生還是方士，今人有爭論。
confidenceNote.en: The next year (212 BCE) more than 460 scholars were buried alive at Xianyang; whether they were Confucians or occult practitioners is debated.

summary.zh: 丞相李斯建議：除秦國史記之外的史書一律焚毀；除博士官所藏外，民間收藏的《詩》《書》與百家之言都要交給郡守、郡尉燒掉；敢私下談論《詩》《書》者棄市，以古非今者滅族；醫藥、卜筮、種樹之書不燒。始皇從之。
summary.en: Chancellor Li Si proposed that all historical records other than Qin's be burned; that the Odes, the Documents and the sayings of the hundred schools held by anyone outside the court scholars be handed to the governors and commandants to be burned; that anyone discussing the Odes and Documents be executed in the market and anyone using the past to criticise the present be exterminated with his clan; and that books on medicine, divination and planting be spared. The First Emperor approved.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 臣請史官非秦記皆燒之。非博士官所職，天下敢有藏詩、書、百家語者，悉詣守、尉雜燒之。有敢偶語詩書者棄市。以古非今者族。吏見知不舉者與同罪。令下三十日不燒，黥為城旦。所不去者，醫藥卜筮種樹之書。
passages.textEn: "I request that the historians' records other than those of Qin all be burned. Except for what is in the keeping of the court scholars, anyone in the realm who dares to keep the Odes, the Documents or the sayings of the hundred schools must take them to the governor or commandant to be burned. Anyone who dares to discuss the Odes and Documents together shall be executed in the market; anyone who uses the past to criticise the present shall be exterminated with his clan; officials who know of it and do not report it share the crime. Whoever has not burned his books thirty days after the order is issued shall be tattooed and sent to build walls. Books to be spared: medicine, divination and planting."

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 於是使御史悉案問諸生，諸生傳相告引，乃自除犯禁者四百六十餘人，皆阬之咸陽，使天下知之，以懲後。
passages.textEn: Then he had the censors examine all the scholars; they denounced one another, and he himself picked out more than four hundred and sixty who had broken the prohibitions and had them all buried alive at Xianyang, so that the realm would know and take warning.

names.name: The death of the First Emperor at Shaqiu

confidenceNote.zh: 北京大學藏西漢竹書《趙正書》記胡亥是始皇臨終同意立的，與《史記》不同；其可信度今人仍有討論。
confidenceNote.en: The Western Han bamboo text Zhao Zheng shu (Peking University collection) says the dying emperor agreed to Huhai's succession, unlike the Shiji; how far to trust it is still debated.

summary.zh: 始皇出巡至平原津而病，寫下賜公子扶蘇的璽書——「與喪會咸陽而葬」——封存在中車府令趙高處，未交使者。七月丙寅，始皇崩於沙丘平臺。丞相李斯恐諸公子及天下有變，秘不發喪，只有胡亥、趙高及親幸宦者五六人知情。其後趙高、李斯偽造詔書，賜死扶蘇，立胡亥為二世皇帝。
summary.en: On tour, the First Emperor fell ill at the Pingyuan ford and wrote a sealed letter to Prince Fusu — "Meet the cortège at Xianyang and bury me" — which stayed with Zhao Gao, keeper of the seals, and was never sent. On bingyin of the seventh month the emperor died at the Pingtai terrace of Shaqiu. Li Si, fearing the princes and the realm might rise, kept the death secret; only Huhai, Zhao Gao and five or six favoured eunuchs knew. Zhao Gao and Li Si then forged orders for Fusu to kill himself and set Huhai on the throne as Second Emperor.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 至平原津而病。始皇惡言死，群臣莫敢言死事。上病益甚，乃為璽書賜公子扶蘇曰：「與喪會咸陽而葬。」書已封，在中車府令趙高行符璽事所，未授使者。七月丙寅，始皇崩於沙丘平臺。丞相斯為上崩在外，恐諸公子及天下有變，乃祕之，不發喪。
passages.textEn: At the Pingyuan ford he fell ill. The First Emperor hated talk of death and none of his ministers dared mention it. As he grew worse he wrote a sealed letter to Prince Fusu: "Meet the cortège at Xianyang and bury me." The letter was sealed but left with Zhao Gao, Director of the Palace Carriages, who kept the seals, and was never handed to a messenger. On bingyin of the seventh month the First Emperor died at the Pingtai terrace of Shaqiu. Chancellor Li Si, because the emperor had died away from the capital and he feared the princes and the realm might rise, kept it secret and announced no mourning.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷六 秦始皇本紀
passages.textZh: 獨子胡亥、趙高及所幸宦者五六人知上死。
passages.textEn: Only his son Huhai, Zhao Gao and five or six favoured eunuchs knew the emperor was dead.

summary.zh: 秦二世元年七月，陳勝、吳廣率戍卒北上戍邊，在大澤鄉遇雨誤期，按秦法當斬。陳勝殺死押送的兩名將尉，號召眾人：「王侯將相寧有種乎！」詐稱公子扶蘇、項燕，袒右臂，稱大楚，築壇盟誓，攻下大澤鄉和蘄縣。天下響應，秦朝隨之崩潰。
summary.en: In the seventh month of 209 BCE Chen Sheng and Wu Guang, leading conscripts north to frontier duty, were held up by rain at Dazexiang; under Qin law being late meant death. Chen Sheng killed the two officers in charge and roused the men: "Kings, nobles, generals and ministers — are they a breed apart?" Claiming to act for Prince Fusu and Xiang Yan, they bared their right arms, called themselves Great Chu, swore an oath at an altar and took Dazexiang and Qi county. Risings followed across the realm, and the Qin empire fell apart.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十八 陳涉世家
passages.textZh: 陳勝佐之，并殺兩尉。召令徒屬曰：「公等遇雨，皆已失期，失期當斬。
passages.textEn: Chen Sheng helped him and they killed both officers. He called the men together and said: "You have all been caught by the rain and are already late, and being late means death.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷四十八 陳涉世家
passages.textZh: 且壯士不死即已，死即舉大名耳，王侯將相寧有種乎！」徒屬皆曰：「敬受命。」乃詐稱公子扶蘇、項燕，從民欲也。袒右，稱大楚。為壇而盟，祭以尉首。陳勝自立為將軍，吳廣為都尉。攻大澤鄉，收而攻蘄。
passages.textEn: …And if a brave man is not to die, well and good; but if he dies, let him die making a great name. Kings, nobles, generals and ministers — are they a breed apart?" The men all said: "We take your orders." They falsely claimed to be led by Prince Fusu and Xiang Yan, as the people wished; they bared their right arms and called themselves Great Chu. They built an altar and swore an oath, offering the officers' heads in sacrifice. Chen Sheng made himself general and Wu Guang commandant. They attacked Dazexiang, took it and attacked Qi county.

summary.zh: 秦將王離圍趙王於鉅鹿。項羽殺上將軍宋義（卿子冠軍）後，率楚軍全部渡河，「皆沈船，破釜甑，燒廬舍，持三日糧」，以示必死。楚軍包圍王離，九戰，斷絕秦軍甬道，大破之，殺蘇角，俘王離；涉閒自焚而死。從此楚兵冠於諸侯。
summary.en: The Qin general Wang Li was besieging the King of Zhao in Julu. Having killed his commander Song Yi, Xiang Yu took the whole Chu army across the river, "sank the boats, smashed the cooking pots, burned the huts and carried three days' rations" to show there would be no turning back. The Chu army surrounded Wang Li, fought nine times, cut the walled supply road and crushed the Qin army, killing Su Jiao and capturing Wang Li; She Jian burned himself to death. From then on Chu stood first among the lords.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀
passages.textZh: 項羽已殺卿子冠軍，威震楚國，名聞諸侯。乃遣當陽君、蒲將軍將卒二萬渡河，救鉅鹿。戰少利，陳餘復請兵。項羽乃悉引兵渡河，皆沈船，破釜甑，燒廬舍，持三日糧，以示士卒必死，無一還心。於是至則圍王離，與秦軍遇，九戰，絕其甬道，大破之，殺蘇角，虜王離。涉閒不降楚，自燒殺。當是時，楚兵冠諸侯。
passages.textEn: When Xiang Yu had killed the "Excellent General", his might shook Chu and his name was known to all the lords. He sent the Lord of Dangyang and General Pu across the river with twenty thousand men to relieve Julu. They had little success, and Chen Yu asked for more troops. Then Xiang Yu took his whole army across, sank the boats, smashed the cooking pots, burned the huts and carried three days' rations, to show the men they must die and not one would turn back. On arrival they surrounded Wang Li, met the Qin army, fought nine times, cut its walled supply road and crushed it, killed Su Jiao and captured Wang Li. She Jian would not surrender to Chu and burned himself to death. At that moment the army of Chu stood first among the lords.

names.name: Liu Bang's code of three articles

confidenceNote.zh: 事在漢元年十月，按當時以十月為歲首的曆法，約當公元前207年末。
confidenceNote.en: In the tenth month of the first year of Han; since the year then began in the tenth month, this falls late in 207 BCE.

summary.zh: 劉邦西入咸陽，聽從樊噲、張良的勸諫，封存秦朝寶物府庫，還軍霸上。他召集諸縣父老豪傑，宣布：「與父老約，法三章耳：殺人者死，傷人及盜抵罪。」其餘秦法全部廢除。
summary.en: Liu Bang went west into Xianyang and, on Fan Kuai and Zhang Liang's advice, sealed up the Qin treasuries and took his army back to Bashang. He summoned the elders and leading men of the counties and announced: "I agree with you, elders, on a code of three articles only: whoever kills shall die; whoever wounds or steals shall be punished accordingly." All the rest of Qin's laws were abolished.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷八 高祖本紀
passages.textZh: 遂西入咸陽。欲止宮休舍，樊噲、張良諫，乃封秦重寶財物府庫，還軍霸上。召諸縣父老豪桀曰：「父老苦秦苛法久矣，誹謗者族，偶語者棄市。吾與諸侯約，先入關者王之，吾當王關中。與父老約，法三章耳：殺人者死，傷人及盜抵罪。餘悉除去秦法。
passages.textEn: He went west into Xianyang. He wanted to stay in the palace, but Fan Kuai and Zhang Liang advised against it, so he sealed up the treasures and storehouses of Qin and took his army back to Bashang. He summoned the elders and leading men of the counties and said: "Elders, you have suffered long under Qin's harsh laws: for slander a man's whole clan was executed, for talking together men were executed in the market. I agreed with the lords that whoever first entered the passes would be king here, so I am to be king of Guanzhong. I agree with you, elders, on a code of three articles only: whoever kills shall die; whoever wounds or steals shall be punished accordingly. All the rest of Qin's laws are abolished.

summary.zh: 項羽駐軍垓下，兵少食盡，被漢軍與諸侯軍重重包圍。夜裡聽到漢軍四面皆唱楚歌，項羽大驚：「漢皆已得楚乎？是何楚人之多也！」夜飲帳中，對美人虞姬、駿馬騅悲歌：「力拔山兮氣蓋世……」突圍後至烏江，亭長備船勸他渡江，他笑道：「天之亡我，我何渡為！」不肯渡江而死。
summary.en: Xiang Yu's army was walled up at Gaixia, few in number and out of food, ringed several deep by the Han army and the lords' troops. In the night he heard Chu songs on every side of the Han lines. "Has Han already taken all of Chu?" he cried. "How many men of Chu there are!" He drank in his tent and sang to his beloved Yu and his horse Zhui: "My strength plucked up mountains, my spirit overtopped the world…" He broke out and reached the Wu River, where the post chief had a boat ready; he laughed — "Heaven is destroying me, why should I cross?" — and died there.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀
passages.textZh: 項王軍壁垓下，兵少食盡，漢軍及諸侯兵圍之數重。夜聞漢軍四面皆楚歌，項王乃大驚曰：「漢皆已得楚乎？是何楚人之多也！」項王則夜起，飲帳中。有美人名虞，常幸從；駿馬名騅，常騎之。於是項王乃悲歌忼慨，自為詩曰：「力拔山兮氣蓋世，時不利兮騅不逝。騅不逝兮可柰何，虞兮虞兮柰若何！」
passages.textEn: King Xiang's army was walled up at Gaixia, few in number and out of food, and the Han army and the lords' troops encircled it several deep. In the night he heard Chu songs on every side of the Han lines. Greatly alarmed, he said: "Has Han already taken all of Chu? How many men of Chu there are!" He rose in the night and drank in his tent. He had a beauty named Yu who was always with him, and a fine horse named Zhui which he always rode. Then he sang a sad and passionate song of his own making: "My strength plucked up mountains, my spirit overtopped the world; but the times are against me and Zhui will run no more. If Zhui will run no more, what can I do? Yu, O Yu, what will become of you?"

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷七 項羽本紀
passages.textZh: 於是項王乃欲東渡烏江。烏江亭長檥船待，謂項王曰：「江東雖小，地方千里，眾數十萬人，亦足王也。願大王急渡。今獨臣有船，漢軍至，無以渡。」項王笑曰：「天之亡我，我何渡為！且籍與江東子弟八千人渡江而西，今無一人還，縱江東父兄憐而王我，我何面目見之？
passages.textEn: Then King Xiang wanted to cross east over the Wu River. The head of the Wujiang post had a boat ready and said: "Jiangdong may be small, but it is a thousand li square with several hundred thousand people — enough to be king of. I beg Your Majesty to cross quickly. I alone have a boat; when the Han army comes it will have no way across." King Xiang laughed: "Heaven is destroying me — why should I cross? Besides, I crossed the river and went west with eight thousand young men of Jiangdong, and now not one comes back. Even if the elders of Jiangdong pitied me and made me their king, how could I face them?

summary.zh: 冒頓單于把精兵藏起，只讓漢軍看到老弱。漢高帝傾全軍三十二萬人北追，多為步兵；高帝先至平城，步兵未到，冒頓縱精兵四十萬騎把他圍困在白登山，七天內外不得相救。高帝派使者暗中厚贈閼氏，閼氏勸冒頓解圍。此後漢以和親與歲贈維持與匈奴的和平。
summary.en: Modu Chanyu hid his best troops and showed the Han only his weak ones. Gaozu sent his whole army north in pursuit — three hundred and twenty thousand, mostly infantry; reaching Pingcheng ahead of his foot soldiers, he was surrounded on Baideng hill by four hundred thousand picked horsemen, and for seven days neither side could help the other. He secretly sent rich gifts to Modu's consort, who persuaded Modu to let him go. For decades afterwards Han kept the peace with marriage alliances and yearly gifts.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十 匈奴列傳
passages.textZh: 冒頓匿其精兵，見其羸弱，於是漢悉兵，多步兵，三十二萬，北逐之。高帝先至平城，步兵未盡到，冒頓縱精兵四十萬騎圍高帝於白登，七日，漢兵中外不得相救餉。
passages.textEn: Modu hid his best troops and showed only the weak, so Han sent its whole army — mostly infantry, three hundred and twenty thousand men — north in pursuit. Gaodi reached Pingcheng first, before all his infantry had arrived, and Modu let loose four hundred thousand picked horsemen and surrounded him at Baideng. For seven days the Han troops inside and outside could neither help nor supply each other.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十 匈奴列傳
passages.textZh: 高帝乃使使閒厚遺閼氏
passages.textEn: Gaodi then secretly sent an envoy with rich gifts to the consort

summary.zh: 漢武帝派張騫出使大月氏，欲聯合夾擊匈奴。張騫途中被匈奴扣留十餘年，逃脫後經大宛、康居到達大月氏，又至大夏。大月氏已無意報仇，張騫歸途再被匈奴所得，前126年才逃回長安：出發時百餘人，去十三歲，唯二人得還。他帶回的西方見聞，開啟了漢與西域的往來。
summary.en: Emperor Wu sent Zhang Qian to the Great Yuezhi to win them as allies against the Xiongnu. Held by the Xiongnu for more than ten years, he escaped and went on through Dayuan and Kangju to the Yuezhi and to Daxia. The Yuezhi had no wish for revenge; captured again on the way back, he only reached Chang'an in 126 BCE — of more than a hundred who set out, two came back after thirteen years. What he reported opened the way between Han and the west.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十三 大宛列傳
passages.textZh: 初，騫行時百餘人，去十三歲，唯二人得還。
passages.textEn: When Qian first set out he had over a hundred men; after thirteen years away, only two came back.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十三 大宛列傳
passages.textZh: 騫身所至者大宛、大月氏、大夏、康居，而傳聞其旁大國五六，具為天子言之。
passages.textEn: The places Qian reached himself were Dayuan, the Great Yuezhi, Daxia and Kangju; he had heard of five or six other great states round about, and described them all to the Son of Heaven.

summary.zh: 驃騎將軍霍去病出隴西，越烏盭，轉戰六日，過焉支山千餘里，殺折蘭王，斬盧胡王，俘渾邪王子及相國、都尉，首虜八千餘級，收休屠王祭天金人。同年夏再擊匈奴，秋渾邪王殺休屠王，率眾降漢，河西走廊歸漢，後設武威、酒泉等郡。
summary.en: Huo Qubing, General of Swift Cavalry, struck from Longxi over the Wuli, fought for six days and went more than a thousand li past Mount Yanzhi, killing the King of Zhelan and the King of Luhu, capturing the son of the Hunye King with his chancellor and commandants, taking over eight thousand heads and prisoners and seizing the golden man the Xiutu King used to worship Heaven. He struck again that summer; in autumn the Hunye King killed the Xiutu King and came over to Han with his people, and the Hexi corridor became Han land, later organised as Wuwei, Jiuquan and other commanderies.

label.en: From Beidi to the Qilian Mountains

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十一 衛將軍驃騎列傳
passages.textZh: 驃騎將軍率戎士踰烏盭，討遬濮，涉狐奴，歷五王國，輜重人眾懾慴者弗取，冀獲單于子。轉戰六日，過焉支山千有餘里，合短兵，殺折蘭王，斬盧胡王，誅全甲，執渾邪王子及相國、都尉，首虜八千餘級，收休屠祭天金人，益封去病二千戶。
passages.textEn: "The General of Swift Cavalry led his men over the Wuli, punished the Supu, crossed the Hunu and passed through five kingdoms, sparing the cowed baggage trains and people in hope of taking the Chanyu's son. He fought for six days and went more than a thousand li beyond Mount Yanzhi; at close quarters he killed the King of Zhelan and beheaded the King of Luhu, destroyed their armoured men, captured the son of the Hunye King with his chancellor and commandants, took over eight thousand heads and prisoners and seized the golden man the Xiutu King used to worship Heaven. Qubing's fief is increased by two thousand households."

confidenceNote.zh: 狼居胥山的位置不能確定，一般認為在今蒙古國肯特山一帶；「瀚海」指何處亦有爭論。
confidenceNote.en: Mount Langjuxu cannot be located with certainty — usually placed in the Khentii range of Mongolia; what the "Hanhai" was is also debated.

summary.zh: 漢武帝派衛青、霍去病各率五萬騎深入漠北。霍去病出代郡，「絕大幕」，俘獲屯頭王、韓王等三人及將軍、相國等八十三人，「封狼居胥山，禪於姑衍，登臨翰海」。衛青出定襄，擊敗單于主力。此後「匈奴遠遁，而幕南無王庭」。
summary.en: Emperor Wu sent Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, each with fifty thousand horsemen, deep beyond the desert. Huo Qubing struck from Dai, "crossed the great desert", captured three kings and eighty-three generals and ministers, "performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Langjuxu and the shan at Guyan, and looked out over the Hanhai". Wei Qing, striking from Dingxiang, beat the Chanyu's main army. Afterwards the Xiongnu withdrew far north and kept no royal camp south of the desert.

passages.sourceEn: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian, c. 91 BCE)
passages.locator: 卷一百一十一 衛將軍驃騎列傳
passages.textZh: 驃騎將軍去病率師，躬將所獲葷粥之士，約輕齎，絕大幕，涉獲章渠，以誅比車耆，轉擊左大將，斬獲旗鼓，歷涉離侯。濟弓閭，獲屯頭王、韓王等三人，將軍、相國、當戶、都尉八十三人，封狼居胥山，禪於姑衍，登臨翰海。
passages.textEn: "Qubing, General of Swift Cavalry, led the army himself, with Xunyu men he had captured, carrying light supplies; he crossed the great desert, forded the Zhangqu to punish Biju'qi, turned to attack the Left General, seized his banners and drums, crossed the Lihou, forded the Gonglü, captured three kings including the Tuntou and Han kings, and eighty-three generals, chancellors, danghu and commandants; he performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Langjuxu and the shan sacrifice at Guyan, and climbed up to look over the Hanhai."

summary.zh: 漢平定南越，以其地設南海、蒼梧、鬱林、合浦、交阯、九真、日南、珠崖、儋耳九郡；又平定西南夷，設武都、牂柯、越嶲、沈黎、文山郡。
summary.en: Han conquered Nanyue and made its land into nine commanderies — Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, Hepu, Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, Rinan, Zhuya and Dan'er; it also settled the south-western peoples and created the commanderies of Wudu, Zangke, Yuexi, Shenli and Wenshan.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷六 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 遂定越地，以為南海、蒼梧、鬱林、合浦、交阯、九真、日南、珠崖、儋耳郡。定西南夷，以為武都、牂柯、越嶲、沈黎、文山郡。
passages.textEn: Then the land of Yue was settled and made into the commanderies of Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, Hepu, Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, Rinan, Zhuya and Dan'er. The south-western peoples were settled and made into the commanderies of Wudu, Zangke, Yuexi, Shenli and Wenshan.

summary.zh: 漢武帝派樓船將軍楊僕、左將軍荀彘率應募的罪人攻打朝鮮。次年夏，朝鮮人殺其王右渠投降，漢以其地設樂浪、臨屯、玄菟、真番四郡。
summary.en: Emperor Wu sent Yang Pu, General of the Towered Ships, and Xun Zhi, General of the Left, with convict volunteers against Chaoxian. The next summer the people of Chaoxian killed their king Youqu and surrendered, and Han made their land into four commanderies: Lelang, Lintun, Xuantu and Zhenfan.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷六 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 遣樓船將軍楊僕、左將軍荀彘將應募罪人擊朝鮮。
passages.textEn: He sent Yang Pu, General of the Towered Ships, and Xun Zhi, General of the Left, with convicts who had volunteered, to attack Chaoxian.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷六 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 夏，朝鮮斬其王右渠降，以其地為樂浪、臨屯、玄菟、真番郡。
passages.textEn: In summer the people of Chaoxian beheaded their king Youqu and surrendered; their land was made into the commanderies of Lelang, Lintun, Xuantu and Zhenfan.

summary.zh: 元封五年，漢武帝「初置刺史部十三州」，把天下分為十三個監察區，各派刺史巡察所部郡國。東漢以後州逐漸成為郡之上的一級行政區；本圖三國時期的州界即沿此而來。
summary.en: In 106 BCE Emperor Wu "for the first time set up the thirteen inspection provinces", dividing the realm into thirteen regions, each with an inspector to tour its commanderies and kingdoms. From Eastern Han on the provinces gradually became an administrative level above the commanderies; the provincial borders on this atlas's Three Kingdoms map descend from them.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷六 武帝紀
passages.textZh: 初置刺史部十三州。
passages.textEn: For the first time the thirteen inspection provinces under regional inspectors were set up.

names.name: The Protectorate of the Western Regions

summary.zh: 神爵二年，匈奴日逐王背叛單于，率眾降漢，護鄯善以西使者鄭吉迎接。漢封日逐王為歸德侯、鄭吉為安遠侯，並使鄭吉兼護北道，號為都護——「都護之起，自吉置矣」。匈奴的僮僕都尉因此撤銷，匈奴勢力退出西域。
summary.en: In the second year of Shenjue the Rizhu King rebelled against the Chanyu and came over to Han, received by Zheng Ji, envoy protecting the lands west of Shanshan. Han made the Rizhu King a marquis and Zheng Ji Marquis Who Pacified the Distant, and put Ji in charge of the Northern Road as well, with the title Protector-General — "the protectorate began with Ji". The Xiongnu officer who had ruled the region was withdrawn, and Xiongnu power left the Western Regions.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷九十六上 西域傳上
passages.textZh: 其後日逐王畔單于，將眾來降，護鄯善以西使者鄭吉迎之。既至漢，封日逐王為歸德侯，吉為安遠侯。是歲，神爵二年也。乃因使吉並護北道，故號曰都護。都護之起，自吉置矣。僮僕都尉由此罷，匈奴益弱，不得近西域。
passages.textEn: Later the Rizhu King rebelled against the Chanyu and came over with his people; Zheng Ji, envoy protecting the lands west of Shanshan, received him. When they reached Han the Rizhu King was made Marquis Who Turned to Virtue and Ji Marquis Who Pacified the Distant. That was the second year of Shenjue. Ji was then made to protect the Northern Road as well, and so was called Protector-General. The protectorate began with Ji. The Xiongnu commandant in charge of slaves was abolished, and the Xiongnu grew weaker and could no longer come near the Western Regions.

names.name: Wang Zhaojun goes to the Xiongnu

summary.zh: 竟寧元年，匈奴呼韓邪單于再度入朝，自言願為漢婿，漢元帝以後宮良家子王嬙（字昭君）賜之。昭君號寧胡閼氏，生一男伊屠智牙師，為右日逐王。
summary.en: In 33 BCE the Huhanye Chanyu came to court again and asked to marry into the Han house; Emperor Yuan gave him the palace lady Wang Qiang (Zhaojun). She was titled Ninghu Yanzhi and bore a son, Yitu Zhiyashi, who became the Right Rizhu King.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷九十四下 匈奴傳下
passages.textZh: 竟寧元年，單于復入朝，禮賜如初，加衣服錦帛絮，皆倍於黃龍時。單于自言願婿漢氏以自親。元帝以後宮良家子王牆字昭君賜單于。
passages.textEn: In the first year of Jingning the Chanyu came to court again and was received and rewarded as before, with twice the clothes, brocade, silk and floss of the Huanglong visit. The Chanyu said he wished to become a son-in-law of the house of Han, to draw closer to it. Emperor Yuan gave the Chanyu Wang Qiang, courtesy name Zhaojun, a good-family girl of the rear palace.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷九十四下 匈奴傳下
passages.textZh: 王昭君號寧胡閼氏，生一男伊屠智牙師，為右日逐王。
passages.textEn: Wang Zhaojun was titled Ninghu Yanzhi — "Consort who brings peace to the Hu". She bore a son, Yitu Zhiyashi, who became the Right Rizhu King.

names.name: Wang Mang founds the Xin dynasty

summary.zh: 王莽「即真天子位，定有天下之號曰新」，改正朔、易服色、變犧牲、殊徽幟，以十二月朔癸酉為始建國元年正月初一。西漢至此結束。
summary.en: Wang Mang "took the throne as true Son of Heaven and fixed the name of the realm as Xin", changing the calendar, the colours of dress, the sacrificial animals and the banners, and making the first day of the twelfth month the New Year's Day of the first year of Shijianguo. The Western Han ended.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Han (Ban Gu, c. 111)
passages.locator: 卷九十九上 王莽傳上
passages.textZh: 以戊辰直定，御王冠，即真天子位，定有天下之號曰新。其改正朔，易服色，變犧牲，殊徽幟，異器制。以十二月朔癸酉為建國元年正月之朔，以雞鳴為時。
passages.textEn: "On the day wuchen, under the sign ding, I put on the royal cap and take the throne as true Son of Heaven, and fix the name of the realm as Xin. The calendar is changed, the colours of dress altered, the sacrificial animals changed, the banners made different and the vessels of a new pattern. The first day of the twelfth month, guiyou, shall be the first day of the first month of the first year of Shijianguo, and the day shall begin at cockcrow."

confidenceNote.zh: 引文中刪去了李賢等人的夾注（以「……」表示）。
confidenceNote.en: Li Xian's interlinear commentary has been left out of the quotations (marked "……").

summary.zh: 王莽派大司徒王尋、大司空王邑率號稱百萬之眾（甲士四十二萬）南下。劉秀率敢死者三千人從城西水上衝擊其中軍，王尋、王邑陣亂，漢軍乘勢殺王尋，城中守軍也鼓譟而出，內外夾擊，莽軍大潰，奔逃者互相踐踏，倒斃百餘里。
summary.en: Wang Mang sent his Grand Ministers Wang Xun and Wang Yi south with an army called a million strong, four hundred and twenty thousand of them armoured. Liu Xiu, with three thousand men ready to die, charged their centre from the river west of the city; their lines broke, Wang Xun was killed, and the garrison came out drumming and shouting. Caught between them, Wang Mang's army collapsed, the fleeing men trampling one another and falling dead for more than a hundred li.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷一 光武帝紀上
passages.textZh: 莽聞阜、賜死，漢帝立，大懼，遣大司徒王尋、大司空王邑……將兵百萬，其甲士四十二萬人，五月，到潁川，復與嚴尤、陳茂合。
passages.textEn: When Wang Mang heard that Zhen Fu and Liang Qiu Ci were dead and a Han emperor had been set up, he was much afraid and sent the Grand Minister over the Masses Wang Xun and the Grand Minister of Works Wang Yi with an army of a million, four hundred and twenty thousand of them armoured men. In the fifth month they reached Yingchuan and joined Yan You and Chen Mao. [Li Xian's commentary omitted.]

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷一 光武帝紀上
passages.textZh: 光武乃與敢死者三千人，從城西水上衝其中堅，……尋、邑陳亂，乘銳崩之，遂殺王尋。城中亦鼓譟而出，中外合埶，震呼動天地，莽兵大潰，走者相騰踐，奔殪百餘里閒。
passages.textEn: Then Guangwu, with three thousand men ready to die, charged from the river west of the city into the enemy's centre. Wang Xun and Wang Yi's lines fell into disorder; riding the momentum, they broke them and killed Wang Xun. The garrison too came out drumming and shouting; inside and outside joined forces, their shouts shook heaven and earth, and Wang Mang's army collapsed, the fleeing men trampling one another and falling dead for more than a hundred li. [Commentary omitted.]

names.name: Ban Chao in the Western Regions

summary.zh: 班超出使西域，在鄯善遇到匈奴使者，鄯善王態度轉冷。班超對部下說：「不入虎穴，不得虎子。」夜裡以火攻殺匈奴使者，鄯善震恐降服。此後班超經營西域近三十年，官至西域都護。
summary.en: Sent to the Western Regions, Ban Chao found a Xiongnu embassy at Shanshan and the king turning cold. He told his men: "If you do not enter the tiger's den you cannot take the tiger's cub," attacked the Xiongnu envoys with fire by night and killed them, and Shanshan submitted in terror. He spent nearly thirty years in the Western Regions, becoming Protector-General.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 班梁列傳
passages.textZh: 超曰：「不入虎穴，不得虎子。當今之計，獨有因夜以火攻虜，使彼不知我多少，必大震怖，可殄盡也。滅此虜，則鄯善破膽，功成事立矣。」
passages.textEn: Chao said: "If you do not enter the tiger's den you cannot take the tiger's cub. The only plan now is to attack the barbarians with fire by night, so they cannot tell how many we are; they will be thrown into terror and we can destroy them all. Once they are wiped out, Shanshan's nerve will break, and our task will be done."

confidenceNote.zh: 2017年中蒙考古隊在蒙古國中戈壁省杭愛山支脈發現這處摩崖石刻，文字與《後漢書》所載班固銘文大體相合。
confidenceNote.en: In 2017 a Chinese–Mongolian team found the inscription on a cliff in Dundgovi province, Mongolia; its text broadly matches Ban Gu's as given in the Book of the Later Han.

summary.zh: 車騎將軍竇憲與執金吾耿秉大破北匈奴，單于遁走，漢軍追擊至私渠比鞮海，斬名王以下一萬三千級，獲牲畜百餘萬頭，八十一部二十餘萬人投降。竇憲、耿秉登燕然山，在離邊塞三千餘里處刻石記功，由班固作銘。
summary.en: Dou Xian, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Geng Bing crushed the Northern Xiongnu; the Chanyu fled and the Han army pursued to the Siqu Biti sea, beheading thirteen thousand from the named kings down and taking over a million animals, while eighty-one tribes — over two hundred thousand people — surrendered. Dou Xian and Geng Bing climbed Mount Yanran, three thousand li beyond the frontier, and carved their victory in the rock, with an inscription by Ban Gu.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷二十三 竇融列傳 附竇憲
