passages.textZh: 虜眾崩潰，單于遁走，追擊諸部，遂臨私渠比鞮海。斬名王以下萬三千級，獲生口馬、牛、羊、橐駝百餘萬頭。於是溫犢須、曰逐、溫吾、夫渠王柳鞮等八十一部率眾降者，前後二十餘萬人。憲、秉遂登燕然山，去塞三千餘里，刻石勒功，紀漢威德，令班固作銘曰
passages.textEn: The enemy host collapsed and the Chanyu fled. They pursued the tribes as far as the Siqu Biti sea, beheaded thirteen thousand men from the named kings down, and took more than a million captives, horses, cattle, sheep and camels. Then eighty-one tribes under the Wendushu, Rizhu and Wenwu kings, Liudi King of Fuqu and others surrendered with their people, over two hundred thousand in all. Xian and Bing then climbed Mount Yanran, more than three thousand li beyond the frontier, carved their deeds in stone to record the might and virtue of Han, and had Ban Gu compose the inscription, which reads…

confidenceNote.zh: 原器不存。今日常見的模型是1950年代王振鐸的復原設計，其內部機構今人仍有不同看法。
confidenceNote.en: The instrument is lost. The familiar model is Wang Zhenduo's reconstruction of the 1950s; how the mechanism worked is still argued.

summary.zh: 陽嘉元年，太史令張衡造候風地動儀：以精銅鑄成，直徑八尺，形似酒尊，飾以篆文與山龜鳥獸；內有都柱，旁出八道，設有機關；外有八龍口銜銅丸，下有蟾蜍張口承接。某方地動，該方龍口吐丸，落入蟾蜍口中，從而知道地震的方向。
summary.en: In 132 the Grand Astrologer Zhang Heng built his instrument for the winds and the movements of the earth: cast in fine bronze, eight chi across, shaped like a wine jar and decorated with seal script, mountains, tortoises, birds and beasts; inside a central pillar with eight channels and a trigger mechanism; outside, eight dragons holding bronze balls above eight toads with open mouths. When the earth moved, the dragon facing that way dropped its ball into the toad's mouth, showing the direction of the quake.

passages.sourceEn: Book of the Later Han (Fan Ye, 445)
passages.locator: 卷五十九 張衡列傳
passages.textZh: 陽嘉元年，復造候風地動儀。以精銅鑄成，員徑八尺，合蓋隆起，形似酒尊，飾以篆文山龜鳥獸之形。中有都柱，傍行八道，施關發機。外有八龍，首銜銅丸，下有蟾蜍，張口承之。其牙機巧制，皆隱在尊中，覆蓋周密無際。如有地動，尊則振龍機發吐丸，而蟾蜍銜之。振聲激揚，伺者因此覺知。雖一龍發機，而七首不動，尋其方面，乃知震之所在。驗之以事，合契若神。
passages.textEn: In the first year of Yangjia he also made an instrument for observing the winds and the movements of the earth. It was cast in fine bronze, eight chi across, with a domed lid, shaped like a wine jar and decorated with seal characters and figures of mountains, tortoises, birds and beasts. Inside was a central pillar, with eight channels running out from it and a trigger mechanism. Outside were eight dragons holding bronze balls in their mouths, and below them toads with open mouths to catch them. The cunning mechanism was all hidden inside the jar, closely covered without a gap. When the earth moved, the jar shook a dragon's trigger and it let fall its ball, which the toad caught. The ringing sound alerted the watchers. Though one dragon's mechanism was set off, the other seven heads did not move; from its direction one knew where the earthquake was. Tested against events, it matched them as if by magic.

summary.zh: 大業元年三月，隋煬帝發河南諸郡男女百餘萬人開通濟渠，從西苑引穀水、洛水入黃河，又從板渚引黃河水通淮河。其後又開永濟渠（608）、江南河（610），形成以洛陽為中心、北抵涿郡、南達餘杭的運河系統。
summary.en: In the third month of 605 Emperor Yang of Sui called up more than a million men and women of the commanderies south of the Yellow River to dig the Tongji Canal, carrying the Gu and Luo from the Western Park to the Yellow River, and the Yellow River from Banzhu through to the Huai. The Yongji Canal (608) and the Jiangnan Canal (610) followed, making a system centred on Luoyang that reached north to Zhuo commandery and south to Yuhang.

label.en: Gu and Luo to the Yellow River

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷三 煬帝紀上
passages.textZh: 辛亥，發河南諸郡男女百餘萬，開通濟渠，自西苑引穀、洛水達于河，自板渚引河通于淮。
passages.textEn: On xinhai more than a million men and women of the commanderies south of the Yellow River were called up to dig the Tongji Canal, carrying the Gu and Luo rivers from the Western Park to the Yellow River, and the Yellow River from Banzhu through to the Huai.

summary.zh: 大業八年，隋煬帝親征高句麗，大軍「總一百一十三萬三千八百，號二百萬，其餽運者倍之」，首尾四十日才發盡，旌旗亙千里。遠征以慘敗告終：宇文述等九軍渡遼者三十萬五千人，還至遼東城時僅存二千七百人。此後兩年再征，民怨沸騰，隋末大亂由此而起。
summary.en: In 612 Emperor Yang led the invasion of Goguryeo himself: "in all one million one hundred and thirty-three thousand eight hundred men, called two million, with twice as many carrying supplies"; it took forty days for the host to march off, and the banners stretched a thousand li. It ended in disaster: of the 305,000 men of Yuwen Shu's nine armies who crossed the Liao, only 2,700 came back to Liaodong. Two more invasions in the next two years drove the realm to the risings that ended Sui.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷四 煬帝紀下
passages.textZh: 總一百一十三萬三千八百，號二百萬，其餽運者倍之。癸未，第一軍發，終四十日，引師乃盡，旌旗亘千里。近古出師之盛，未之有也。
passages.textEn: In all one million one hundred and thirty-three thousand eight hundred men, called two million, with twice as many carrying supplies. On guiwei the first army set out; it took forty days for the whole host to march off, and the banners stretched a thousand li. In recent ages there had never been so great an expedition.

names.name: Murder of Emperor Yang at Jiangdu

summary.zh: 618年三月，右屯衛將軍宇文化及、虎賁郎將司馬德戡等率驍果軍作亂，攻入江都宮。煬帝崩於溫室，年五十。蕭后令宮人拆床板作棺埋葬。
summary.en: In the third month of 618 Yuwen Huaji, General of the Right Encampment Guard, Sima Dekan and others rose with the Courageous Guards and broke into the palace at Jiangdu. Emperor Yang died in the Warm Chamber at fifty; Empress Xiao had the palace women take apart a bed to make his coffin.

passages.sourceEn: Book of Sui (Wei Zheng et al., 636)
passages.locator: 卷四 煬帝紀下
passages.textZh: 二年三月，右屯衞將軍宇文化及，武賁郎將司馬德戡、元禮，監門直閣裴虔通，將作少監宇文智及，武勇郎將趙行樞，鷹揚郎將孟景，內史舍人元敏，符璽郎李覆、牛方裕，千牛左右李孝本、弟孝質，直長許弘仁、薛世良，城門郎唐奉義，醫正張愷等，以驍果作亂，入犯宮闈。上崩于溫室，時年五十。蕭后令宮人撤牀簀為棺以埋之。
passages.textEn: In the third month of the second year, Yuwen Huaji, General of the Right Encampment Guard, with Sima Dekan and Yuan Li, Pei Qiantong, Yuwen Zhiji, Zhao Xingshu, Meng Jing, Yuan Min, Li Fu, Niu Fangyu, Li Xiaoben and his brother Xiaozhi, Xu Hongren, Xue Shiliang, Tang Fengyi, the physician Zhang Kai and others, rose with the Courageous Guards and broke into the palace. The emperor died in the Warm Chamber, aged fifty. Empress Xiao had the palace women take apart a bed to make a coffin and buried him.

summary.zh: 隋恭帝禪位後，李淵於甲子日即皇帝位於太極殿，大赦天下，改隋義寧二年為唐武德元年。此後經多年征戰才平定各地群雄。
summary.en: After the last Sui emperor abdicated, Li Yuan took the throne in the Taiji Hall on jiazi, proclaimed an amnesty and turned the second year of Yining of Sui into the first year of Wude of Tang. It took years more of war to put down the rival claimants.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一 高祖本紀
passages.textZh: 甲子，高祖即皇帝位於太極殿，命刑部尚書蕭造兼太尉，告於南郊，大赦天下，改隋義寧二年為唐武德元年。
passages.textEn: On jiazi Gaozu took the imperial throne in the Taiji Hall, had the Minister of Justice Xiao Zao act as Grand Commandant to report to Heaven at the southern altar, proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the second year of Yining of Sui into the first year of Wude of Tang.

confidenceNote.zh: 貞觀十七年太宗曾調閱高祖與本朝的實錄，並指示直書「六月四日事」；今人多認為現存官方記載對事件經過有所修飾。
confidenceNote.en: In 643 Taizong had the Veritable Records of his father's reign and his own brought to him and gave instructions on how "the events of the fourth day of the sixth month" were to be written; many historians think the surviving official account was shaped accordingly.

summary.zh: 武德九年六月四日，秦王李世民率長孫無忌、尉遲敬德、房玄齡、杜如晦等在玄武門誅殺太子李建成、齊王李元吉。《舊唐書》說是二人先「謀害太宗」。數日後李世民被立為皇太子，總攬朝政，八月即位。
summary.en: On the fourth day of the sixth month of 626 Li Shimin, Prince of Qin, with Zhangsun Wuji, Yuchi Jingde, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui and others, killed the Crown Prince Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji, Prince of Qi, at the Xuanwu Gate. The Old Book of Tang says the two had first "plotted against Taizong". Days later Li Shimin was made Crown Prince and took over the government, and in the eighth month he took the throne.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷二 太宗本紀上
passages.textZh: 九年，皇太子建成、齊王元吉謀害太宗。六月四日，太宗率長孫無忌、尉遲敬德、房玄齡、杜如晦、宇文士及、高士廉、侯君集、程知節、秦叔寶、段志玄、屈突通、張士貴等於玄武門誅之。甲子，立為皇太子，庶政皆斷決。
passages.textEn: In the ninth year the Crown Prince Jiancheng and Yuanji, Prince of Qi, plotted against Taizong. On the fourth day of the sixth month Taizong, with Zhangsun Wuji, Yuchi Jingde, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Yuwen Shiji, Gao Shilian, Hou Junji, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, Duan Zhixuan, Qutu Tong, Zhang Shigui and others, killed them at the Xuanwu Gate. On jiazi he was made Crown Prince, and all affairs of government were decided by him.

names.name: Li Jing destroys the Eastern Turks

summary.zh: 貞觀四年正月，定襄道行軍總管李靖大破突厥，俘獲隋煬帝蕭皇后及煬帝之孫楊正道。二月甲辰，李靖又破突厥於陰山，頡利可汗輕騎遠遁，不久被擒，東突厥汗國滅亡。
summary.en: In the first month of 630 Li Jing, Field Commander of the Dingxiang route, crushed the Turks and captured Empress Xiao of Sui and Emperor Yang's grandson Yang Zhengdao. On jiachen of the second month he beat the Turks again in the Yin Mountains; Illig Qaghan fled with a few light horsemen, was soon captured, and the Eastern Turkic khaganate came to an end.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷三 太宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 四年春正月乙亥，定襄道行軍總管李靖大破突厥，獲隋皇后蕭氏及煬帝之孫正道，送至京師。
passages.textEn: In the first month of the fourth year, on yihai, Li Jing, Field Commander of the Dingxiang route, crushed the Turks and captured Empress Xiao of Sui and Zhengdao, grandson of Emperor Yang, and sent them to the capital.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷三 太宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 甲辰，李靖又破突厥於陰山，頡利可汗輕騎遠遁。
passages.textEn: On jiachen Li Jing beat the Turks again in the Yin Mountains, and Illig Qaghan fled far away with a few light horsemen.

summary.zh: 唐太宗攻破龜茲後，把安西都護府遷到龜茲都城，以郭孝恪為都護，兼統于闐、疏勒、碎葉，稱為「四鎮」。高宗時一度放棄四鎮、把安西移回西州；其後吐蕃大舉進入，焉耆以西四鎮城堡都被攻陷。四鎮此後幾經得失，8世紀末終為吐蕃所有。
summary.en: When Taizong had beaten Kucha he moved the Anxi Protectorate to its capital, with Guo Xiaoke as Protector, also in charge of Khotan, Kashgar and Suyab — the "Four Garrisons". Gaozong at one point gave them up and moved Anxi back to Xizhou; later Tubo came in force and took every fort west of Karashahr. The garrisons changed hands several times and were lost to Tubo for good at the end of the eighth century.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十八 西戎傳 龜茲
passages.textZh: 先是，太宗既破龜茲，移置安西都護府於其國城，以郭孝恪為都護，兼統於闐、疏勒、碎葉，謂之「四鎮」。高宗嗣位，不欲廣地勞人，復命有司棄龜茲等四鎮，移安西依舊於西州。其後吐蕃大入，焉耆已西四鎮城堡，並為賊所陷。
passages.textEn: Earlier, when Taizong had beaten Kucha, he moved the Anxi Protectorate to its capital, with Guo Xiaoke as Protector, also in charge of Khotan, Kashgar and Suyab — the "Four Garrisons". When Gaozong succeeded he did not want to stretch the realm and burden the people, and had the Four Garrisons abandoned and Anxi moved back to Xizhou. Later Tubo came in great force, and the forts of the Four Garrisons west of Karashahr all fell to them.

summary.zh: 貞觀十五年，唐太宗以文成公主嫁吐蕃贊普弄贊（松贊干布），命江夏郡王李道宗主婚並持節護送。弄贊率部兵駐柏海，親迎於河源，見道宗時執子婿之禮甚恭，並讚嘆唐朝服飾禮儀之美。
summary.en: In 641 Taizong gave Princess Wencheng in marriage to the Tibetan Tsenpo Nongzan (Songtsen Gampo), with Li Daozong, Prince of Jiangxia, presiding and escorting her. Nongzan led his troops to Lake Bo and came himself to meet her at the source of the Yellow River; he behaved towards Daozong with all the respect of a son-in-law, and admired the beauty of Tang dress and ceremony.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十六上 吐蕃傳上
passages.textZh: 貞觀十五年，太宗以文成公主妻之，令禮部尚書、江夏郡王道宗主婚，持節送公主於吐蕃。弄贊率其部兵次柏海，親迎於河源。見道宗，執子婿之禮甚恭。既而嘆大國服飾禮儀之美，俯仰有愧沮之色。
passages.textEn: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan Taizong gave him Princess Wencheng in marriage, and had Daozong, Minister of Rites and Prince of Jiangxia, preside over the wedding and escort the princess to Tubo with the imperial tally. Nongzan [Songtsen Gampo] led his troops to camp at Lake Bo and came himself to meet her at the source of the Yellow River. Meeting Daozong he behaved most respectfully, as a son-in-law should. Then, admiring the beauty of the great country's dress and ceremony, he looked abashed.

summary.zh: 玄奘認為當時佛經譯本多有訛謬，貞觀初隨商人西行求取原本。他經高昌、龜茲，越天山至碎葉，經中亞諸國南下印度，在那爛陀寺學法多年。「在西域十七年，經百余國」，645年回到長安，撰《大唐西域記》十二卷，並主持翻譯佛經。
summary.en: Believing the Buddhist translations full of errors, Xuanzang went west with merchants early in Zhenguan to find the originals. He went by Gaochang and Kucha, over the Tianshan to Suyab, through the states of Central Asia and down into India, where he studied for years at Nalanda. "He was in the west seventeen years and passed through more than a hundred countries"; back in Chang'an in 645 he wrote the Record of the Western Regions in twelve chapters and directed the translation of the sutras.

label.en: Kucha and over the Tianshan to Suyab

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十一 方伎傳 玄奘
passages.textZh: 僧玄奘，姓陳氏，洛州偃師人。大業末出家，博涉經論。嘗謂翻譯者多有訛謬，故就西域，廣求異本以參驗之。貞觀初，隨商人往游西域。玄奘既辯博出群，所在必為講釋論難，蕃人遠近咸尊伏之。在西域十七年，經百余國，悉解其國之語，仍采其山川謠俗，土地所有，撰《西域記》十二卷。
passages.textEn: The monk Xuanzang, surname Chen, was from Yanshi in Luo prefecture. He left home at the end of the Daye era and read widely in the sutras and treatises. Believing the translations full of errors, he went to the Western Regions to search for other texts to compare them with. Early in Zhenguan he travelled west with merchants. His learning and eloquence were outstanding; wherever he went he lectured and debated, and foreigners near and far revered him. He was in the west seventeen years and passed through more than a hundred countries, learning all their languages; he also gathered their landscapes, customs and products, and wrote the Record of the Western Regions in twelve chapters.

summary.zh: 天授元年九月九日，武則天「革唐命，改國號為周」，改元天授，加尊號聖神皇帝，降睿宗為皇嗣，在神都（洛陽）立武氏七廟。705年神龍政變後退位，唐朝復辟。
summary.en: On the ninth day of the ninth month of 690 Wu Zetian "ended the mandate of Tang and changed the name of the state to Zhou", proclaiming the Tianshou era, taking the title Sage and Divine Emperor, reducing Emperor Ruizong to Imperial Heir and setting up the seven ancestral temples of the Wu family in the Divine Capital, Luoyang. She was forced to step down in the coup of 705, and Tang was restored.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷六 則天皇后本紀
passages.textZh: 九月九日壬午，革唐命，改國號為周。改元為天授，大赦天下，賜酺七日。乙酉，加尊號曰聖神皇帝，降皇帝為皇嗣。丙戌，初立武氏七廟於神都。
passages.textEn: On the ninth day of the ninth month, renwu, she ended the mandate of Tang and changed the name of the state to Zhou. The era was changed to Tianshou, there was a general amnesty and seven days of feasting. On yiyou she took the title Sage and Divine Emperor and reduced the emperor to Imperial Heir. On bingxu the seven ancestral temples of the Wu family were first set up in the Divine Capital.

confidenceNote.zh: 《通鑑》作「恆羅斯」。戰場一般認為在今哈薩克塔拉茲與吉爾吉斯交界一帶。
confidenceNote.en: The Comprehensive Mirror writes the name Hengluosi. The battlefield is usually placed near Taraz on the Kazakh–Kyrgyz border.

summary.zh: 高仙芝俘虜石國王後，石國王子逃往諸胡，控訴仙芝欺誘貪暴，諸胡皆怒，暗中招引大食（阿拉伯）想一同進攻安西四鎮。高仙芝率蕃、漢三萬人迎擊大食，深入七百餘里，在怛羅斯城與大食遭遇。相持五日，葛邏祿部眾倒戈，與大食夾攻唐軍，仙芝大敗，士卒幾乎死盡，只剩數千人。
summary.en: Gao Xianzhi had captured the King of Shi (Tashkent); the king's son escaped and told the other Hu peoples of Gao's treachery and greed, and in their anger they secretly called in the Arabs to attack the Four Garrisons with them. Gao led thirty thousand foreign and Han troops against the Arabs, seven hundred li deep, and met them at the city of Talas. After five days the Qarluqs changed sides and attacked the Tang army together with the Arabs; Gao was routed and almost all his men were killed, only a few thousand surviving.

passages.sourceEn: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance (Sima Guang, 1084)
passages.locator: 卷二百一十六 唐紀三十二
passages.textZh: 髙仙芝之虜石國王也，石國王子逃詣諸胡，具告仙芝欺誘貪暴之狀。諸胡皆怒，潛引大食慾共攻四鎭。仙芝聞之，將蕃、漢三萬衆撃大食，深入七百餘里，至恆羅斯城，與大食遇。相持五日，葛羅祿部衆叛，與大食夾攻唐軍，仙芝大敗，士卒死亡略盡，所餘才數千人。
passages.textEn: When Gao Xianzhi captured the King of Shi [Tashkent], the king's son escaped to the other Hu peoples and told them all about Xianzhi's treachery and greed. The Hu were all enraged and secretly brought in the Arabs to attack the Four Garrisons together. Hearing this, Xianzhi led thirty thousand foreign and Han troops against the Arabs, went more than seven hundred li deep and met them at the city of Talas. After five days of stalemate the Qarluq troops changed sides and attacked the Tang army together with the Arabs; Xianzhi was utterly defeated, almost all his men were killed, and only a few thousand were left.

summary.zh: 天寶十四載十一月丙寅，范陽節度使安祿山率蕃、漢之兵十餘萬自幽州南下，以誅楊國忠為名起兵。叛軍攻陷洛陽，次年破潼關、陷長安，玄宗奔蜀。安祿山、史思明父子相繼稱帝，戰亂延續八年，763年史朝義兵敗自殺才告平定。唐朝從此由盛轉衰，河北諸鎮割據自立。
summary.en: On bingyin of the eleventh month of 755 An Lushan, Military Governor of Fanyang, marched south from Youzhou with over a hundred thousand foreign and Han troops in the name of punishing Yang Guozhong. The rebels took Luoyang, broke through Tong Pass the next year and took Chang'an, and Xuanzong fled to Shu. An Lushan, Shi Siming and their sons took the imperial title in turn; the war lasted eight years, until Shi Chaoyi was defeated and killed himself in 763. Tang never recovered its strength, and the provinces of Hebei became virtually independent.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷九 玄宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 丙寅，范陽節度使安祿山率蕃、漢之兵十餘萬，自幽州南向詣闕，以誅楊國忠為名，先殺太原尹楊光翽於博陵郡。
passages.textEn: On bingyin An Lushan, Military Governor of Fanyang, led more than a hundred thousand foreign and Han troops south from Youzhou towards the capital, in the name of punishing Yang Guozhong, first killing Yang Guanghui, Intendant of Taiyuan, at Boling.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷九 玄宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 辛卯，哥舒翰至潼關，為其帳下火拔歸仁以左右數十騎執之降賊，關門不守，京師大駭，河東、華陰、上洛等郡皆委城而走。甲午，將謀幸蜀，乃下詔親征，仗下，從士庶恐駭，奔走於路。乙未，凌晨自延秋門出，微雨沾濕，扈從惟宰相楊國忠、韋見素、內侍高力士及太子，親王，妃主、皇孫已下多從之不及。
passages.textEn: On xinmao Geshu Han reached Tong Pass, where his own officer Huoba Guiren with a few dozen horsemen seized him and went over to the rebels; the pass was lost, the capital was in panic, and Hedong, Huayin, Shangluo and other commanderies abandoned their cities. On jiawu, planning to go to Shu, the emperor issued an edict for a personal campaign; when the court dispersed, officials and commoners fled in terror along the roads. On yiwei at dawn he left by the Yanqiu Gate in a light rain, attended only by the chief ministers Yang Guozhong and Wei Jiansu, the eunuch Gao Lishi and the Crown Prince; most of the princes, consorts, princesses and grandsons could not follow in time.

summary.zh: 潼關失守後，玄宗於六月乙未凌晨出延秋門西逃。丙辰至馬嵬驛，護駕禁軍停步不前，龍武大將軍陳玄禮奏請誅殺楊國忠以平眾怒。楊國忠被殺，楊貴妃亦被賜死。玄宗繼續入蜀，太子則北上靈武即位。
summary.en: After Tong Pass fell Xuanzong fled west at dawn on yiwei of the sixth month by the Yanqiu Gate. On bingchen, at the Mawei post station, his guards halted and would go no further; Chen Xuanli, General of the Dragon-Martial Army, demanded Yang Guozhong's death to calm the men. Yang Guozhong was killed and Consort Yang was made to die too. Xuanzong went on into Shu, while the Crown Prince went north and took the throne at Lingwu.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷九 玄宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 辛卯，哥舒翰至潼關，為其帳下火拔歸仁以左右數十騎執之降賊，關門不守，京師大駭，河東、華陰、上洛等郡皆委城而走。甲午，將謀幸蜀，乃下詔親征，仗下，從士庶恐駭，奔走於路。乙未，凌晨自延秋門出，微雨沾濕，扈從惟宰相楊國忠、韋見素、內侍高力士及太子，親王，妃主、皇孫已下多從之不及。
passages.textEn: On xinmao Geshu Han reached Tong Pass, where his own officer Huoba Guiren with a few dozen horsemen seized him and went over to the rebels; the pass was lost, the capital was in panic, and Hedong, Huayin, Shangluo and other commanderies abandoned their cities. On jiawu, planning to go to Shu, the emperor issued an edict for a personal campaign; when the court dispersed, officials and commoners fled in terror along the roads. On yiwei at dawn he left by the Yanqiu Gate in a light rain, attended only by the chief ministers Yang Guozhong and Wei Jiansu, the eunuch Gao Lishi and the Crown Prince; most of the princes, consorts, princesses and grandsons could not follow in time.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷九 玄宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 丙辰，次馬嵬驛，諸衛頓軍不進。龍武大將軍陳玄禮奏曰：「逆胡指闕，以誅國忠為名，然中外群情，不無嫌怨。今國步艱阻，乘輿震蕩，陛下宜徇群情，為社稷大計，國忠之徒，可置之於法。」
passages.textEn: On bingchen they stopped at the Mawei post station, and the guards halted and would go no further. Chen Xuanli, General of the Dragon-Martial Army, memorialised: "The rebel barbarian marches on the palace in the name of punishing Guozhong, yet at court and in the realm there is no little resentment of him. Now that the state is in peril and Your Majesty's carriage is shaken, Your Majesty should follow the feeling of the men and, for the sake of the dynasty, let Guozhong and his faction be dealt with by the law."

summary.zh: 廣德元年，吐蕃率吐谷渾、党項等二十餘萬眾東進，郭子儀退兵，代宗出奔陝州，長安失守。降將高暉引吐蕃入城，與吐蕃大將馬重英等立廣武王李承宏為帝。郭子儀南保商州；吐蕃在城中十五日後退去，唐軍收復長安。
summary.en: In 763 Tubo, with more than two hundred thousand Tuyuhun and Tangut troops, marched east; Guo Ziyi fell back, Emperor Daizong fled to Shanzhou and the capital was lost. The renegade Gao Hui led Tubo into the city and with the Tubo general Ma Chongying set up Li Chenghong, Prince of Guangwu, as emperor. Guo Ziyi held Shangzhou to the south; after fifteen days in the city Tubo withdrew and Tang retook Chang'an.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十六上 吐蕃傳上
passages.textZh: 吐蕃以吐谷渾、党項羌之眾二十余萬，自龍光度而東。郭子儀退軍，車駕幸陜州，京師失守。降將高暉引吐蕃入上都城，與吐蕃大將馬重英等立故邠王男廣武王承宏為帝，立年號，大赦，署置官員，尋以司封崔瑰等為相。郭子儀退軍南保商州，吐蕃居城十五日退，官軍收上都，以郭子儀為留守。
passages.textEn: Tubo, with more than two hundred thousand Tuyuhun and Tangut troops, crossed east at Longguang. Guo Ziyi fell back, the emperor fled to Shanzhou and the capital was lost. The renegade general Gao Hui led Tubo into the capital, and with the Tubo general Ma Chongying set up Chenghong, Prince of Guangwu, son of the late Prince of Bin, as emperor, with an era name, an amnesty and appointed officials, soon making Cui Gui and others his ministers. Guo Ziyi withdrew south to hold Shangzhou. Tubo stayed in the city fifteen days and left; the government troops retook the capital and Guo Ziyi was made its regent.

summary.zh: 廣明元年十二月三日夜，唐僖宗從開遠門出逃，奔向駱谷；四日黃巢軍至昭應，金吾大將軍張直方率在京官員到灞上迎接；五日黃巢陷京師。入城時尚讓對圍觀百姓說：「黃王為生靈，不似李家不恤汝輩。」黃巢在長安稱帝，國號大齊，883年被唐軍與沙陀李克用逐出。
summary.en: On the night of the third day of the twelfth month of 880 Emperor Xizong slipped out by the Kaiyuan Gate and made for the Luo valley; on the fourth Huang Chao's army reached Zhaoying, where General Zhang Zhifang led the officials left in the capital to welcome it at Bashang; on the fifth the rebels took the capital. Shang Rang told the watching crowds: "King Huang has risen for the people's sake; he is not like the house of Li, which cared nothing for you." Huang Chao took the imperial title as emperor of Great Qi; Tang armies and the Shatuo leader Li Keyong drove him out in 883.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷二百下 黃巢傳
passages.textZh: 十二月三日，僖宗夜自開遠門出，趨駱谷，諸王官屬相次奔命。觀軍容使田令孜、王若儔收合禁軍扈從。四日，賊至昭應，金吾大將軍張直方率在京兩班迎賊灞上。五日，賊陷京師。
passages.textEn: On the third day of the twelfth month Xizong left at night by the Kaiyuan Gate and made for the Luo valley; the princes and officials fled after him one by one. The army supervisor Tian Lingzi and Wang Ruochou gathered the palace troops to escort him. On the fourth the rebels reached Zhaoying, and Zhang Zhifang, General of the Golden Guard, led the officials who remained in the capital to welcome them at Bashang. On the fifth the rebels took the capital.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷二百下 黃巢傳
passages.textZh: 既入春明門，坊市聚觀，尚讓慰曉市人曰：「黃王為生靈，不似李家不恤汝輩，但各安家。」
passages.textEn: When they had come in through the Chunming Gate and the people of the wards and markets crowded to watch, Shang Rang reassured them: "King Huang has risen for the people's sake; he is not like the house of Li, which cared nothing for you. Just stay quietly at home."

summary.zh: 天祐四年四月，宣武軍節度使朱溫（朱全忠）受唐哀帝禪讓。甲子日，宰相張文蔚、楊涉等奉冊寶至汴州金祥殿，朱溫「被袞冕，即皇帝位」，國號梁，唐亡，五代十國開始。
summary.en: In the fourth month of 907 Zhu Wen (Zhu Quanzhong), Military Governor of Xuanwu, accepted the abdication of the last Tang emperor. On jiazi the ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She brought the patents and seals to the Jinxiang Hall at Bianzhou, and Zhu Wen "put on the imperial robes and crown and took the throne", naming his state Liang. Tang was over, and the age of the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms began.

passages.sourceEn: Old History of the Five Dynasties (Xue Juzheng et al., 974)
passages.locator: 卷三 梁書 太祖紀三
passages.textZh: 甲子，張文蔚、楊涉乘輅自上源驛至，從冊寶諸司各備儀衛鹵簿前導，百官從其後，至金祥殿前陳之。王被袞冕，即皇帝位。
passages.textEn: On jiazi Zhang Wenwei and Yang She arrived from the Shangyuan post station in state carriages, the offices carrying the patents and seals leading with their guards and insignia and the officials following, and set them out before the Jinxiang Hall. The prince put on the imperial robes and crown and took the throne.

names.name: The Sixteen Prefectures ceded to the Khitan

summary.zh: 936年後唐河東節度使石敬瑭借契丹兵滅後唐，受契丹冊立為帝（後晉），以割地為酬。938年晉遣趙瑩奉表，以幽、薊、瀛、莫、涿、檀、順、媯、儒、新、武、雲、應、朔、寰、蔚十六州並圖籍獻契丹；契丹升幽州為南京。此後中原王朝失去燕山一線的屏障，直到明代。
summary.en: In 936 Shi Jingtang, Military Governor of Hedong, destroyed the Later Tang with Khitan help and was enthroned by them as emperor of (Later) Jin, promising land in return. In 938 Jin sent Zhao Ying with a memorial presenting the sixteen prefectures — You, Ji, Ying, Mo, Zhuo, Tan, Shun, Gui, Ru, Xin, Wu, Yun, Ying, Shuo, Huan and Yu — with their maps and registers; the Khitan made Youzhou their Southern Capital. The Chinese dynasties lost the barrier of the Yan mountains until the Ming.

passages.sourceEn: History of Liao (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷四 太宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 是月，晉復遣趙瑩奉表來賀，以幽、薊、瀛、莫、涿、檀、順、媯、儒、新、武、雲、應、朔、寰、蔚十六州並圖籍來獻。於是詔以皇都為上京，府曰臨潢。升幽州為南京，南京為東京。
passages.textEn: That month Jin again sent Zhao Ying with a memorial of congratulation, presenting the sixteen prefectures of You, Ji, Ying, Mo, Zhuo, Tan, Shun, Gui, Ru, Xin, Wu, Yun, Ying, Shuo, Huan and Yu, with their maps and registers. An edict then made the imperial capital the Upper Capital, with the prefecture called Linhuang; Youzhou was raised to the Southern Capital, and the old Southern Capital became the Eastern Capital.

passages.sourceEn: New History of the Five Dynasties (Ouyang Xiu, 1053)
passages.locator: 卷七十二 四夷附錄一
passages.textZh: 契丹當莊宗、明宗時攻陷營、平二州，及已立晉，又得鴈門以北幽州節度管內，合一十六州。乃以幽州為燕京，改天顯十一年為會同元年，更其國號大遼，置百官，皆依中國，參用中國之人。
passages.textEn: In the time of Zhuangzong and Mingzong the Khitan had taken Ying and Ping prefectures; once they had set up Jin they also got the lands north of Yanmen and the Youzhou command — sixteen prefectures in all. They then made Youzhou "Yanjing", changed the eleventh year of Tianxian into the first year of Huitong, renamed their state Great Liao, and set up officials all on the Chinese model, employing Chinese among them.

question.zh: 十六州何時、怎樣歸契丹？
question.en: When and how did the sixteen prefectures pass to the Khitan?

claim.zh: 《遼史》記會同元年（938）晉遣趙瑩奉表，以十六州並圖籍來獻。
claim.en: The History of Liao says Jin sent Zhao Ying in 938 to present the sixteen prefectures with their maps and registers.

source.en: History of Liao, Annals of Taizong

accounts.quoteZh: 以幽、薊、瀛、莫、涿、檀、順、媯、儒、新、武、雲、應、朔、寰、蔚十六州並圖籍來獻

claim.zh: 《新五代史》說營、平二州在後唐時已被契丹攻陷，其餘各州是石敬瑭立國時所得，合為十六州；並把改元會同寫作「改天顯十一年」（936），與《遼史》的年份不同。
claim.en: The New History of the Five Dynasties says Ying and Ping had already fallen to the Khitan under the Later Tang and the rest came with the founding of Jin, sixteen in all; it also dates the change to the Huitong era to "the eleventh year of Tianxian" (936), unlike the History of Liao.

source.en: New History of the Five Dynasties, Appendix on the Four Barbarians

accounts.quoteZh: 契丹當莊宗、明宗時攻陷營、平二州

summary.zh: 後周顯德七年正月，殿前都點檢趙匡胤率軍北禦契丹，夜宿陳橋驛。五更時軍士聚集驛門，宣稱要擁立點檢為天子；天明逼入寢所，諸將露刃列於庭中說：「諸軍無主，願策太尉為天子。」趙匡胤還沒回答，「有以黃衣加太祖身」，眾人羅拜高呼萬歲。他回師開封，受周恭帝禪讓，建立宋朝。
summary.en: In the first month of 960 Zhao Kuangyin, Commander of the Palace Army of Later Zhou, marched north against the Khitan and camped at the Chenqiao post station. At the fifth watch the soldiers gathered at the gate declaring they would make him emperor; at dawn the officers pressed into his room with drawn swords: "The armies have no lord. We wish to make the Grand Commandant emperor." Before he could answer, "someone put a yellow garment on him", and they bowed and cried "Ten thousand years". He went back to Kaifeng, took the abdication of the boy emperor of Zhou and founded the Song.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖本紀一
passages.textZh: 夜五鼓，軍士集驛門，宣言策點檢為天子，或止之，眾不聽。遲明，逼寢所，太宗入白，太祖起。諸校露刃列於庭，曰：「諸軍無主，願策太尉為天子。」未及對，有以黃衣加太祖身，眾皆羅拜，呼萬歲，即掖太祖乘馬。
passages.textEn: At the fifth watch of the night the soldiers gathered at the gate of the post station and declared that they would make the Commander of the Palace Army emperor; some tried to stop them, but the crowd would not listen. At dawn they pressed into his bedchamber; Taizong went in to tell him, and Taizu rose. The officers stood in the courtyard with drawn swords and said: "The armies have no lord. We wish to make the Grand Commandant emperor." Before he could answer, someone put a yellow garment on him; they all bowed around him and cried "Ten thousand years!", and helped him onto his horse.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二百五十 石守信傳
passages.textZh: 乾德初，帝因晚朝與守信等飲酒，酒酣，帝曰：「我非爾曹不及此，然吾為天子，殊不若為節度使之樂，吾終夕未嘗安枕而臥。」守信等頓首曰：「今天命已定，誰復敢有異心，陛下何為出此言耶？」帝曰：「人孰不欲富貴，一旦有以黃袍加汝之身，雖欲不為，其可得乎？」守信等謝曰：「臣愚不及此，惟陛下哀矜之。」帝曰：「人生駒過隙爾，不如多積金、市田宅以遺子孫，歌兒舞女以終天年。君臣之間無所猜嫌，不亦善乎？」守信謝曰：「陛下念及此，所謂生死而肉骨也。」明日，皆稱病，乞解兵權，帝從之
passages.textEn: Early in Qiande, after the evening audience, the emperor was drinking with Shixin and the others. When the wine was flowing he said: "Without you I would not be here. But being emperor is not nearly as pleasant as being a military governor — I have not slept easy a single night." Shixin and the others bowed their heads: "Heaven's mandate is settled now — who would dare to think otherwise? Why does Your Majesty say this?" The emperor said: "Who does not want wealth and honour? If one day someone puts the yellow robe on you, then even if you do not want it, how could you refuse?" Shixin and the others bowed: "We are too dull to have thought of this. We beg Your Majesty's pity." The emperor said: "Life passes like a colt glimpsed through a crack. Better to pile up gold and buy fields and houses to leave to your sons and grandsons, and live out your years with singing boys and dancing girls. With no suspicion between lord and subject — would that not be good?" Shixin bowed: "That Your Majesty thinks of this is to raise the dead and put flesh on bones." The next day they all pleaded illness and asked to give up their commands, and the emperor agreed.

question.zh: 加在趙匡胤身上的是「黃衣」還是「黃袍」？
question.en: Was it a "yellow garment" or a "yellow robe"?

claim.zh: 〈太祖本紀〉作「黃衣」。
claim.en: The Annals of Taizu say "a yellow garment".

source.en: History of Song, Annals of Taizu

accounts.quoteZh: 有以黃衣加太祖身

claim.zh: 〈石守信傳〉記太祖對諸將說「一旦有以黃袍加汝之身」，「黃袍加身」的說法由此流行。
claim.en: The biography of Shi Shouxin has Taizu tell his generals "if one day someone puts the yellow robe on you", and the phrase "the yellow robe put on him" became the usual one.

source.en: History of Song, biography of Shi Shouxin

accounts.quoteZh: 一旦有以黃袍加汝之身

note.zh: 兵變是否事先策劃，史家多有懷疑；官方史書強調他是被擁立的。
note.en: Historians have long suspected the mutiny was planned in advance; the official histories stress that he was forced into it.

confidenceNote.zh: 《宋史》繫於「乾德初」（963年前後），李燾《續資治通鑑長編》繫於建隆二年（961）七月；本圖從後者。
confidenceNote.en: The History of Song puts it "early in Qiande" (around 963); Li Tao's Long Draft puts it in the seventh month of 961, which the atlas follows.

summary.zh: 宋太祖在晚朝後與石守信等禁軍大將飲酒，說做皇帝不如做節度使快樂，夜裡從未安枕；又說：「人孰不欲富貴，一旦有以黃袍加汝之身，雖欲不為，其可得乎？」勸他們「多積金、市田宅以遺子孫，歌兒舞女以終天年」。次日諸將皆稱病，請求解除兵權，太祖應允。
summary.en: After an evening audience Taizu of Song drank with Shi Shouxin and his other palace-army generals; being emperor, he said, was not nearly as pleasant as being a military governor, and he never slept easy. Then: "Who does not want wealth and honour? If one day someone puts the yellow robe on you, then even if you do not want it, how could you refuse?" He urged them to "pile up gold and buy fields and houses to leave to your sons, and live out your years with singing boys and dancing girls". The next day they all pleaded illness and asked to give up their commands, and he agreed.

question.zh: 這場宴會真的發生過嗎？
question.en: Did the banquet really happen?

claim.zh: 《宋史》照錄其事。
claim.en: The History of Song records it as fact.

source.en: History of Song, biography of Shi Shouxin (compiled under the Yuan)

accounts.quoteZh: 人生駒過隙爾

claim.zh: 宋初的官方記錄沒有這段對話，故事最早見於北宋中期的筆記（如王曾《王文正公筆錄》、司馬光《涑水記聞》），各本細節不一；今人有認為禁軍將領是陸續被調離、並非一夕之事。
claim.en: The early Song official records do not have the conversation; the story first appears in mid-Northern Song notebooks (such as Wang Zeng's and Sima Guang's), with differing details; some modern historians argue the generals were moved out of their commands gradually, not overnight.

source.en: Northern Song notebooks; modern scholarship

summary.zh: 宋軍自荊湖沿江東下，在采石架設浮橋渡過長江，圍金陵近一年。開寶八年十一月城破，南唐後主李煜出降。此前宋已滅荊南、湖南（963）、後蜀（965）、南漢（971）；其後吳越納土（978），北漢亡（979）。
summary.en: Song armies came down the Yangtze from Jinghu, crossed by a pontoon bridge at Caishi and besieged Jinling for nearly a year. The city fell in the eleventh month of 975 and Li Yu, last ruler of Southern Tang, surrendered. Song had already taken Jingnan and Hunan (963), Later Shu (965) and Southern Han (971); Wuyue surrendered its lands in 978 and Northern Han fell in 979.

confidenceNote.zh: 此條據通行史實整理，原文尚未錄入；歡迎補充出處。
confidenceNote.en: Written from the standard histories; no passage has been entered yet — contributions welcome.

summary.zh: 宋太宗滅北漢後乘勝北攻幽州，圍城不下，在城西北的高梁河被遼將耶律休哥等擊潰，太宗中箭，乘驢車南逃。宋收復燕雲的企圖受挫。
summary.en: Fresh from destroying Northern Han, Emperor Taizong of Song pushed on to besiege Youzhou, but could not take it and was routed on the Gaoliang River north-west of the city by the Liao general Yelü Xiuge and others; wounded by an arrow, he escaped south in a donkey cart. Song's hope of recovering the sixteen prefectures was dashed.

summary.zh: 景德元年遼聖宗與蕭太后大舉南下，宋真宗在寇準等人勸說下親征。遼軍至澶州北，主帥蕭撻凜（撻覽）出陣時中伏弩而死；真宗至澶州，渡河登北城樓撫慰諸軍。十二月遼使來講和，雙方立誓：宋每年給遼絹二十萬匹、銀十萬兩，兩國以兄弟相稱。此後宋遼維持了百餘年的和平。
summary.en: In 1004 Emperor Shengzong of Liao and the Empress Dowager Xiao invaded in force, and Emperor Zhenzong of Song, urged on by Kou Zhun, took the field himself. North of Chanzhou the Liao commander Xiao Talan rode out before his lines and was killed by a hidden crossbow; the emperor reached Chanzhou, crossed the river and climbed the north tower to encourage the troops. In the twelfth month the Liao envoys came to make peace, and the two sides swore an oath: Song would give Liao two hundred thousand bolts of silk and a hundred thousand taels of silver a year, and the two rulers would call each other brothers. The peace lasted more than a century.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷七 真宗本紀二
passages.textZh: 契丹兵至澶州北，直犯前軍西陣，其大帥撻覽耀兵出陣，俄中伏弩死。丙子，帝次澶州，渡河，幸北砦，御城北樓，召諸將撫慰。
passages.textEn: The Khitan army reached the north of Chanzhou and struck straight at the western line of the vanguard; their great commander Talan rode out in front of his lines in display and was soon killed by a hidden crossbow. On bingzi the emperor stopped at Chanzhou, crossed the river, went to the northern stockade, mounted the north tower of the city wall and called the generals to encourage them.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷七 真宗本紀二
passages.textZh: 十二月庚辰朔，日有食之。契丹使韓杞來講和。
passages.textEn: On gengchen, the first day of the twelfth month, there was an eclipse of the sun. The Khitan envoy Han Qi came to make peace.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷七 真宗本紀二
passages.textZh: 乙未，契丹使丁振以誓書來。
passages.textEn: On yiwei the Khitan envoy Ding Zhen came with the sworn letter.

summary.zh: 党項首領元昊於十月十一日在郊壇備禮即皇帝位，「國稱大夏，年號天授禮法延祚」，史稱西夏。他又自製蕃書，命野利仁榮演繹成十二卷，教國人用以紀事，並以之翻譯《孝經》《爾雅》等書。宋拒絕承認，雙方隨即開戰。
summary.en: On the eleventh day of the tenth month the Tangut leader Yuanhao took the throne with full rites at the suburban altar — "the state was named Great Xia, and the era Tianshou Lifa Yanzuo" — the Western Xia. He also devised a native script, which Yeli Renrong worked up into twelve chapters, taught his people to keep records in it and had the Classic of Filial Piety, the Erya and other books translated. Song refused to recognise him, and war followed.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百八十五 夏國傳上
passages.textZh: 遂以十月十一日郊壇備禮，為世祖始文本武興法建禮仁孝皇帝，國稱大夏，年號天授禮法延祚。
passages.textEn: [Yuanhao's memorial to Song:] "So on the eleventh day of the tenth month, with full rites at the suburban altar, I became the Emperor Shiwen Benwu Xingfa Jianli Renxiao, the state was named Great Xia, and the era Tianshou Lifa Yanzuo."

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百八十五 夏國傳上
passages.textZh: 元昊自製蕃書，命野利仁榮演繹之，成十二卷，字形體方整類八分，而畫頗重複。教國人紀事用蕃書，而譯孝經、爾雅、四言雜字為蕃語。
passages.textEn: Yuanhao devised a native script himself and had Yeli Renrong elaborate it, in twelve chapters; the characters were square like the bafen style of clerical script, but with many strokes repeated. He taught his people to keep records in the native script, and had the Classic of Filial Piety, the Erya and the Four-Character Miscellany translated into the native language.

summary.zh: 宋神宗任用王安石，設制置三司條例司，陸續推行農田水利、青苗、均輸、保甲、免役、市易、保馬、方田等法，「號為新法」，派提舉官四十餘人頒行天下。青苗法以常平倉的本錢作青苗錢貸給民戶，取息二分，春貸秋還。新法在朝中引發激烈的新舊黨爭，神宗死後大多被廢除。
summary.en: Emperor Shenzong put Wang Anshi in charge; a new fiscal commission launched, one after another, the measures for farmland and water works, green-sprout loans, equitable transport, mutual security, hired service, state trade, horse-rearing and land survey — "called the New Laws" — and more than forty commissioners were sent out to enforce them. The green-sprout law lent the granary funds to households at two-tenths interest, paid out in spring and collected in autumn. The New Laws split the court into bitterly opposed factions, and most were repealed after Shenzong's death.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百二十七 王安石傳
passages.textZh: 而農田水利、青苗、均輸、保甲、免役、市易、保馬、方田諸役相繼並興，號為新法，遣提舉官四十餘輩，頒行天下。青苗法者，以常平糴本作青苗錢，散與人戶，令出息二分，春散秋斂。
passages.textEn: Then the measures for farmland and water works, green-sprout loans, equitable transport, mutual security, hired service, state trade, horse-rearing and land survey were launched one after another, called the New Laws, and more than forty commissioners were sent out to put them into force across the realm. The green-sprout law took the price-stabilisation funds as "green-sprout money" and lent it to households at two-tenths interest, paid out in spring and collected in autumn.

summary.zh: 元豐二年，御史李定、舒亶、何正臣摘取蘇軾謝表中的語句，又羅織他的詩作，指為譏謗朝政，把他逮捕押入御史臺獄，欲置之死地，審訊許久不決。神宗獨憐之，從輕發落，貶為黃州團練副使安置。蘇軾在黃州築室於東坡，自號東坡居士。
summary.en: In 1079 the censors Li Ding, Shu Dan and He Zhengchen picked phrases from Su Shi's memorial of thanks and twisted his poems into slander of the government; he was arrested and taken to the Censorate prison, and they wanted him put to death, but the case dragged on. Shenzong alone pitied him and let him off lightly, sending him to Huangzhou as a Deputy Militia Commissioner under supervision. There Su built a house on the eastern slope and called himself Dongpo.

label.en: Taken from Huzhou to the capital

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百三十八 蘇軾傳
passages.textZh: 徙知湖州，上表以謝。又以事不便民者不敢言，以詩託諷，庶有補於國。御史李定、舒亶、何正臣摭其表語，並媒蘖所爲詩以爲訕謗，逮赴臺獄，欲置之死，鍛煉久之不決。神宗獨憐之，以黃州團練副使安置。軾與田父野老，相從溪山間，築室於東坡，自號「東坡居士」。
passages.textEn: Moved to Huzhou, he sent up a memorial of thanks. Since he dared not speak openly of the things that harmed the people, he hinted at them in poems, hoping to help the state. The censors Li Ding, Shu Dan and He Zhengchen picked out phrases from his memorial and twisted his poems into slander; he was arrested and taken to the Censorate prison, and they wanted him put to death, but the case dragged on undecided. Shenzong alone pitied him and had him sent to Huangzhou as Deputy Militia Commissioner under supervision. There Shi went about the streams and hills with old farmers, built a house on the eastern slope and called himself "the Retired Scholar of the Eastern Slope" — Dongpo.

summary.zh: 收國元年正月初一，女真完顏部首領阿骨打即皇帝位。他說遼以賓鐵為號取其堅固，但賓鐵終會變壞，「惟金不變不壞」，金色白而完顏部尚白，於是國號大金，改元收國。數日後親率大軍進攻遼的黃龍府。
summary.en: On the first day of the first month of 1115 Aguda, chief of the Jurchen Wanyan clan, took the throne. Liao, he said, had named itself for fine iron because it was hard; but hard as it is, iron in the end decays — "only gold does not change or decay", and gold is white, the colour the Wanyan honoured. So the state was named Great Jin and the era Shouguo. A few days later he marched on the Liao stronghold of Huanglong.

passages.sourceEn: History of Jin (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷二 太祖本紀
passages.textZh: 收國元年正月壬申朔，群臣奉上尊號。是日，即皇帝位。上曰：「遼以賓鐵爲號，取其堅也。賓鐵雖堅，終亦變壞，惟金不變不壞。金之色白，完顏部色尚白。」于是國號大金，改元收國。丙子，上自將攻黃龍府，進臨益州。
passages.textEn: In the first year of Shouguo, on renshen, the first day of the first month, the ministers presented him with an imperial title, and that day he took the throne. He said: "Liao took its name from fine iron, for its hardness. But hard as fine iron is, in the end it changes and decays; only gold does not change or decay. The colour of gold is white, and the Wanyan tribe honours white." So the state was named Great Jin [Gold], and the era Shouguo. On bingzi the emperor marched in person against Huanglong and advanced to Yizhou.

summary.zh: 靖康元年閏十一月金軍攻破開封。次年三月金人立張邦昌為楚帝，搜取宋宗室；丁巳脅迫太上皇（徽宗）北行，四月庚申把欽宗及皇后、皇太子押往北方，連同法駕鹵簿、禮器、八寶、九鼎、渾天儀、秘閣藏書與天下州府圖等一併擄去。北宋亡。
summary.en: Jin armies broke into Kaifeng in the intercalary eleventh month of 1126. In the third month of 1127 they set up Zhang Bangchang as Emperor of Chu and rounded up the Song imperial clan; on dingsi they forced the Retired Emperor Huizong to go north, and on gengshen of the fourth month carried off Emperor Qinzong with the empress and the crown prince — together with the state carriages and regalia, the ritual vessels, the eight seals, the nine cauldrons, the armillary sphere, the books of the imperial libraries and the maps of every prefecture. The Northern Song was over.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二十三 欽宗本紀
passages.textZh: 丁酉，金人立張邦昌為楚帝。庚子，金人來取宗室，開封尹徐秉哲令民結保，毋藏匿。丁巳，金人脅上皇北行。
passages.textEn: On dingyou the Jin set up Zhang Bangchang as Emperor of Chu. On gengzi the Jin came to take the imperial clansmen, and Xu Bingzhe, Intendant of Kaifeng, ordered the people into mutual-security groups so that none could hide. On dingsi the Jin forced the Retired Emperor to go north.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二十三 欽宗本紀
passages.textZh: 夏四月庚申朔，大風吹石折木。金人以帝及皇后、皇太子北歸。凡法駕、鹵簿，皇后以下車輅、鹵簿，冠服、禮器、法物，大樂、教坊樂器，祭器、八寶、九鼎、圭璧，渾天儀、銅人、刻漏，古器、景靈宮供器，太清樓秘閣三館書、天下州府圖……
passages.textEn: On gengshen, the first day of the fourth month of summer, a great wind blew stones about and broke trees. The Jin took the emperor, the empress and the crown prince back north with them, and with them all the state carriages and processional regalia, the carriages and regalia of the empress and below, the robes, ritual vessels and sacred objects, the court and conservatory instruments, the sacrificial vessels, the eight seals, the nine cauldrons, the jade tablets, the armillary sphere, the bronze acupuncture figure, the clepsydras, the antiques, the vessels of the Jingling Temple, the books of the Taiqing Tower, the Secret Pavilion and the Three Institutes, the maps of all the prefectures of the realm…

names.name: Gaozong takes the throne at Yingtian

summary.zh: 靖康二年五月庚寅朔，康王趙構在應天府登壇受命，禮畢痛哭，遙拜被擄的二帝，即位於府治，改元建炎；大赦，張邦昌及供奉金國之人一律不問。南宋由此開始。
summary.en: On gengyin, the first day of the fifth month of 1127, Zhao Gou, Prince of Kang, ascended the altar at Yingtian prefecture to receive the mandate; when the rite was over he wept and bowed towards the two captive emperors, then took the throne in the prefectural office and proclaimed the Jianyan era, with an amnesty that spared Zhang Bangchang and all who had served the Jin. So began the Southern Song.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷二十四 高宗本紀一
passages.textZh: 五月庚寅朔，帝登壇受命，禮畢慟哭，遙謝二帝，即位於府治。改元建炎。大赦，常赦所不原者咸赦除之。張邦昌及應于供奉金國之人，一切不問。
passages.textEn: On gengyin, the first day of the fifth month, the emperor ascended the altar and received the mandate; when the rite was over he wept bitterly, bowing in the distance to the two emperors, and took the throne in the prefectural office. The era was changed to Jianyan. There was a great amnesty, pardoning even crimes not normally pardoned; Zhang Bangchang and all who had served the Jin were not to be questioned.

summary.zh: 紹興十年金軍毀約南下，岳飛出兵北伐，所遣諸將相繼報捷。大軍駐潁昌，岳飛自率輕騎駐郾城。兀朮（完顏宗弼）認為諸帥易與、唯岳飛難敵，便集中兵力來攻郾城，被岳飛擊敗。不久宋廷連發金字牌命其班師。
summary.en: In 1140 the Jin broke the truce and came south; Yue Fei marched north, and the generals he sent out reported victory after victory. While the main army held Yingchang, Yue Fei held Yancheng with light cavalry. Wuzhu (Wanyan Zongbi), judging the other Song commanders easy to deal with but Yue Fei not, gathered his forces against Yancheng, and was beaten. Soon afterwards the court sent golden tablets one after another ordering Yue Fei back.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百六十五 岳飛傳
passages.textZh: 未幾，所遣諸將相繼奏捷。大軍在潁昌，諸將分道出戰，飛自以輕騎駐郾城，兵勢甚銳。兀朮大懼，會龍虎大王議，以為諸帥易與，獨飛不可當，欲誘致其師，併力一戰。
passages.textEn: Before long the generals he had sent out reported victory one after another. The main army was at Yingchang and the generals went out by separate roads; Fei himself held Yancheng with light cavalry, in high fighting spirit. Wuzhu was greatly alarmed and conferred with the Longhu Prince: the other commanders were easy to deal with, but Fei could not be withstood, so they would lure his army out and fight it with all their strength together.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百六十五 岳飛傳
passages.textZh: 飛大喜，語其下曰：「直抵黃龍府，與諸君痛飲爾！」
passages.textEn: Fei was delighted and said to his officers: "We will drive straight to Huanglong and drink deep there together!"

summary.zh: 紹興十一年宋金議和。宋主趙構向金進誓表稱臣：「今來畫疆，合以淮水中流為界，西有唐、鄧州割屬上國」，「世世子孫，謹守臣節」；並每年向金貢銀、絹各二十五萬兩匹。南北以淮河—大散關一線為界，此後二十年無大戰。
summary.en: In 1141 Song and Jin made peace. The Song ruler Zhao Gou sent a sworn memorial as Jin's subject: "in fixing the border now, it shall run along the middle of the Huai River; to the west, Tang and Deng prefectures are ceded to the superior state", and "for all generations we will keep the duty of subjects"; Song also paid a yearly tribute of 250,000 taels of silver and 250,000 bolts of silk. The line of the Huai and the Dasan Pass divided north from south, and there was no major war for twenty years.

passages.sourceEn: History of Jin (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷七十七 宗弼傳
passages.textZh: 宋主遣端明殿學士何鑄等進誓表，其表曰：「臣構言，今來畫疆，合以淮水中流為界，西有唐、鄧州割屬上國。自鄧州西四十裏並南四十裏為界，屬鄧州。其四十裏外並西南盡屬光化軍，為弊邑沿邊州城。既蒙恩造，許備籓方，世世子孫，謹守臣節。
passages.textEn: The Song ruler sent He Zhu, Academician of the Duanming Hall, and others with a sworn memorial, which said: "Your subject Gou says: in fixing the border now, it shall run along the middle of the Huai River; to the west, Tang and Deng prefectures are ceded to the superior state. Forty li west and forty li south of Dengzhou shall be the line, belonging to Dengzhou; beyond those forty li, to the west and south-west, all belongs to Guanghua Army, as border towns of our humble state. Having received your favour and been allowed to serve as a frontier vassal, we and our sons and grandsons for all generations will keep the duty of subjects."

confidenceNote.zh: 卒於紹興十一年十二月，公曆已入1142年1月。
confidenceNote.en: The twelfth month of 1141 falls in January 1142.

summary.zh: 紹興十一年，岳飛被秦檜等誣以謀反，下大理寺獄，十二月被殺，其子岳雲、部將張憲同死。韓世忠不平，質問秦檜，秦檜答：「飛子雲與張憲書雖不明，其事體莫須有。」韓世忠說：「『莫須有』三字，何以服天下？」
summary.en: In 1141 Yue Fei was framed for treason by Qin Hui and others, imprisoned and put to death in the twelfth month, with his son Yue Yun and his officer Zhang Xian. Han Shizhong, outraged, demanded the facts from Qin Hui, who replied: "Though the letter from Fei's son Yun to Zhang Xian is unclear, the matter is mo xu you — it need not be that it did not happen." Han Shizhong said: "Mo xu you — how can those three words satisfy the realm?"

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百六十五 岳飛傳
passages.textZh: 獄之將上也，韓世忠不平，詣檜詰其實，檜曰：「飛子雲與張憲書雖不明，其事體莫須有。」世忠曰：「『莫須有』三字，何以服天下？」
passages.textEn: When the case was about to be submitted, Han Shizhong, indignant, went to Qin Hui and demanded the facts. Hui said: "Though the letter from Fei's son Yun to Zhang Xian is unclear, the matter is mo xu you — it need not be that it did not happen." Shizhong said: "Mo xu you — how can those three words satisfy the realm?"

summary.zh: 紹興三十一年金主完顏亮大舉南侵，兩淮盡失。十一月金主率大軍至采石，另以兵爭瓜洲。中書舍人虞允文奉命到采石犒師，主將王權已去、新帥李顯忠未到，金騎遍佈江北；虞允文收集散兵，督軍迎戰，擊退渡江的金軍。不久完顏亮在瓜洲被部下所殺，金軍北撤。
summary.en: In 1161 the Jin ruler Wanyan Liang invaded in force and the lands between the Huai and the Yangtze were lost. In the eleventh month he reached Caishi with his main army, sending another force against Guazhou. Yu Yunwen, a secretary sent to reward the troops at Caishi, found Wang Quan gone, his replacement Li Xianzhong not yet arrived and Jin horsemen everywhere; he rallied the scattered men, led them out and threw back the Jin crossing. Soon afterwards Wanyan Liang was murdered by his own officers at Guazhou and the Jin withdrew.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百八十三 虞允文傳
passages.textZh: 十一月壬申，金主率大軍臨采石，而別以兵爭瓜洲。
passages.textEn: On renshen of the eleventh month the Jin ruler arrived at Caishi with his main army, sending another force to fight for Guazhou.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷三百八十三 虞允文傳
passages.textZh: 丙子，允文至采石，權已去，顯忠未來，敵騎充斥。
passages.textEn: On bingzi Yunwen reached Caishi. Wang Quan had already left and Li Xianzhong had not yet come, and the enemy horsemen were everywhere.

summary.zh: 元年丙寅（1206），鐵木真大會諸王群臣，建九游白旗，即皇帝位於斡難河之源，諸王群臣共上尊號曰成吉思皇帝。這一年是金泰和六年。
summary.en: In the first year, bingyin (1206), Temüjin held a great assembly of the princes and ministers, raised the white banner with nine tails and took the throne at the source of the Onon; together they gave him the title Chinggis Emperor. It was the sixth year of Taihe of the Jin.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷一 太祖本紀
passages.textZh: 元年丙寅，帝大會諸王羣臣，建九游白旗，即皇帝位於斡難河之源。諸王羣臣共上尊號曰成吉思皇帝。是歲實金泰和之六年也。
passages.textEn: In the first year, bingyin, the emperor held a great assembly of the princes and ministers, raised the white banner with nine tails, and took the throne at the source of the Onon River. The princes and ministers together gave him the title Chinggis Emperor. That year was in fact the sixth year of Taihe of the Jin.

confidenceNote.zh: 此條據通行史實整理，原文尚未錄入；歡迎補充出處。
confidenceNote.en: Written from the standard histories; no passage has been entered yet — contributions welcome.

summary.zh: 1211年起蒙古屢次南下攻金。1214年金宣宗南遷開封，次年蒙古軍攻陷中都（今北京），金失黃河以北大片土地。
summary.en: From 1211 the Mongols raided Jin again and again. In 1214 Emperor Xuanzong of Jin moved his court south to Kaifeng; the next year the Mongols took Zhongdu (Beijing), and Jin lost most of its land north of the Yellow River.

confidenceNote.zh: 此條據通行史實整理，原文尚未錄入；歡迎補充出處。
confidenceNote.en: Written from the standard histories; no passage has been entered yet — contributions welcome.

summary.zh: 1226年成吉思汗再征西夏，圍中興府（興慶府）。1227年夏末主李晛出降，旋被殺，西夏亡；成吉思汗亦在此役中去世。
summary.en: Chinggis Khan invaded Xi Xia again in 1226 and besieged Zhongxing (Xingqing). In 1227 the last ruler, Li Xian, came out to surrender and was soon killed, and Xi Xia ended; Chinggis himself died during the campaign.

names.name: Siege of Caizhou: the end of Jin

summary.zh: 1233年金哀宗逃入蔡州，蒙古與南宋聯軍圍城。1234年正月，哀宗傳位於宗室完顏承麟，承麟即位後出城禦敵，南城已樹敵旗，敵軍四面殺入；哀宗自縊於幽蘭軒，末帝承麟為亂兵所殺，金亡。
summary.en: In 1233 Emperor Aizong of Jin fled into Caizhou, and a combined Mongol and Song army besieged it. In the first month of 1234 he handed the throne to his kinsman Wanyan Chenglin; as Chenglin went out to fight, enemy banners were already on the south wall and the attackers broke in on every side. Aizong hanged himself in the Youlan Pavilion and the last emperor Chenglin was killed by the soldiery: the end of Jin.

passages.sourceEn: History of Jin (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷十八 哀宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 己亥，上入蔡州，詔尚書省為書召武仙會兵入援。
passages.textEn: On jihai the emperor entered Caizhou and had the Department of State Affairs write to Wu Xian to bring troops to his aid.

passages.sourceEn: History of Jin (Toqto'a et al., 1344)
passages.locator: 卷十八 哀宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 己酉，承麟即皇帝位。百官稱賀。禮畢，亟出捍敵，而南面已立幟。俄頃，四面呼聲震天地。南面守者棄門，大軍入，與城中軍巷戰，城中軍不能禦。帝自縊于幽蘭軒。末帝退保子城，聞帝崩，率群臣入哭，諡曰哀宗。哭奠未畢，城潰，諸禁近舉火焚之。奉禦絳山收哀宗骨瘞之汝水上。末帝為亂兵所害，金亡。
passages.textEn: On jiyou Chenglin took the throne and the officials offered congratulations. The rite over, he hurried out to resist the enemy, but their banners were already raised on the south wall. In a moment shouts shook heaven and earth on all four sides. The defenders of the south gate abandoned it, the great army came in and fought in the streets, and the city's troops could not hold them. The emperor hanged himself in the Youlan Pavilion. The last emperor fell back to the inner citadel; hearing that the emperor was dead he led the ministers in to mourn and gave him the posthumous name Aizong. Before the mourning was done the city fell, and the attendants set fire to the body. The servant Jiang Shan gathered Aizong's bones and buried them by the Ru River. The last emperor was killed by the soldiery, and Jin ended.

summary.zh: 蒙哥汗親征四川，圍攻合州釣魚城，宋將王堅固守。六月蒙軍夜登外城馬軍寨，被王堅擊退，天明遇雨，梯折而止。是月蒙哥不豫，七月崩於釣魚山。蒙古諸王為爭汗位紛紛北返，忽必烈與宋議和北還，南宋又延續了二十年。
summary.en: Möngke Khan led the invasion of Sichuan himself and besieged the Diaoyu fortress at Hezhou, held by the Song general Wang Jian. In the sixth month Mongol troops climbed into the outer cavalry stockade by night but were driven back by Wang Jian; at dawn it rained, the ladders broke and the attack stopped. That month Möngke fell ill, and in the seventh month he died at Diaoyu Mountain. The Mongol princes hurried north to contend for the succession, Khubilai made a truce with Song and went home, and the Southern Song lived on for twenty years more.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷三 憲宗本紀
passages.textZh: 六月丁巳，汪田哥復選兵夜登外城馬軍寨，殺寨主及守城者。王堅率兵來戰。遲明，遇雨，梯折，後軍不克進而止。是月，帝不豫。秋七月辛亥，留精兵三千守之，餘悉攻重慶。癸亥，帝崩于釣魚山，壽五十有二，在位九年。
passages.textEn: On dingsi of the sixth month Wang Tiange again picked men to climb by night into the cavalry stockade of the outer wall, killing its commander and defenders. Wang Jian led his troops out to fight. At dawn it rained, the ladders broke, and the troops behind could not go on, so the attack stopped. That month the emperor fell ill. On xinhai of the seventh month he left three thousand picked men to hold the siege and sent the rest to attack Chongqing. On guihai the emperor died at Diaoyu Mountain, aged fifty-two, in the ninth year of his reign.

question.zh: 蒙哥是病死的，還是被城上炮石所傷？
question.en: Did Möngke die of illness, or of a wound from the fortress?

claim.zh: 《元史》只記他六月「不豫」，七月崩於釣魚山。
claim.en: The History of Yuan says only that he fell ill in the sixth month and died at Diaoyu Mountain in the seventh.

source.en: History of Yuan, Annals of Xianzong

accounts.quoteZh: 是月，帝不豫。

claim.zh: 宋人與後世地方記載說他被城上發出的炮石所傷而死；也有說死於疫病者。
claim.en: Song accounts and later local records say he died of a wound from a missile shot from the walls; others speak of an epidemic.

source.zh: 宋人記載與合川地方志
source.en: Song accounts and Hechuan local records

confidenceNote.zh: 元軍以「回回炮」（配重式投石機）攻城，見《元史》相關列傳。
confidenceNote.en: The Yuan used "Muslim trebuchets" (counterweight trebuchets) in the siege, according to biographies in the History of Yuan.

summary.zh: 至元五年（1268）起元軍圍困襄陽、樊城，築城立寨、斷絕援道。宋軍堅守五年。至元十年（1273）正月，阿里海牙等大舉進攻樊城，攻克之；二月襄陽守將呂文煥懼而請降。長江中游門戶洞開，元軍隨即沿江東下。
summary.en: From 1268 Yuan armies besieged Xiangyang and Fancheng, building forts and cutting off relief. The Song defenders held for five years. In the first month of 1273 Ariq Qaya and others stormed Fancheng and took it; in the second month Lü Wenhuan, commander of Xiangyang, afraid, asked to surrender. The door to the middle Yangtze stood open and the Yuan armies soon came down the river.

passages.sourceEn: History of Yuan (Song Lian et al., 1370)
passages.locator: 卷八 世祖本紀五
passages.textZh: 癸亥，阿里海牙等大攻樊城，拔之，守將呂文煥懼而請降
passages.textEn: On guihai Ariq Qaya and others launched a great assault on Fancheng and took it; the commander Lü Wenhuan, afraid, asked to surrender.
