confidenceNote.en: Written from the standard histories; no passage has been entered yet — contributions welcome.

summary.zh: 德祐二年正月，元丞相伯顏率軍兵臨臨安，太皇太后謝氏與宋恭帝奉表出降；二月元軍入城，三月恭帝等被押往大都。部分大臣擁立益王趙昰、廣王趙昺南走福建、廣東繼續抵抗。
summary.en: In the first month of 1276 the Yuan chancellor Bayan reached Lin'an, and the Grand Empress Dowager Xie and the boy emperor Gongdi sent their surrender; Yuan troops entered in the second month and the emperor was taken to Dadu in the third. Some ministers carried the young princes Zhao Shi and Zhao Bing south to Fujian and Guangdong to fight on.

summary.zh: 祥興元年，宋帝趙昺遷居崖山；元都元帥張弘範、李恒率軍進攻。祥興二年二月宋軍潰敗，翟國秀等解甲投降；黃昏風雨大霧，張世傑與蘇劉義斬斷纜繩，以十餘艘船奪港而去。陸秀夫見帝舟大且被諸舟環結，無法突圍，便背負趙昺投海，後宮與諸臣多從死，七日後海上浮屍十餘萬。楊太后聞訊亦赴海死，張世傑不久自溺，宋亡。
summary.en: In 1278 the boy emperor Zhao Bing moved to Yashan, and the Yuan commanders Zhang Hongfan and Li Heng marched against it. In the second month of 1279 the Song fleet broke; Zhai Guoxiu and others surrendered. As night fell in wind, rain and fog, Zhang Shijie and Su Liuyi cut their moorings and fought their way out with a dozen ships. Lu Xiufei, seeing that the emperor's ship was too large and too tightly lashed to the others to escape, took the boy on his back and leapt into the sea; many of the palace women and ministers followed, and after seven days more than a hundred thousand bodies floated up. Empress Dowager Yang threw herself into the sea when she heard, and Zhang Shijie soon drowned himself. Song was gone.

label.en: Wen Tianxiang (a prisoner with the Yuan fleet)

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 瀛國公本紀 二王附
passages.textZh: 己未，昺徙居崖山，升廣州爲翔龍府。
passages.textEn: On jiwei Bing moved to Yashan, and Guangzhou was raised to Xianglong prefecture.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 瀛國公本紀 二王附
passages.textZh: 己卯，都元帥張弘范、李恒征崖山。
passages.textEn: On jimao the Commanders-in-Chief Zhang Hongfan and Li Heng marched against Yashan.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四十七 瀛國公本紀 二王附
passages.textZh: 諸軍潰，翟國秀及團練使劉俊等解甲降。大軍至中軍，會暮，且風雨，昏霧四塞，咫尺不相辨。世傑乃與蘇劉義斷維，以十餘舟奪港而去，陸秀夫走衛王舟，王舟大，且諸舟環結，度不得出走，乃負昺投海中，後宮及諸臣多從死者，七日，浮屍出於海十餘萬人。楊太后聞昺死，撫膺大慟曰：「我忍死艱關至此者，正爲趙氏一塊肉爾，今無望矣！」遂赴海死，世傑葬之海濱，已而世傑亦自溺死。宋遂亡。
passages.textEn: The armies broke; Zhai Guoxiu, the militia commissioner Liu Jun and others took off their armour and surrendered. When the great army reached the central squadron, night was falling with wind and rain, and a dark fog shut everything in, so that one could not see a foot ahead. Shijie and Su Liuyi cut their moorings and fought their way out of the harbour with a dozen ships. Lu Xiufei went to the Prince of Wei's ship; it was large and lashed in a ring with the others, and judging it could not escape, he took Bing on his back and leapt into the sea. Many of the palace women and ministers died with them; after seven days more than a hundred thousand bodies floated up out of the sea. When Empress Dowager Yang heard that Bing was dead she beat her breast and wailed: "I endured death and hardship to come this far only for this one morsel of Zhao flesh — now there is no hope!" She threw herself into the sea. Shijie buried her on the shore, and soon drowned himself too. And so Song ended.

passages.sourceEn: History of Song (Toqto'a et al., 1345)
passages.locator: 卷四百一十八 文天祥傳
passages.textZh: 天祥至潮陽，見弘範，左右命之拜，不拜，弘範遂以客禮見之，與俱入厓山，使為書招張世傑。天祥曰：「吾不能捍父母，乃教人叛父母，可乎？」索之固，乃書所過《零丁洋詩》與之。其末有云：「人生自古誰無死，留取丹心照汗青。」弘範笑而置之。
passages.textEn: When Tianxiang reached Chaoyang and was brought before Zhang Hongfan, the attendants ordered him to bow; he would not, and Hongfan received him as a guest. Hongfan took him to Yashan and wanted him to write a letter calling on Zhang Shijie to surrender. Tianxiang said: "I could not defend my own parents — shall I now teach others to betray theirs?" Pressed hard, he wrote out the poem he had made crossing the Lingding Sea and gave it to him. It ends: "Since ancient times who has not died? Let me leave a loyal heart to shine in the annals." Hongfan laughed and put it aside.

confidenceNote.zh: 「魏徵等諫阻」與侯君集為主將兩點不在所引文字中。
confidenceNote.en: That Wei Zheng was among those who objected and that Hou Junji led the army are not in the quoted text.

summary.zh: 貞觀十四年，侯君集率軍滅麴氏高昌。大臣魏徵等諫阻在此設州駐兵，太宗不從，以其地置西州，又置安西都護府，留兵鎮守；屯兵可汗浮圖城的西突厥葉護畏懼來降，其地置為庭州。
summary.en: In 640 Hou Junji destroyed the Qu kingdom of Gaochang. Wei Zheng and others advised against making it a prefecture with a garrison; Taizong would not listen, made it Xizhou, set up the Anxi Protectorate and left troops to hold it. The Western Turkic yabghu stationed at the city of Qaghan Stupa came over in fear, and his land became Tingzhou.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十八 西戎傳 高昌
passages.textZh: 太宗不從，竟以其地置西州，又置安西都護府，留兵以鎮之。初，西突厥遣其葉護，屯兵於可汗浮圖城，與高昌相影響，至是懼而來降，以其地為庭州。於是勒石紀功而旋。
passages.textEn: Taizong would not listen, and made the land Xizhou prefecture, set up the Anxi Protectorate and left troops to hold it. The Western Turks had stationed their yabghu with troops at the city of Qaghan Stupa, in league with Gaochang; now, afraid, he came over, and his land was made Tingzhou. Then a stone was carved to record the victory and the army went home.

summary.zh: 貞觀十九年太宗親征高句麗。五月渡遼河，以火箭攻破遼東城；六月至安市城，擊潰十五萬援軍，高延壽等投降，改所駐之山名為駐蹕山並刻石紀功。此後圍攻安市城至九月仍不能下，入冬班師。
summary.en: In 645 Taizong led the invasion of Goguryeo himself. In the fifth month he crossed the Liao and took Liaodong with fire arrows; in the sixth he reached Anshi and routed a relief army of a hundred and fifty thousand, whose commanders Go Yeonsu and others surrendered; the hill he had stood on was renamed Zhubi and a stone carved. But Anshi itself held out through the ninth month, and with winter coming he withdrew.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷三 太宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 五月丁丑，車駕渡遼。甲申，上親率鐵騎與李勣會圍遼東城，因烈風發火弩，斯須城上屋及樓皆盡，麾戰士令登，乃拔之。六月丙辰，師至安市城。丁巳，高麗別將高延壽、高惠真帥兵十五萬來援安市，以拒王師。李勣率兵奮擊，上自高峰引軍臨之，高麗大潰，殺獲不可勝紀。延壽等以其眾降，因名所幸山為駐蹕山，刻石紀功焉。
passages.textEn: On dingchou of the fifth month the emperor crossed the Liao. On jiashen he led his armoured horsemen himself to join Li Ji in besieging Liaodong; in a fierce wind they shot fire arrows, and in moments every roof and tower on the walls was burning; he waved the soldiers up and took the city. On bingchen of the sixth month the army reached Anshi. On dingsi the Goguryeo commanders Go Yeonsu and Go Hyejin came with a hundred and fifty thousand men to relieve Anshi and resist the imperial army. Li Ji attacked hard, the emperor led troops down from a high peak, and Goguryeo broke, with more killed and taken than could be counted. Yeonsu and the others surrendered with their men, and the hill where the emperor had stood was named Zhubi ("where the imperial carriage halted"), with a stone carved to record the victory.

names.name: Su Dingfang against the Western Turks

confidenceNote.zh: 引文只到出兵；擊破賀魯（及次年擒獲）出自通行史實。
confidenceNote.en: The quotations stop at the expedition; the defeat (and capture the next year) of Helu is from the standard histories.

summary.zh: 永徽元年末，瑤池都督阿史那賀魯叛唐，自稱可汗，盡有西域之地。唐軍數度征討不利；顯慶二年（657）正月，高宗命蘇定方等四將軍為伊麗道將軍出兵討伐，同年擊破賀魯，西突厥汗國滅亡，唐在其地分置都護府。
summary.en: At the end of 650 Ashina Helu, Commander-General of Yaochi, rebelled, called himself qaghan and took all the Western Regions. Several Tang expeditions failed; in the first month of 657 Gaozong sent Su Dingfang and three other generals out on the Ili route, and that year they broke Helu. The Western Turkic khaganate came to an end, and Tang set up protectorates over its lands.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷四 高宗本紀上
passages.textZh: 十二月，瑤池都督、沙缽羅葉護阿史那賀魯以府叛，自稱可汗，總有西域之地。
passages.textEn: In the twelfth month Ashina Helu, Commander-General of Yaochi and Ishbara yabghu, rebelled with his command, called himself qaghan and took all the lands of the Western Regions.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷四 高宗本紀上
passages.textZh: 二年春正月庚寅，幸洛陽。命右屯衛將軍蘇定方等四將軍為伊麗道將軍，帥師以討賀魯。
passages.textEn: In the first month of the second year [657], on gengyin, the emperor went to Luoyang. He made Su Dingfang, General of the Right Encampment Guard, and three other generals commanders of the Ili route, to lead an army against Helu.

summary.zh: 顯慶五年八月，蘇定方等攻滅百濟，反綁百濟王扶餘義慈。百濟原有五部、三十七郡、二百城、七十六萬戶，唐以其地分置熊津等五都督府。
summary.en: In the eighth month of 660 Su Dingfang and others conquered Baekje and took King Buyeo Uija with his hands bound. Baekje had five divisions, thirty-seven commanderies, two hundred cities and seven hundred and sixty thousand households; Tang divided its land into five area commands, Ungjin and others.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷四 高宗本紀上
passages.textZh: 八月庚辰，蘇定方等討平百濟，面縛其王扶餘義慈。國分為五部，郡三十七，城二百，戶七十六萬，以其地分置熊津等五都督府。
passages.textEn: On gengchen of the eighth month Su Dingfang and the others conquered Baekje and took its king Buyeo Uija with his hands bound. The kingdom had five divisions, thirty-seven commanderies, two hundred cities and seven hundred and sixty thousand households; its land was divided into five area commands, Ungjin and others.

confidenceNote.zh: 白江口的確切位置（錦江口一帶）仍有爭論；日本史料稱「白村江之戰」。
confidenceNote.en: The exact site (around the mouth of the Geum River) is debated; Japanese sources call it the battle of Hakusukinoe.

summary.zh: 百濟遺臣聯合倭國（日本）出兵復國。唐將劉仁軌率水軍在白江口與倭兵遭遇，四戰皆捷，焚其戰船四百艘，煙焰漲天，海水皆赤，倭與百濟軍大潰。
summary.en: Baekje loyalists, with an army from Wa (Japan), tried to restore their kingdom. The Tang commander Liu Rengui, leading the fleet, met the Wa forces at the mouth of the Baek River, won four engagements and burned four hundred of their ships — "the smoke and flames rose to the sky, the sea ran red" — and the Wa and Baekje forces broke.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷八十四 劉仁軌傳
passages.textZh: 仁軌遇倭兵於白江之口，四戰捷，焚其舟四百艘，煙焰漲天，海水皆赤，賊眾大潰。
passages.textEn: Rengui met the Wa [Japanese] forces at the mouth of the Baek River, won four engagements and burned four hundred of their ships; the smoke and flames rose to the sky, the sea ran red, and the enemy host broke.

summary.zh: 總章元年九月，李勣攻破高句麗，攻下平壤城，俘高句麗王高藏及大臣男建等。高句麗全境投降，共一百七十城、六十九萬七千戶，唐以其地設安東都護府，分置四十二州。
summary.en: In the ninth month of 668 Li Ji defeated Goguryeo, took Pyongyang and captured King Go Jang and the strongman Namgeon. The whole country surrendered — a hundred and seventy cities, six hundred and ninety-seven thousand households — and Tang made it the Andong Protectorate with forty-two prefectures.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷五 高宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 九月癸巳，司空、英國公勣破高麗，拔平壤城，擒其王高藏及其大臣男建等以歸。境內盡降，其城一百七十，戶六十九萬七千，以其地為安東都護府，分置四十二州。
passages.textEn: On guisi of the ninth month Li Ji, Minister of Works and Duke of Ying, defeated Goguryeo, took Pyongyang and brought back its king Go Jang and his minister Namgeon and others as prisoners. The whole country surrendered — a hundred and seventy cities, six hundred and ninety-seven thousand households — and its land was made the Andong Protectorate, divided into forty-two prefectures.

summary.zh: 咸亨元年，唐將薛仁貴、郭待封進至大非川，被吐蕃大將論欽陵襲擊，大敗，薛仁貴等被免職。吐谷渾全境淪沒，只有慕容諾曷缽率親信數千帳內附，被遷到靈州一帶。唐在青海一帶的優勢自此喪失。
summary.en: In 670 the Tang generals Xue Rengui and Guo Daifeng reached the Dafei River, were attacked by the Tibetan general Gar Trinring and badly beaten; Xue and the others were dismissed. All of Tuyuhun was lost; only Murong Nuohebo with a few thousand tents came over and was moved near Lingzhou. Tang never regained the upper hand around Kokonor.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷五 高宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 薛仁貴、郭待封至大非川，為吐蕃大將論欽陵所襲，大敗，仁貴等並坐除名。吐谷渾全國盡沒，唯慕容諾曷缽及其親信數千帳內屬，仍徙於靈州界。
passages.textEn: Xue Rengui and Guo Daifeng reached the Dafei River, were attacked by the Tibetan general Gar Trinring and badly beaten; Rengui and the others were stripped of rank. The whole of Tuyuhun was lost; only Murong Nuohebo with a few thousand tents of his followers came over, and they were moved to the Lingzhou border.

summary.zh: 神龍元年正月，張柬之、崔玄暐、敬暉、桓彥範、袁恕己等率羽林兵誅殺武則天的寵臣張易之、張昌宗，迎太子李顯監國。武則天隨即退位，中宗復位，國號恢復為唐。
summary.en: In the first month of 705 Zhang Jianzhi, Cui Xuanwei, Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, Yuan Shuji and others led the Yulin guards to kill Wu Zetian's favourites Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong and brought in the Crown Prince Li Xian as regent. Wu Zetian soon abdicated, Zhongzong was restored and the dynasty was Tang again.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷七 中宗本紀
passages.textZh: 神龍元年正月，鳳閣侍郎張柬之、鸞臺侍郎崔玄暐、左羽林將軍敬暉、右羽林將軍桓彥範、司刑少卿袁恕己等定策率羽林兵誅易之、昌宗，迎皇太子監國，總司庶政。
passages.textEn: In the first month of the first year of Shenlong, Zhang Jianzhi, Vice-Director of the Phoenix Pavilion, Cui Xuanwei, Jing Hui and Huan Yanfan, generals of the Yulin guards, Yuan Shuji and others planned it together and led the Yulin troops to kill Zhang Yizhi and Zhang Changzong; they brought in the Crown Prince to act as regent and take charge of all government.

summary.zh: 景龍四年六月中宗暴崩，韋后臨朝稱制，韋溫、宗楚客等圖謀不軌。臨淄王李隆基與太平公主合謀，與劉幽求、葛福順、李仙鳧等率萬騎起兵，誅殺韋后一黨，擁立其父睿宗復位。
summary.en: In the sixth month of 710 Zhongzong died suddenly and Empress Wei took over as regent, while Wei Wen, Zong Chuke and others plotted. Li Longji, Prince of Linzi, conspired with Princess Taiping and, with Liu Youqiu, Ge Fushun, Li Xianfu and the Ten Thousand Horsemen, rose and destroyed Empress Wei's faction, restoring his father Ruizong.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷八 玄宗本紀上
passages.textZh: 至六月，中宗暴崩，韋后臨朝稱制。韋溫、宗楚客、紀處訥等謀傾宗社，以睿宗介弟之重，先謀不利。道士馮道力、處士劉承祖皆善於占兆，詣上布誠款。上所居里名隆慶，時人語訛以「隆」為「龍」；韋庶人稱制，改元又為唐隆，皆符御名。上益自負，乃與太平公主謀之，公主喜，以子崇簡從。上乃與崇簡、朝邑尉劉幽求、長上折沖麻嗣宗、押萬騎果毅葛福順李仙鳧、寶昌寺僧普潤等定策誅之。
passages.textEn: In the sixth month Zhongzong died suddenly and Empress Wei took over the court as regent. Wei Wen, Zong Chuke, Ji Chune and others plotted to overthrow the dynasty and, because Ruizong as the emperor's brother carried weight, meant to strike at him first. The Taoist Feng Daoli and the recluse Liu Chengzu, both skilled at omens, came to [Li Longji] to pledge their loyalty. The ward he lived in was called Longqing, which people pronounced as "dragon"; and when the commoner Wei took the regency she changed the era to Tanglong — both matched his name. All the more confident, he planned with Princess Taiping, who was delighted and sent her son Chongjian to join him. With Chongjian, Liu Youqiu, Ma Sizong, Ge Fushun and Li Xianfu of the Ten Thousand Horsemen, the monk Purun and others, he resolved to destroy them.

summary.zh: 先天二年七月，太平公主與竇懷貞、岑羲、蕭至忠、崔湜等密謀以羽林軍作亂。玄宗事先得知，與岐王、薛王、郭元振、王毛仲等先發制人，太平公主一黨覆滅，玄宗獨掌大權，改元開元。
summary.en: In the seventh month of 713 Princess Taiping with Dou Huaizhen, Cen Xi, Xiao Zhizhong, Cui Shi and others plotted to rise with the Yulin guards. Xuanzong learned of it and, with the Princes of Qi and Xue, Guo Yuanzhen and Wang Maozhong, struck first; the princess's faction was destroyed, Xuanzong held power alone, and the era was changed to Kaiyuan.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷八 玄宗本紀上
passages.textZh: 先天二年七月三日，尚書左僕射竇懷貞、侍中岑羲、中書令蕭至忠崔湜、雍州長史李晉、左羽林大將軍常元楷、右羽林將軍李慈等與太平公主同謀，期以其月四日以羽林軍作亂。上密知之，因以中旨告岐王範、薛王業、兵部尚書郭元振、將軍王毛仲，取閑廄馬及家人三百餘人
passages.textEn: On the third day of the seventh month of the second year of Xiantian, Dou Huaizhen, Vice-Director of the Department of State Affairs, Cen Xi, Xiao Zhizhong and Cui Shi, Li Jin, the Yulin generals Chang Yuankai and Li Ci and others conspired with Princess Taiping to rise with the Yulin troops on the fourth. The emperor learned of it secretly and, by palace order, told Li Fan, Prince of Qi, Li Ye, Prince of Xue, the Minister of War Guo Yuanzhen and General Wang Maozhong, and took horses from the stables and some three hundred of his household men…

summary.zh: 至德二載九月，廣平王李俶統率朔方、安西、回紇、南蠻、大食等兵二十萬東進，在香積寺西北大敗叛軍安守忠、李歸仁，斬首六萬，叛將張通儒棄長安東逃，唐軍收復西京；十月又收復東都洛陽。
summary.en: In the ninth month of 757 Li Chu, Prince of Guangping, led two hundred thousand men — from Shuofang and Anxi, Uyghurs, southerners and Arabs — east, routed the rebel generals An Shouzhong and Li Guiren north-west of the Xiangji temple with sixty thousand killed, and the rebel commander Zhang Tongru abandoned Chang'an; the Western Capital was recovered, and the Eastern Capital, Luoyang, the next month.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷十 肅宗本紀
passages.textZh: 丁亥，元帥廣平王統朔方、安西、回紇、南蠻、大食之眾二十萬，東向討賊。壬寅，與賊將安守忠、李歸仁等戰於香積寺西北，賊軍大敗，斬首六萬級，賊帥張通儒棄京城東走。癸卯，廣平王收西京。
passages.textEn: On dinghai the Commander-in-Chief, the Prince of Guangping, led two hundred thousand men — from Shuofang and Anxi, Uyghurs, men of the south and Arabs — east against the rebels. On renyin they fought the rebel generals An Shouzhong and Li Guiren north-west of the Xiangji temple; the rebels were routed with sixty thousand beheaded, and the rebel commander Zhang Tongru abandoned the capital and fled east. On guimao the Prince of Guangping recovered the Western Capital.

names.name: The end of the An–Shi rebellion

confidenceNote.zh: 《舊唐書·代宗紀》把李懷仙獻首繫於寶應元年（762）末；一般記史朝義死於廣德元年（763）正月。
confidenceNote.en: The Old Book of Tang puts Li Huaixian's presentation of the head at the end of 762; Shi Chaoyi's death is usually dated to the first month of 763.

summary.zh: 寶應元年十月，雍王李适統率諸道兵與回紇兵十餘萬討伐史朝義，在洛陽橫水大敗叛軍，俘斬六萬，收復東京及河陽、汴、鄭、滑、相、魏等州，史朝義北逃。河北州郡相繼歸順，叛將李懷仙斬史朝義首級來降，歷時八年的安史之亂結束；降將田承嗣、李寶臣、李懷仙等仍領河北諸鎮。
summary.en: In the tenth month of 762 Li Kuo, Prince of Yong, led over a hundred thousand men of the provinces and the Uyghurs against Shi Chaoyi, routed him at the Heng River by Luoyang with sixty thousand killed or taken, and recovered the Eastern Capital, Heyang, Bian, Zheng, Hua, Xiang, Wei and other prefectures; Shi Chaoyi fled north. The provinces north of the Yellow River came over one by one, and the rebel general Li Huaixian cut off Shi Chaoyi's head and surrendered. The eight-year rebellion was over — but the surrendered generals Tian Chengsi, Li Baochen and Li Huaixian kept the Hebei provinces.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷十一 代宗本紀
passages.textZh: 甲戌，戰於橫水，賊大敗，俘斬六萬計。史朝義奔冀州。乙亥，雍王奏收東京、河陽、汴、鄭、滑、相、魏等州。
passages.textEn: On jiaxu they fought at the Heng River and the rebels were crushed, some sixty thousand killed or captured. Shi Chaoyi fled to Jizhou. On yihai the Prince of Yong reported the recovery of the Eastern Capital and of Heyang, Bian, Zheng, Hua, Xiang, Wei and other prefectures.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷十一 代宗本紀
passages.textZh: 於是河北州郡悉平。賊范陽尹李懷仙斬史朝義首來獻，請降。
passages.textEn: So all the prefectures and commanderies north of the Yellow River were pacified. Li Huaixian, the rebels' Intendant of Fanyang, cut off Shi Chaoyi's head, presented it and asked to surrender.

summary.zh: 建中四年十月，涇原軍奉命東援襄城，途經長安時在滻水嘩變，姚令言無法約束。德宗急召神策軍護駕，竟無一人應召，只得與太子、諸王及妃主百餘人出苑北門出逃，經咸陽奔奉天。叛軍擁立朱泚稱帝，次年唐軍才收復長安。
summary.en: In the tenth month of 783 the Jingyuan army, ordered east to relieve Xiangcheng, mutinied at the Chan River as it passed Chang'an, and Yao Lingyan could not hold it. Dezong called on the Shence army and not one man came; with the Crown Prince and over a hundred princes, consorts and princesses he fled by the park's north gate, by Xianyang to Fengtian. The mutineers made Zhu Ci emperor, and Chang'an was only retaken the next year.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷十二 德宗本紀上
passages.textZh: 冬十月丙午，詔涇原節度使姚令言率涇原之師救哥舒曜。丁未，涇原軍出京城，至滻水，倒戈謀叛，姚令言不能禁。上令載繒彩二車，遣晉王往慰諭之，亂兵已陳於丹鳳闕下，促神策軍拒之。無一人至者。與太子諸王妃主百餘人出苑北門，右龍武軍使令狐建方教射於軍中，聞難，聚射士得四百人扈從。
passages.textEn: On bingwu of the tenth month in winter, Yao Lingyan, Military Governor of Jingyuan, was ordered to take the Jingyuan army to relieve Geshu Yao. On dingwei the Jingyuan army left the capital; at the Chan River it turned its weapons round and mutinied, and Yao Lingyan could not stop it. The emperor had two cartloads of silk sent and the Prince of Jin went to calm them, but the mutineers were already drawn up below the Danfeng gate; he called on the Shence army to resist them, and not one man came. With the Crown Prince and over a hundred princes, consorts and princesses he left by the north gate of the park; Linghu Jian, commissioner of the Right Dragon-Martial army, was drilling archers, and hearing of the trouble gathered four hundred of them to escort him.

names.name: Li Su takes Caizhou in the snow

confidenceNote.zh: 「淮西割據三十餘年」與「元和中興」兩點不在所引文字中。
confidenceNote.en: That Huaixi had been independent for over thirty years, and the "Yuanhe restoration", are not in the quoted text.

summary.zh: 元和十二年冬，唐鄧節度使李愬在風雪之夜率軍急行，至張柴才宣布「入蔡州取吳元濟也」。半夜雪下得更大，他令人驚擾城邊的鵝鴨池以掩蓋行軍聲；李祐、李忠義鑿牆先登，殺盡守門士卒。黎明雪止，李愬入城，吳元濟還以為是自家士兵回城取寒衣。淮西割據三十餘年至此平定，藩鎮紛紛歸順，史稱「元和中興」。
summary.en: In the winter of 817 Li Su, Military Governor of Tang and Deng, marched his army through a night of wind and snow, telling his officers only at Zhangchai: "We are going into Caizhou to take Wu Yuanji." At midnight the snow grew heavier; he had the geese and ducks in a pond by the walls startled to cover the noise, and Li You and Li Zhongyi climbed the wall and killed the gate guards. At dawn the snow stopped and Li Su entered; Wu Yuanji at first thought it was his own men home for winter clothes. Huaixi, independent for more than thirty years, was subdued; other provinces submitted, the "Yuanhe restoration".

label.zh: 自文城柵經張柴夜襲蔡州
label.en: Night march by Zhangchai to Caizhou

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百三十三 李晟傳 附李愬
passages.textZh: 是日，陰晦雨雪，大風裂旗旆，馬栗而不能躍，士卒苦寒，抱戈僵仆者道路相望。其川澤梁逕險夷，張柴已東，師人未嘗蹈其境，皆謂投身不測。初至張柴，諸將請所止，愬曰：「入蔡州取吳元濟也。」諸將失色。
passages.textEn: That day it was dark with sleet and snow; a great wind tore the banners, the horses shivered and could not leap, and soldiers clutching their spears fell frozen along the road. East of Zhangchai no one in the army had ever set foot, and none knew the rivers, marshes, bridges and roads; all thought they were marching to their deaths. When they first reached Zhangchai the officers asked where they would halt. Su said: "We are going into Caizhou to take Wu Yuanji." The officers went pale.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百三十三 李晟傳 附李愬
passages.textZh: 夜半，雪愈甚。近城有鵝鴨池，愬令驚擊之，以雜其聲。賊恃吳房、朗山之固，晏然無一人知者。李祐、李忠義坎墉而先登，敢銳者從之，盡殺守門卒而登其門，留擊柝者。黎明，雪亦止，愬入，止元濟外宅。蔡吏告元濟曰：「城已陷矣。」元濟曰：「是洄曲子弟歸求寒衣耳。」
passages.textEn: At midnight the snow grew heavier. Near the city was a pond of geese and ducks, and Su had them startled to cover the noise. The rebels, trusting in the strength of Wufang and Langshan, slept on and not one knew. Li You and Li Zhongyi cut footholds in the wall and climbed first, the bravest after them; they killed all the gate guards and took the gate, leaving the watchman to keep beating his rattle. At dawn the snow stopped and Su went in, halting at Yuanji's outer residence. A Cai official told Yuanji: "The city has fallen." Yuanji said: "It's the Huiqu boys come home for winter clothes."

names.name: Han Yu protests the Buddha's bone

summary.zh: 元和十四年正月，憲宗派人到鳳翔法門寺迎佛指骨入宮供奉三日，再送各寺，王公百姓爭相施捨，甚至有人傾家蕩產、燒頂灼臂。刑部侍郎韓愈上〈論佛骨表〉諫阻，憲宗大怒欲處死，經眾人求情，貶為潮州刺史。
summary.en: In the first month of 819 Xianzong had the Buddha's finger bone from the Famen monastery brought into the palace for three days and then round the monasteries; princes and commoners competed in giving, some ruining themselves or burning their scalps and arms. Han Yu, Vice-Minister of Justice, sent up his "Memorial on the Buddha's Bone" in protest; the furious emperor wanted him executed, but after many pleaded for him he was demoted to Prefect of Chaozhou.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百六十 韓愈傳
passages.textZh: 十四年正月，上令中使杜英奇押宮人三十人，持香花赴臨臯驛迎佛骨。自光順門入大內，留禁中三日，乃送諸寺。王公士庶，奔走舍施，唯恐在後。百姓有廢業破產、燒頂灼臂而求供養者。愈素不喜佛，上疏諫曰：
passages.textEn: In the first month of the fourteenth year the emperor sent the palace commissioner Du Yingqi with thirty palace women carrying incense and flowers to the Linhao post station to welcome the Buddha's bone. It came in through the Guangshun gate into the palace, stayed three days and was then sent round the monasteries. Princes, officials and commoners rushed to give alms, each afraid to be last; some common people abandoned their livelihoods and ruined themselves, or burned their scalps and arms as offerings. Yu, who had never liked Buddhism, sent up a memorial of protest:

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百六十 韓愈傳
passages.textZh: 於是人情驚惋，乃至國戚諸貴，亦以罪愈太重，因事言之，乃貶為潮州刺史。
passages.textEn: People were shocked and dismayed, and even the emperor's in-laws and other nobles thought Yu's punishment too heavy and found ways to say so; so he was demoted to Prefect of Chaozhou.

summary.zh: 大和九年十一月，文宗與宰相李訓、鄭注謀誅宦官，詐稱金吾仗院的石榴樹上降了甘露，引宦官前往觀看伏兵誅殺。宦官發現帷幕後的伏兵，急忙擁文宗回宮。神策軍中尉仇士良率兵反撲，宰相王涯、賈餗、舒元輿、李訓等十餘家被滅族，京師大駭。此後宦官控制朝政更甚。
summary.en: In the eleventh month of 835 Emperor Wenzong and his ministers Li Xun and Zheng Zhu plotted to kill the eunuchs, announcing that sweet dew had fallen on a pomegranate tree at the Golden Guard's quarters to lure them into an ambush. The eunuchs saw the soldiers hidden behind the curtains and hurried the emperor back into the palace; the army supervisor Qiu Shiliang struck back, and the chief ministers Wang Ya, Jia Su, Shu Yuanyu, Li Xun and others — more than ten families — were exterminated. The capital was in terror, and the eunuchs' grip on the court grew tighter.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷十七下 文宗本紀下
passages.textZh: 壬戌，中尉仇士良率兵誅宰相王涯、賈餗、舒元輿、李訓，新除太原節度王璠，郭行餘、鄭注、羅立言、李孝本，韓約等十餘家，皆族誅。時李訓、鄭注謀誅內官，詐言金吾仗舍石榴樹有甘露，請上觀之。內官先至金吾仗，見幕下伏甲，遽扶帝輦入內，故訓等敗，流血塗地。京師大駭，旬日稍安。
passages.textEn: On renxu the army supervisor Qiu Shiliang led troops to kill the chief ministers Wang Ya, Jia Su, Shu Yuanyu and Li Xun, Wang Fan, newly appointed Military Governor of Taiyuan, and Guo Xingyu, Zheng Zhu, Luo Liyan, Li Xiaoben, Han Yue and others — more than ten families, all exterminated with their clans. Li Xun and Zheng Zhu had plotted to kill the eunuchs, falsely announcing that sweet dew had fallen on a pomegranate tree at the Golden Guard's quarters and asking the emperor to come and see. The eunuchs went ahead to the Golden Guard's quarters, saw armed men hidden behind the curtains, and hurried the emperor's litter back into the palace. So Li Xun and the others failed, and blood covered the ground. The capital was in terror and only grew calm after ten days.

confidenceNote.zh: 引文只有檢括數字；拆毀寺院、勒令還俗的詔令出自同年八月，原文尚未錄入。
confidenceNote.en: The quotation gives only the count; the edict ordering the demolitions, issued in the eighth month, has not been entered yet.

summary.zh: 會昌五年，唐武宗下令檢括天下寺院與僧尼，共有寺院四千六百所、蘭若四萬、僧尼二十六萬五百人。隨即大規模拆毀寺院、勒令僧尼還俗、沒收寺產，佛教在中國受到沉重打擊。次年武宗死，宣宗即位後停止。
summary.en: In 845 Emperor Wuzong ordered a count of the realm's monasteries, monks and nuns: four thousand six hundred monasteries, forty thousand shrines and two hundred and sixty thousand five hundred monks and nuns. Mass demolition followed — monasteries pulled down, monks and nuns returned to lay life, their property confiscated — a heavy blow to Buddhism in China. Wuzong died the next year and Xuanzong stopped it.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷十八上 武宗本紀
passages.textZh: 敕祠部檢括天下寺及僧尼人數。大凡寺四千六百，蘭若四萬，僧尼二十六萬五百。
passages.textEn: The Bureau of Sacrifices was ordered to count the monasteries, monks and nuns of the realm. In all there were four thousand six hundred monasteries, forty thousand shrines and two hundred and sixty thousand five hundred monks and nuns.

names.name: Zhang Yichao returns Hexi to Tang

confidenceNote.zh: 《舊唐書》作「張義潮」，敦煌文書作「張議潮」。848年起兵一事不在所引文字中。
confidenceNote.en: The Old Book of Tang writes his name 義潮; the Dunhuang manuscripts 議潮. The rising of 848 is not in the quoted text.

summary.zh: 大中二年沙州人張議潮起兵逐走吐蕃守將。大中五年他派兄長張義澤送上瓜、沙、伊、肅等十一州的戶籍，河西、隴右陷於吐蕃百餘年後重歸唐朝；唐以張議潮為瓜沙伊等州節度使，後號歸義軍。
summary.en: In 848 Zhang Yichao of Shazhou rose and drove out the Tibetan garrison. In 851 he sent his brother Yize with the population registers of eleven prefectures — Gua, Sha, Yi, Su and others — and after more than a century under Tubo, Hexi and Longyou were back with Tang. He was made Military Governor of Gua, Sha, Yi and other prefectures, later known as the Guiyi Army.

label.zh: 遣使入朝獻十一州圖籍
label.en: Envoys bring the registers to Chang'an

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷十八下 宣宗本紀
passages.textZh: 沙州刺史張義潮遣兄義澤以瓜、沙、伊、肅等十一州戶口來獻，自河、隴陷蕃百餘年，至是悉復隴右故地。以義潮為瓜沙伊等州節度使。
passages.textEn: Zhang Yichao, Prefect of Shazhou, sent his brother Yize to present the population registers of eleven prefectures — Gua, Sha, Yi, Su and others. Since Hexi and Longyou fell to Tubo more than a hundred years before, now at last all the old lands of Longyou were recovered. Yichao was made Military Governor of Gua, Sha, Yi and other prefectures.

summary.zh: 咸通九年，徐州派往桂林戍邊的士卒五百人殺死將領，推糧料判官龐勛為首，擅自北還，九月攻陷宿州、徐州，殺節度使崔彥曾，開官庫募兵，十日內聚眾五萬。次年被唐軍與沙陀兵平定。
summary.en: In 868 five hundred Xuzhou soldiers on garrison duty at Guilin killed their commander, made the grain clerk Pang Xun their leader and marched home on their own; in the ninth month they took Suzhou and Xuzhou, killed the Military Governor Cui Yanzeng and opened the government stores to hire men — fifty thousand in ten days. Tang and Shatuo troops put them down the next year.

label.en: The Guilin garrison marches home to Xuzhou

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷十九上 懿宗本紀
passages.textZh: 其月，徐州赴桂林戍卒五百人，官健許佶、趙可立殺其將王仲甫，以糧料判官龐勳為都頭，剽掠湘潭、衡山兩縣，有眾千人，擅還本鎮。
passages.textEn: That month five hundred soldiers from Xuzhou on garrison duty at Guilin — Xu Ji, Zhao Keli and others — killed their commander Wang Zhongfu, made the grain clerk Pang Xun their leader, plundered the counties of Xiangtan and Hengshan and, a thousand strong, marched home on their own authority.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷十九上 懿宗本紀
passages.textZh: 乙未，龐勳陷徐州，殺節度使崔彥曾、判官焦潞、李稅溫延皓、崔蘊、韋廷乂，惟免監軍張道謹。遂出徐、宿官庫錢帛，召募凶徒，不旬日其徒五萬。
passages.textEn: On yiwei Pang Xun took Xuzhou and killed the Military Governor Cui Yanzeng and his staff, sparing only the army supervisor Zhang Daojin. He opened the government stores of Xu and Su to hire desperate men, and in less than ten days had fifty thousand.

names.name: Wang Xianzhi and Huang Chao rise

summary.zh: 乾符二年五月，濮州王仙芝聚眾於長垣，攻陷濮州，鄆州節度使出兵鎮壓失敗。冤句人黃巢起兵響應，兩軍轉戰中原與江淮，揭開唐末大起事的序幕。
summary.en: In the fifth month of 875 Wang Xianzhi of Puzhou gathered men at Changyuan and took Puzhou; the Military Governor of Yunzhou failed to put him down. Huang Chao of Yuanju rose to join him, and their armies ranged across the central plain and the Huai region — the opening of the great risings that ended Tang.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷十九下 僖宗本紀
passages.textZh: 五月，濮州賊首王仙芝聚於長垣縣，其眾三千，剽掠閭井，進陷濮州，俘丁壯萬人。鄆州節度使李種出兵擊之，為賊所敗。
passages.textEn: In the fifth month the Puzhou bandit chief Wang Xianzhi gathered at Changyuan county with three thousand men, plundered the villages, went on to take Puzhou and captured ten thousand able-bodied men. Li Zhong, Military Governor of Yunzhou, sent troops against him and was beaten.

confidenceNote.zh: 「外甥」一點出自《新唐書》，不在所引文字中。
confidenceNote.en: That Lin Yan was his nephew comes from the New Book of Tang, not the quoted text.

summary.zh: 中和四年，黃巢被逐出長安後東走，在瑕丘被徐州將李師悅擊潰，部眾幾乎死盡。七月黃巢逃到泰山狼虎谷的襄王村，外甥林言斬下黃巢、黃揆、黃秉的首級投降。
summary.en: In 884, having been driven from Chang'an, Huang Chao fled east and was crushed at Xiaqiu by the Xuzhou general Li Shiyue, his men almost all killed. In the seventh month he reached the village of Xiangwang in the Langhu valley of Mount Tai, where his nephew Lin Yan cut off the heads of Huang Chao, Huang Kui and Huang Bing and surrendered.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷十九下 僖宗本紀
passages.textZh: 秋七月己未朔。癸酉，賊將林言斬黃巢、黃揆、黃秉三人首級降時溥。初，徐將李師悅與賊戰於瑕丘，賊殊死戰，其眾殆盡。林言與巢走至太山狼虎谷之襄王村，懼追至並命，乃斬賊降師悅。
passages.textEn: Autumn, the seventh month, first day jiwei. On guiyou the rebel general Lin Yan cut off the heads of Huang Chao, Huang Kui and Huang Bing and surrendered them to Shi Pu. The Xuzhou general Li Shiyue had fought the rebels at Xiaqiu, where they fought to the death and were almost all killed. Lin Yan and Chao fled to the village of Xiangwang in the Langhu valley of Mount Tai; fearing they would be caught and both die, Lin Yan cut off the rebel leader's head and surrendered to Li Shiyue.

question.zh: 黃巢是被林言所殺，還是自殺？
question.en: Was Huang Chao killed by Lin Yan, or did he take his own life?

claim.zh: 《舊唐書》記林言斬黃巢等首級投降。
claim.en: The Old Book of Tang says Lin Yan cut off his head and surrendered.

source.en: Old Book of Tang, Annals of Xizong

accounts.quoteZh: 賊將林言斬黃巢、黃揆、黃秉三人首級降時溥

claim.zh: 《新唐書》記黃巢自刎不死，由林言取其首；也有記載說他出家為僧得免，屬後世傳說。
claim.en: The New Book of Tang has Huang Chao try to cut his own throat and Lin Yan finish it; later stories that he escaped to become a monk are legend.

source.en: New Book of Tang; later notebooks

summary.zh: 唐太宗時的諫臣，以直言敢諫著稱，前後進諫二百餘事。魏徵死後，太宗對侍臣說：「以銅為鏡，可以正衣冠；以古為鏡，可以知興替；以人為鏡，可以明得失……今魏徵殂逝，遂亡一鏡矣！」
summary.en: Taizong's outspoken counsellor, famous for daring to tell the emperor he was wrong — more than two hundred times by tradition. After his death Taizong told his ministers: "With bronze as a mirror one can straighten one's cap; with the past as a mirror one can understand rise and fall; with a man as a mirror one can see one's gains and failings… Now Wei Zheng is dead, and I have lost a mirror!"

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷七十一 魏徵傳
passages.textZh: 嘗臨朝謂侍臣曰：「夫以銅爲鏡，可以正衣冠；以古爲鏡，可以知興替；以人爲鏡，可以明得失。朕常保此三鏡，以防己過。今魏徵殂逝，遂亡一鏡矣！
passages.textEn: He once said to his ministers at court: "With bronze as a mirror one can straighten one's cap and clothes; with the past as a mirror one can understand rise and fall; with a man as a mirror one can see one's own gains and failings. I have always kept these three mirrors to guard against my faults. Now Wei Zheng is dead, and I have lost a mirror!"

summary.zh: 唐初名將，本名藥師。630年率精騎乘夜進至陰山，突襲東突厥頡利可汗牙帳，斬萬餘級、俘男女十餘萬，頡利逃走後被擒，東突厥滅亡。後又平吐谷渾。
summary.en: The leading general of early Tang, born Li Yaoshi. In 630 he led picked horsemen by night to the Yin Mountains and fell on Illig Qaghan's camp, killing over ten thousand and taking over a hundred thousand captive; Illig fled and was caught, and the Eastern Turkic khaganate ended. He later subdued the Tuyuhun.

label.en: Routs Illig at the Yin Mountains

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷六十七 李靖傳
passages.textZh: 督軍疾進，師至陰山，遇其斥候千餘帳，皆俘以隨軍。頡利見使者，大悅，不虞官兵至也。靖軍將逼其牙帳十五里，虜始覺。頡利畏威先走，部眾因而潰散。靖斬萬餘級，俘男女十餘萬，殺其妻隋義成公主。
passages.textEn: He drove the army on fast. Reaching the Yin Mountains they met more than a thousand tents of the enemy's scouts and took them all along as prisoners. Illig, receiving the [Tang] envoys, was delighted and never expected government troops. Only when Jing's army was within fifteen li of his camp did the enemy notice. Illig, in fear, fled first, and his people scattered. Jing beheaded more than ten thousand, took over a hundred thousand men and women captive, and killed Illig's wife, the Sui Princess Yicheng.

summary.zh: 華州鄭縣人。安史之亂中任朔方節度使，與李光弼收復河北，757年隨廣平王收復兩京，763年吐蕃攻入長安後又收復京城。史稱「天下以其身為安危者殆二十年」，「權傾天下而朝不忌，功蓋一代而主不疑」。
summary.en: From Zheng county in Huazhou. In the An–Shi rebellion he was Military Governor of Shuofang, fought with Li Guangbi in Hebei, recovered the two capitals with the Prince of Guangping in 757, and retook Chang'an after the Tibetan raid of 763. The history says "for nearly twenty years the safety of the realm rested on him", and "his power overshadowed the realm, yet the court did not fear him; his merit was the greatest of his age, yet his sovereign did not suspect him".

label.en: Military Governor of Shuofang, Director of the Secretariat

label.zh: 任朔方節度使，起兵討安祿山
label.en: Military Governor of Shuofang; marches against An Lushan
Fights in Hebei with Li Guangbi
Falls back to Shangzhou, then retakes Chang'an

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十 郭子儀傳
passages.textZh: 郭子儀，華州鄭縣人。
passages.textEn: Guo Ziyi was from Zheng county in Huazhou.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百二十 郭子儀傳
passages.textZh: 天下以其身為安危者殆二十年。校中書令考二十有四。權傾天下而朝不忌，功蓋一代而主不疑，侈窮人欲而君子不之罪。
passages.textEn: For nearly twenty years the safety of the realm rested on him. He served twenty-four years as Director of the Secretariat. His power overshadowed the realm, yet the court did not fear him; his merit was the greatest of his age, yet his sovereign did not suspect him; he lived in every luxury, yet gentlemen did not blame him.

summary.zh: 名玉環，早孤，由叔父撫養。初為玄宗之子壽王妃，武惠妃死後被召入宮，先為女道士，號太真，天寶四載冊為貴妃，極受寵愛，族兄楊國忠因而拜相。756年安史之亂中隨玄宗西逃，在馬嵬驛被賜死。
summary.en: Yang Yuhuan, orphaned young and raised by her uncle. First married to Xuanzong's son the Prince of Shou, she was summoned to the palace after Consort Wu Hui's death, first as a Taoist nun called Taizhen, and made Precious Consort in 745; she was the emperor's great favourite, and her cousin Yang Guozhong became chief minister. Fleeing west with Xuanzong in 756, she was made to die at the Mawei station.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷五十一 后妃傳上 楊貴妃
passages.textZh: 玄宗楊貴妃，高祖令本，金州刺史。父玄琰，蜀州司戶。妃早孤，養於叔父河南府士曹玄璬。開元初，武惠妃特承寵遇，故王皇后廢黜。二十四年惠妃薨，帝悼惜久之，後庭數千，無可意者。或奏玄琰女姿色冠代，宜蒙召見。
passages.textEn: Consort Yang of Xuanzong: her great-great-grandfather Lingben was Prefect of Jinzhou; her father Xuanyan was a revenue officer of Shuzhou. Orphaned young, she was raised by her uncle Xuanjiao, an officer in Henan. Early in Kaiyuan Consort Wu Hui enjoyed special favour, and so Empress Wang was deposed. When Consort Wu Hui died in the twenty-fourth year, the emperor mourned her a long time; among the thousands of the rear palace none pleased him. Someone told him that the daughter of Xuanyan was the beauty of the age and should be summoned.

fiction.zh: 〈長恨歌〉以後的「仙山相會」與流亡日本等說法屬文學與傳說；正史只記她死於馬嵬驛。
fiction.en: The meeting on the immortals' mountain of the "Song of Everlasting Regret", and stories that she escaped to Japan, are poetry and legend; the histories say only that she died at Mawei.

confidenceNote.zh: 卒地《舊唐書》作宣城，通行說法據李陽冰〈草堂集序〉作當塗；行跡年份為約數。
confidenceNote.en: The Old Book of Tang says he died at Xuancheng; the usual view, after Li Yangbing's preface to his works, is Dangtu. The years of his travels are approximate.

summary.zh: 字太白，號青蓮居士。少有逸才，志氣宏放。天寶初入長安，賀知章見而稱為「天上謫仙人」，玄宗召為翰林供奉，不久離京漫遊。安史之亂中入永王李璘幕府，永王兵敗後被判長流夜郎，中途遇赦東還，762年卒。
summary.en: Courtesy name Taibai, sobriquet the Retired Scholar of Green Lotus. A youth of extraordinary talent and bold spirit, he came to Chang'an early in Tianbao, where He Zhizhang called him "an immortal banished from Heaven" and Xuanzong made him an attendant of the Hanlin; he soon left to wander again. In the An–Shi rebellion he joined the staff of Li Lin, Prince of Yong; after the prince's defeat he was sentenced to exile at Yelang, pardoned on the way, and died in 762.

label.zh: 離長安，在洛陽與杜甫相識
label.en: Leaves Chang'an; meets Du Fu at Luoyang
At Xuanzhou; joins the Prince of Yong

label.zh: 因永王事繫潯陽獄，判長流夜郎
label.en: Jailed at Xunyang; sentenced to exile at Yelang

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十下 文苑傳下 李白
passages.textZh: 李白字太白，山東人。少有逸才，志氣宏放，飄然有超世之心，父爲任城尉，因家焉。
passages.textEn: Li Bai, courtesy name Taibai, was a man of Shandong. As a youth he had extraordinary talent, a bold and expansive spirit and an air of being above the world. His father was a sheriff of Rencheng, and so the family settled there.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十下 文苑傳下 李白
passages.textZh: 初賀知章見白，賞之曰：「此天上謫仙人也。」祿山之亂，玄宗幸蜀，在途以永王璘為江淮兵馬都督、揚州節度大使。白在宣州謁見，遂辟爲從事。永王謀亂，兵敗，白坐長流夜郎。後遇赦得還，竟以飲酒過度，醉死於宣城。
passages.textEn: When He Zhizhang first met Bai he praised him: "This is an immortal banished from Heaven." In An Lushan's rebellion, as Xuanzong fled to Shu he made Li Lin, Prince of Yong, commander of the Jiang–Huai forces. Bai called on him at Xuanzhou and was taken onto his staff. When the Prince of Yong rebelled and was defeated, Bai was sentenced to exile at distant Yelang. Later he was pardoned and came back, and in the end died of drink at Xuancheng.

question.en: Where was Li Bai from?

claim.zh: 《舊唐書》說他是山東人，父親做過任城尉，因而安家。
claim.en: The Old Book of Tang calls him a man of Shandong, whose father had been sheriff of Rencheng and settled there.

source.en: Old Book of Tang, Biographies of literary men

accounts.quoteZh: 李白字太白，山東人。

claim.zh: 《新唐書》與李陽冰〈草堂集序〉說他祖上隋末因罪流徙西域，神龍初才遷回，客居巴西（今四川），今人多認為他生於西域碎葉一帶、長於蜀中。
claim.en: The New Book of Tang and Li Yangbing's preface say his ancestors were banished to the Western Regions at the end of Sui and came back early in Shenlong to settle in Baxi (Sichuan); many now think he was born around Suyab and grew up in Shu.

source.zh: 《新唐書·文藝傳中》；李陽冰〈草堂集序〉
source.en: New Book of Tang; Li Yangbing's preface

fiction.zh: 李白醉後入水捉月而死的故事見於五代以後的筆記，屬傳說。
fiction.en: The story that he drowned drunk trying to embrace the moon in the river appears in notebooks from the Five Dynasties on; it is legend.

summary.zh: 字子美，本襄陽人，後徙河南鞏縣。天寶年間應試不第，長期困居長安；安史之亂中陷於叛軍，後逃奔肅宗。759年入蜀，在成都浣花溪畔築草堂。765年後順江東下，漂泊荊湘，卒於湘江舟中。後世尊為「詩聖」，其詩被稱為「詩史」。
summary.en: Courtesy name Zimei, originally of Xiangyang, his family later of Gong county in Henan. He failed the examination in Tianbao and lived long in poverty at Chang'an; caught by the rebels in the An–Shi war, he escaped to Suzong. In 759 he went to Shu and built his thatched cottage by the Huanhua stream at Chengdu. After 765 he drifted down the Yangtze through Jing and Xiang and died on a boat on the Xiang. Later ages called him the Sage of Poetry and his poems a "history in verse".

label.en: Caught by the rebels in Chang'an
Escapes to Fengxiang; Reminder of the Left

label.zh: 入蜀，於成都浣花溪築草堂

label.en: Dies on a boat on the Xiang

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十下 文苑傳下 杜甫
passages.textZh: 杜甫，字子美，本襄陽人，後徙河南鞏縣。
passages.textEn: Du Fu, courtesy name Zimei, was originally of Xiangyang; the family later moved to Gong county in Henan.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十下 文苑傳下 杜甫
passages.textZh: 甫於成都浣花里種竹植樹，結廬枕江，縱酒嘯詠，與田夫野老相狎，蕩無拘檢，嚴武過之，有時不冠，其傲誕如此。
passages.textEn: At Huanhua in Chengdu Fu planted bamboo and trees and built a cottage by the river, where he drank and sang freely, kept company with old farmers and lived without restraint; when Yan Wu called he sometimes did not even put on his cap — so proud and eccentric was he.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百九十下 文苑傳下 杜甫
passages.textZh: 甫以其家避亂荊、楚，扁舟下峽，未維舟而江陵亂，乃泝沿湘流，遊衡山，寓居耒陽。甫嘗遊嶽廟，為暴水所阻，旬日不得食。耒陽聶令知之，自棹舟迎甫而還。永泰二年，啗牛肉白酒，一夕而卒於耒陽，時年五十九。
passages.textEn: Fu took his family to escape the disorders to Jing and Chu, going down the gorges in a small boat; before he could moor, Jiangling was in turmoil, so he went up the Xiang, visited Mount Heng and lodged at Leiyang. Once, visiting the temple of the sacred mountain, he was cut off by a flood and went ten days without food. Magistrate Nie of Leiyang heard of it and rowed out himself to bring him back. In the second year of Yongtai he ate beef and drank white wine, and died in one night at Leiyang, aged fifty-nine.

question.en: When and how did Du Fu die?

claim.zh: 《舊唐書》說他永泰二年（766）在耒陽吃了牛肉白酒，一夜而卒，年五十九。
claim.en: The Old Book of Tang says he died in one night at Leiyang in 766 after eating beef and drinking white wine, aged fifty-nine.

source.en: Old Book of Tang, Biographies of literary men

accounts.quoteZh: 永泰二年，啗牛肉白酒，一夕而卒於耒陽

claim.zh: 今人據其詩作考訂，他在大曆五年（770）冬病逝於潭州往岳州的湘江舟中；「牛肉白酒」之說多被視為傳聞。
claim.en: Modern scholars, working from his own poems, date his death to the winter of 770 on a boat on the Xiang between Tanzhou and Yuezhou; the beef-and-wine story is generally treated as hearsay.

source.en: Modern scholarship (dating from his poems)

summary.zh: 字退之，昌黎人，古文運動的領袖，主張文以載道，排斥佛老。819年上〈論佛骨表〉諫阻憲宗迎佛骨，被貶為潮州刺史；後召回長安，官至吏部侍郎。
summary.en: Courtesy name Tuizhi, of Changli; leader of the "ancient prose" movement, who held that writing should carry the Way and opposed Buddhism and Taoism. In 819 his "Memorial on the Buddha's Bone" against Xianzong's veneration of the relic got him demoted to Prefect of Chaozhou; recalled to Chang'an, he rose to Vice-Minister of Personnel.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百六十 韓愈傳
passages.textZh: 韓愈，字退之，昌黎人。
passages.textEn: Han Yu, courtesy name Tuizhi, was of Changli.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百六十 韓愈傳
passages.textZh: 十四年正月，上令中使杜英奇押宮人三十人，持香花赴臨臯驛迎佛骨。自光順門入大內，留禁中三日，乃送諸寺。王公士庶，奔走舍施，唯恐在後。百姓有廢業破產、燒頂灼臂而求供養者。愈素不喜佛，上疏諫曰：
passages.textEn: In the first month of the fourteenth year the emperor sent the palace commissioner Du Yingqi with thirty palace women carrying incense and flowers to the Linhao post station to welcome the Buddha's bone. It came in through the Guangshun gate into the palace, stayed three days and was then sent round the monasteries. Princes, officials and commoners rushed to give alms, each afraid to be last; some common people abandoned their livelihoods and ruined themselves, or burned their scalps and arms as offerings. Yu, who had never liked Buddhism, sent up a memorial of protest:

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百六十 韓愈傳
passages.textZh: 於是人情驚惋，乃至國戚諸貴，亦以罪愈太重，因事言之，乃貶為潮州刺史。
passages.textEn: People were shocked and dismayed, and even the emperor's in-laws and other nobles thought Yu's punishment too heavy and found ways to say so; so he was demoted to Prefect of Chaozhou.

summary.zh: 字樂天，太原人。與元稹齊名，詩作平易通俗，「自衣冠士子，至閭閻下俚，悉傳諷之」，號「元和體」。815年貶江州司馬，後任杭州、蘇州刺史；晚年居洛陽，與香山僧如滿結社，自稱香山居士。
summary.en: Courtesy name Letian, of Taiyuan. Named with Yuan Zhen as the poets of the age, he wrote plain, accessible verse that "everyone from scholars in office to common people in the lanes recited" — the "Yuanhe style". Demoted to Assistant Prefect of Jiangzhou in 815, he later governed Hangzhou and Suzhou; in old age he lived at Luoyang, formed a Buddhist society with the monk Ruman of Xiangshan and called himself the Retired Scholar of Xiangshan.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百六十六 白居易傳
passages.textZh: 白居易，字樂天，太原人。
passages.textEn: Bai Juyi, courtesy name Letian, was a man of Taiyuan.

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百六十六 元稹傳
passages.textZh: 稹聰警絕人，年少有才名，與太原白居易友善。工為詩，善狀詠風態物色，當時言詩者，稱元、白焉。自衣冠士子，至閭閻下俚，悉傳諷之，號為「元和體」。
passages.textEn: [Yuan] Zhen was brilliant and quick, famous for his talent when young, and a close friend of Bai Juyi of Taiyuan. He wrote fine poetry, good at catching moods and scenes; people who talked of poetry then spoke of "Yuan and Bai". From scholars in office to common people in the lanes, everyone recited their poems, which were called the "Yuanhe style".

passages.sourceEn: Old Book of Tang (Liu Xu et al., 945)
passages.locator: 卷一百六十六 白居易傳
passages.textZh: 會昌中，請罷太子少傅，以刑部尚書致仕。與香山僧如滿結香火社，每肩輿往來，白衣鳩杖，自稱香山居士。
passages.textEn: In the Huichang era he asked to give up his post as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and retired with the rank of Minister of Justice. He formed a Buddhist society with the monk Ruman of Xiangshan, came and went in a sedan chair, in white robes with a dove-headed staff, and called himself the Retired Scholar of Xiangshan.
